ground_truth_answer:
Pretty much what JR V says.  Note that this is covered in A12.12.  After the side setting up first is done (and done out of sight of the opponent), they place their scenario-designed ?? but only in concealment terrain.  He can place these on existing units or make dummy stacks, as he sees fit.  E.g. if you have 12 scenario-designated ??, you could conceal 12 of your stacks or make 6 2-high dummy stacks or some combination of the two (almost always better to do a combination, as adding 6 2-high dummy stacks will quickly let your opponent know that you have exactly 6 2-high dummy stacks 🙂 ).

If your opponent does not also set up on the board, then you can /also/ place free ?? markers on any stacks that don't already have ?? (key being you never get to place a free ?? on top of a scenario-designated ??).

If your opponent sets up on board, he does so after your scenario-designated ??, then BOTH of you get to conceal units out of enemy LOS or >17 hexes from all enemies.  Note that you don't get to inspect the enemy stacks, ONLY THE TOPMOST UNIT (A2.9).  If he also has scenario-designated ??, he would do his setup and place those out of your view, then you both would check for free ??.

ground_truth_answer:
Are the following true?
5/8" MTR are being considered as Guns, and may thusly Intensive Fire. 1/2" MTR can't.
1/2" MTR are SW but can't Subsequent First Fire, only MG can.

Q: Can a 5/8" MTR use Intensive Fire, even though its ROF has been previously exhausted?

Q: Is there any situation where a MTR FP wouldn't be halved on the IFT (CH excepted)?
1) Yes. One interesting case is that the MTR can Intensive Fire using SMOKE ammo. That also applies to non-MTRs, but with MTRs you can potentially get off a series of SMOKE with ROF, then throw an Intensive Fire SMOKE round down range for good measure.

2) There are technicalities where the weapon is called in real life a "mortar" but is not in ASL terms. So the British PIAT SW and the Petard on the Churchill AVRE are spigot mortars, and they use full FP. For a weapon marked as a MTR I can't think of any. When OBA represents the same weapon (e.g. 80+ OBA often represents 81mm mortars—not always because it might instead be a 25-lbr or a German 88), the OBA is at "full" FP, i.e. sixteen FP. But when used on board the MTR always uses Area Target Type, and so is always halved. Note it is the Target Type that halves the FP, not the weapon type.

title: MTR fire against Passengers in OT vehicle/LC (1)
raw_question:
How to resolve a successful TH Mortar fire against Infantry units (passengers) being carried by a moving Armored but OT Landing Craft at sea (un-beached)? 
First, regarding G 12.63, although the counter is showing front and rear/side AF, as the LC is OT, should it be considered as fully armored or not fully armored for the Area Fire resolution?
Then, how should the MTR attack be resolved against the Infantry units being carried? Do G 12.672 Ordnance Hull Hit and 12.673 Ordnance Turret Hit apply when firing a MTR ordnance against a LC? Should the C 1.55 procedure be disregarded then?

This is quite confusing to me.
ground_truth_answer:
The difference between fully-armored and partially-armored is that a partially-armored vehicle or LC has a ★ for one or more of its aspects/facings [D1.22]. Any vehicle with numeric armor factors for all its aspects/facings is fully armored even if open-topped. 

As a side note, *all* partially- and fully-armored LC are open-topped.

On the LC Destruction Table (after G12.64) cross-reference the effects DR vs. the TK# on the HE (Area Target Type; OBA) column. For a fully-armored LC if it is ≤ the TK# on the IFT column, Passengers are attacked collaterally at half FP on a hull hit per G12.672. On a turret hit the crew is attacked but not the Passengers.

query: FFE2 and Smoke: I know another round of HE goes off on the FFE2, but if I opted for Smoke on FFE1, does another round of Smoke fall on the same hex's, basically refreshing the Smoke to +3 again, or is the Fire Mission over after the first round of Smoke has fallen on FFE1?
title: FFE2 and Smoke
raw_question: I know another round of HE goes off on the FFE2, but if I opted for Smoke on FFE1, does another round of Smoke fall on the same hex's, basically refreshing the Smoke to +3 again, or is the Fire Mission over after the first round of Smoke has fallen on FFE1?
ground_truth_answer:
Depends on when you called it...

Prep Fire for FF1, then +3 smokes are placed.  Assuming you don't correct, then during next Defensive Fire they'll drop ANOTHER +2 level of smoke (see A24.5).  This doesn't really matter too much as the max DRM is +3 (+4 if units are in the hex).

However, if you fire first in the DFPh, then the OBA places +2 Smoke...which is then removed at the start of your PFPh, only to be replaced by +3 Smoke.

If you correct Smoke OBA after firing during the PFPh, you can get some pretty impressive Smoke fields laid down... as you'll get 7 hexes of +3 Smoke and another 7 of +2 Smoke (though these latter will disappear at the start of your next PFPh).

-K

Capturing/Entering Abandoned vehicles: The rules in A21.2 are pretty clear on capturing an abandoned vehicle. However, it does state that if infantry of both side in the location can both roll to capture the vehicle. 

The rules for entering an abandoned vehicle in D5.42 does not indicate if this is for only friendly MMC or both friendly and enemy MMC?

My read is that if you want to take two turns to capture the vehicle by moving to the vehicle location first turn and then occupy the vehicle in the second turn or take one turn by advancing into CC and capturing (Automatic capture if no enemy infantry in location) you choose. title: Capturing/Entering Abandoned vehicles
raw_question:
The rules in A21.2 are pretty clear on capturing an abandoned vehicle. However, it does state that if infantry of both side in the location can both roll to capture the vehicle. 

The rules for entering an abandoned vehicle in D5.42 does not indicate if this is for only friendly MMC or both friendly and enemy MMC?

My read is that if you want to take two turns to capture the vehicle by moving to the vehicle location first turn and then occupy the vehicle in the second turn or take one turn by advancing into CC and capturing (Automatic capture if no enemy infantry in location) you choose. However, CC is the only method available if enemy in the location. 

Any clarification would be great. Thanks all.
ground_truth_answer:
Per A21.2, "If there are no enemy Personnel in the Location with an Abandoned enemy AFV, it may be captured automatically by any Infantry unit in the same location at the end of a CCPh but Ambush is NA." The rule then continues on with "otherwise," i.e. the case where there are units from both sides. Note that the vehicle has to be *enemy* in order to be captured "automatically." A friendly vehicle not in a CC location would have to be re-manned per D5.42.

There is also this q&a: 
"A21.2 & D5.42 1). Friendly Infantry in the same Location as an Abanoned enemy vehicle are not in a CC Location if no other enemy units are present (because an Abandoned vehicle is not a Unit because it is incapable of movement (Index)). So said Friendly Infantry may not Capture the AFV using A21.2 mechanics because said Infantry is not in a CC Location. Yes?
A. No. Read the sentence right before that. An Abandoned enemy AFV may be automatically captured at the end of the CCPh, regardless of being in a “CC Location” or not.
2). May a Friendly AFV be Crewed this way?
A. No, unless actually in CC."

DRM when a 10-2 leader becomes a heroic leader: 1) If a 10-2 leader becomes a Hero can he use the leader DRM of -2 if he only directs fire from the location he is in, or must he use the heroic DRM of -1?

2) If he enters CC in a building, can he use the Heros stealty ability in Ambush and then the leader DRM of -2 in CC?
title: DRM when a 10-2 leader becomes a heroic leader
raw_question:
1) If a 10-2 leader becomes a Hero can he use the leader DRM of -2 if he only directs fire from the location he is in, or must he use the heroic DRM of -1?

2) If he enters CC in a building, can he use the Heros stealty ability in Ambush and then the leader DRM of -2 in CC?
ground_truth_answer:
1) If a 10-2 leader becomes a Hero can he use the leader DRM of -2 if he only directs fire from the location he is in, or must he use the heroic DRM of -1?

2) If he enters CC in a building, can he use the Heros stealty ability in Ambush and then the leader DRM of -2 in CC?

1) a heroic leader may use either its leadership DRM or its heroic DRM in an attack. If it wants to use its leadership DRM it can't add its FP to the attack; conversely if it wants to use its heroic DRM it must add its FP (at normal range) to the attack.
2) Both the stealthy drm and any leadership drm would apply to ambush. The stealthy drm is not an application of the heroic drm, which does not apply to ambush. In CC the player can choose which DRM (heroic or leadership) to apply, except that a SMC attacking alone can't use the leadership DRM for itself but could use the heroic DRM.

A11.4 "Whenever Infantry advance into CC (unless reinforcing a Melee) in a woods/building Location or with/against a concealed unit(s) an Ambush can conceivably occur."
Since pillboxes have limited CAs and LOS, it's almost trivial to enter a pillbox hex and remain concealed, even in open ground. But beyond that, pillboxes can be set up in grain,  orchards, etc., making it easy to advance in while concealed even if there are other units around to provide LOS to the pillbox hex. And pillboxes can set up in woods, which doesn't require a concealed unit at all.

Moreover, it could be the unit inside the pillbox that's the concealed one. Although B30.7 says attacks against a pillbox aren't affected by concealment, other effects of concealment still apply.

query:
WA (Wall Advantage effects): There are 3 pages in the rulebook describing how to/when gain/loose Wall Advantage, but what does the WA do actually!? What's the benefit?
Does a unit need to get the WA in order to get the +2 TEM? Anything else I'd be missing?
title: WA (Wall Advantage effects)
raw_question:
There are 3 pages in the rulebook describing how to/when gain/loose Wall Advantage, but what does the WA do actually!? What's the benefit?
Does a unit need to get the WA in order to get the +2 TEM? Anything else I'd be missing?
ground_truth_answer:
Does a unit need to get the WA in order to get the +2 TEM? 

This is one of the more confusing aspects of Wall Advantage. The target does not necessarily need WA to use the wall TEM. In order to use the wall(/hedge/bocage) TEM it is sufficient that the *enemy* unit that is firing does *not* have Wall Advantage over the hexside. If the unit firing is not adjacent to the target, then it can't have WA over a hexside of the target hex and the target can use the hexside TEM. That's a simple case. When the firer is adjacent (and most likely ADJACENT) then by possessing WA it can deny the use of the hexside terrain to the target. Otherwise the target, whether because it possesses WA or because neither side has WA, can choose to use the hexside TEM.

Anything else I'd be missing?

There are lots of ifs, buts and gotchas with WA. This thread covers non-adjacent firers and also vehicles in hexes with positive TEM. PRC [EXC: motorcyclists (really?)] never get hexside TEM. Walls can only be at one level (ground or hilltop) and with hillside walls [B9.35, B9.62] only units on one side of the wall can use wall advantage. Hexside TEM can be reduced by sufficient elevation advantage [B9.33]; this can be very helpful in an urban setting where level two buildings have walls or hedges around them.

query:
Pillbox versus LATW: Does the +7 TEM from the pillbox in KK5 apply to the TH number of the BAZ44? 

If so, how to get rid of that pillbox? Is CC the only way to get rid of units entrenched under such a pillbox counter?
title: Pillbox versus LATW
raw_question:
Does the +7 TEM from the pillbox in KK5 apply to the TH number of the BAZ44? 

If so, how to get rid of that pillbox? Is CC the only way to get rid of units entrenched under such a pillbox counter?
ground_truth_answer:
From 30. PILLBOXES
30.2
…Fire from inside a pillbox into its own hex is limited to CC, or SMOKE grenade placement, or a Thrown DC (30.31), or to vertices of its CA, or to PBF vs units currently crossing the CA hexsides of its own hex.

30.6 SAME HEX: Same-level units inside and outside a pillbox in the same hex are ADJACENT…

How to understand "to vertices of its CA"? We're talking of units occupying the same hex here, no?
Can same-level infantry units outside a pillbox in the same hex point blank fire at enemy units inside the pillbox? If so, is the CA TEM to be applied?

Tracing LOS to(/from) the "vertex of its CA" would apply to an attack that traced LOS from the pillbox (i.e. the center dot of the hex) to a vertex of that same hex and by reciprocity vice-versa. The most obvious case for such an attack/LOS would be against a unit in bypass of an obstacle in that hex. If the pillbox is in a woods hex and an enemy unit bypassed that woods obstacle in front of the CA, the units in the pillbox could take a whack. Infantry can't remain in bypass, but a vehicle and (I believe) cavalry may, and as such may fire back at the pillbox through its CA [B30.1]. There may be a few other causes for such a LOS; underbelly attacks [D4.3] would be one example but that would not allow a return attack. Since Infantry can't remain in bypass of a hex I can think of no situations where an Infantry unit in a pillbox hex but outside the pillbox would trace LOS from the vertex of the hex, for making an attack anyway.

See my just-completed example for the two different random selections after a Critical Hit. You can end up in a situation where different units are affected by different results. In my example, a 2KIA may not eliminate two units even though there are four present if only one of them is selected by Random Selection for the Critical Hit.

There are other ways that different units might be affected by different results. For example some units might be in a foxhole and some outside. Or some units may be holding flamethrowers. Or indirect Fire might hit a building and some units might be on upper levels and others on lower levels [B23.32]. I'm sure there are others. In each of these cases if there are multiple units but only one unit is affected by, say, a 2KIA, only that one unit is eliminated by that 2KIA. The other units are affected by their respective results (which may also be #KIAs, but may not be. 

So another quick example: 120mm OBA is firing on four units, three in a trench and one outside (with zero TEM). The effects DR is a three, a 2KIA for the unit outside the trench and a 3MC for units in the trench. The unit outside the trench is eliminated (but only one unit on a 2KIA) and the units in the trench take their 3MCs. No Random Selection is needed here.

From the digital rulebook:

…Once a MG has lost its Multiple ROF, it is marked with an appropriate Prep, First or Final Fire counter.

and 

9.3 SUSTAINED FIRE: A MG that attacks using Subsequent-First-Fire/ FPF (8.3/8.31), or during the DFPh while marked with a First Fire counter (8.4), is using Sustained Fire

Lesson - you get more opportunities to shoot during the movement phase, plus the ability to place Residual. Learning how to use firepower during the movement phase is one way to win at ASL.

query: Reducing an unbroken squad: I might have been playing this wrong for almost 2 years. Does a squad being reduced indeed keep their broken status!? So a full, unbroken squad, suffering reduction, would become an unbroken HS!?
title: Reducing an unbroken squad
raw_question: I might have been playing this wrong for almost 2 years. Does a squad being reduced indeed keep their broken status!? So a full, unbroken squad, suffering reduction, would become an unbroken HS!?
ground_truth_answer:
I might have been playing this wrong for almost 2 years. Does a squad being reduced indeed keep their broken status!? So a full, unbroken squad, suffering reduction, would become an unbroken HS!?
For the most part true but it depends upon how the squad comes across its CR. On a K/# result [A7.302] an unbroken squad is reduced to an unbroken halfsquad that then has to take the corresponding #MC, but from its unbroken side with its unbroken ML. However if a squad rolls a casualty MC (an original twelve [A10.31]), it is CR and always broken, even if the final DR was not enough to break the squad. It's very rare to come across a situation where a unit, especially a MMC, could theoretically pass a MC on an original twelve. Such a situation can be found, but the resulting halfsquad is always broken anyway by A10.31.

In other cases, a CR in Close Combat leaves an unbroken halfsquad from a full squad. Booby traps [B28.9] leave an unbroken halfsquad. Crew Small Arms [A11.62] leave an unbroken halfsquad. PF abuse [C13.36] leaves an unbroken halfsquad. A Japanese or CPVA striped squad striping again leaves an unbroken halfsquad (this technically isn't CR I suppose). I'm probably missing some other, uncommon cases.

You surely know that game! 😄
Thanks

query: Broken units and DM tokens: Does any broken unit automatically get a DM token when being fired at with enough FP to potentially cause a NMC? Whatever the attack DR result?
title: Broken units and DM tokens
raw_question: Does any broken unit automatically get a DM token when being fired at with enough FP to potentially cause a NMC? Whatever the attack DR result?
ground_truth_answer:
Does any broken unit automatically get a DM token when being fired at with enough FP to potentially cause a NMC? Whatever the attack DR result?
Correct. If an IFT attack *might* have inflicted a NMC that is enough. On a one FP flat a broken unit is marked DM regardless if the attack DR is a twelve, and even if the firing weapon breaks.

On a one FP up two the answer depends on whether the unit/weapon can cower. If it can cower, no DR can result in a NMC because an original snakeeyes cowers off the IFT and so no DM is placed, regardless of the actual IFT DR. If it can't cower the broken target is marked with a DM, again regardless of the actual DR. Those BMGs firing at long range can DM a broken unit hiding in a wooden building.

For ordnance a hit would have to be achieved first, but the actual *effects* DR doesn't matter. Ordnance doesn't cower, of course, but you would have to factor in TEM for the ATT.

Why did the moving unit not lose concealment straightaway, according to Chart A12.121 (note A specifically notes Detection) & how did they stay in the same hex subsequently?
Or did you mean to say they Advanced into the hex?
I did not mean to say anything; I did not specify how they came to be in the same hex at the start of the CCPh both concealed. It wasn't especially important to my question. In my particular case it was the obvious way, one Advanced on the other. But this can also happen if G.4 applies, which allows units to move into hexes with HIP enemy units without invoking Detection. It might also occur if Personnel unloads from a vehicle. query:
WA Non adjacent fire: I don´t seem to find a post about this.

It´s the german PFPh and a german squad have WA in G3.
A german Hero and 2 HS in G4 fires on the enemies in G2.

Do the enemies in G2 get Wall Tem or are they considered to be in Open Ground?
title: WA Non adjacent fire
raw_question:
I don´t seem to find a post about this.

It´s the german PFPh and a german squad have WA in G3.
A german Hero and 2 HS in G4 fires on the enemies in G2.

Do the enemies in G2 get Wall Tem or are they considered to be in Open Ground?
ground_truth_answer:
Only one Location can ever have WA over the same hexside, so they are in Open Ground because the Germans already have WA (B9.321).
The unit in G3 can fire on the target in G2 using in-hex TEM only, but it doesn't share its WA with units in other hexes. In fact if G3 were a multi-level building hex and there were Germans on an upper level, the target in G2 could use the wall TEM against an attack from the upper level despite the ground-level having WA. WA for one particular unit does not grant WA for all units firing through the hexside. See my above post quoting B9.31.

query:
PSK against a Jeep with a half squad and Sniper effects: Playing Apples to Apples, my half squad with a PSK hit a Jeep with a loaded half squad.  How is this resolved?

Shortly after, my opponent activated my Sniper.  My Sniper landed on a Half Track loaded with a Squad.  What happens to it and the Squad?  It was not designated as Buttoned up.
title: PSK against a Jeep with a half squad and Sniper effects
raw_question:
Playing Apples to Apples, my half squad with a PSK hit a Jeep with a loaded half squad.  How is this resolved?

Shortly after, my opponent activated my Sniper.  My Sniper landed on a Half Track loaded with a Squad.  What happens to it and the Squad?  It was not designated as Buttoned up.
ground_truth_answer:
The Sniper has two eligible targets:  the half track crew and the passenger squad.

Random Selection determines which gets attacked.

If it is the squad, it can be broken (by a dr 1) or pinned (by a dr 2) and can remain as a passenger (D6.62).

If it is the crew, the sniper will inflict either a Stun or STUN (ie Stun + recall) result (see D5.34 and D5.341).
As fate would have it, Random roll was 4 and 4.  So the Crew was STUNNED/Recalled and the Squad was Broken.  Do they stay loaded on the Half Track or are they allowed to bail out before the HT moves off the board in the MPh?

query: Halving FP for a MG with ROF as SFF vs DFPh?: I think I have had this wrong for a long time. See if this is right. A four FP squad with a two FP LMG fires on an ADJACENT target at twelve FP. The target is not eliminated and spent > one MP. The LMG keeps ROF. The defender could use DFF (not SFF) to fire again with the LMG alone at four FP. The squad could use SFF with its inherent only at four FP. It could use SFF with both its inherent *and* the LMG for six FP, firing the LMG as Sustained Fire even though the LMG retained ROF [A8.3]. Alternately the squad and LMG could fire in the DFPh against the ADJACENT target at eight FP, four FP for the inherent marked with First Fire, four FP for the LMG not marked with First Fire. In the DFPh the LMG would *not* be treated as using Sustained Fire because it retained ROF. Treating an unmarked MG as using Sustained Fire when firing together with inherent that is marked with First Fire only applies when using Subsequent First Fire and not in the DFPh.

ground_truth_answer:
Following along these same lines, could the LMG, after maintaining its ROF, fire at a unit that is further away than the unit it (and its owning squad) previously fired at? 

Yes, the LMG fired alone is not restricted by SFF restrictions because it is using DFF, not SFF. It can fire beyond the nearest KEU. It can fire at long range.

Also, could the LMG wait until the Defensive Fire Phase to fire at any unit, even though its owning Squad has previously First Fired?
Yes, as long as you don't mean something silly by "any" like, for example, a unit out of LOS. In the DFPh a unit/weapon not marked can fire normally, and a unit/weapon marked with First Fire can fire at an adjacent (or same hex) target.

query: LOS hills: Shouldn't the 4-6-7 in 3F9 be able to see the building on hill 3I10 since this is now a building on level 2?
title: LOS hills
raw_question: Shouldn't the 4-6-7 in 3F9 be able to see the building on hill 3I10 since this is now a building on level 2?
ground_truth_answer:
LOS is always traced to the base of the obstacle or terrain feature, not to all its height. 
If the building in 3I10 had a second story, there would be a LOS to that second story, which would be 2 levels from the ground. Or if it had a rooftop, which would be 1.5 levels from the ground, or a slope, which would be 1.75 levels from the ground. But the building's Level 0 is always out of LOS of that unit.

query:
D14.31 Impulse Movement, D7.1 OVR and A12.41 concealed infantry (AFV entering hex): My platoon of Italian tankettes starts in motion 25DD5 (level 2 open ground) and 25DD6 (base level 2; AFV in the wadi at level 1), like so:

On their first impulse, they each move one hex forward to 25CC6 (level 3 open ground) and 25CC7 (base level 2; AFV in the wadi at level 1), like so:

The tankette in 25CC6 secretly wants to OVR the Indian unit in that hex but because the hex contains only unknown enemy units it is exempt from the usual requirement of announcing the OVR as a combined expenditure with that of entering the hex (D7.1).

The Indian 4-4-7 tries to keep its concealment by taking a PAATC (A12.41) but fails and is revealed and pinned (I haven't placed the pin marker to avoid clutter):

What I want to do next is move onto impulse 2, in which the tankette in 25CC6 conducts an OVR for 3.25 MPs and the tankette in 25CC7 moves to 25BB6 (base level 3; AFV in the wadi at level 2, having ascended one level):

The cost of that impulse would be 7 MPs:  the most MP spent by any unit (4 MPs for the elevation change from 25CC7 to 25BB6 +2 MPs for the wadi +1 MP COT).

I can't think of a way for one unit to be ADJACENT and the other not ADJACENT.
Probably true.  Whenever there's a seeming asymmetry re ADJACENT, if one is clearly ADJACENT, then it's mutual, generally.

EX:
At first glance, one unit in an OG hex is lower-case adjacent to one in an abutting Marsh hex (because the OG dweller could not enter that Marsh hex in an APh).
B16.4 Infantry/Cavalry may enter a marsh hex only at the cost of their entire MF allotment (inclusive of a broken unit’s RtPh allotment); a marsh hex cannot be entered during the APh, nor can it be entered via Low Crawl (A10.52) [EXC to all: along a bridge]. Entry of a marsh hex from a lower elevation is a Minimum Move (A4.134).
That unit in Marsh is ADJACENT to the one in OG, though (because it could  enter that OG hex in an APh).

But the Index defintion doesn't require symmetry, only that one unit be ADJACENT -- when so, both are.
ADJACENT (Locations [and units in them] are considered ADJACENT if any Infantry unit in one Location could conceivably—ignoring any enemy presence—advance into the other during the APh and a LOS exists between the two Locations, excluding SMOKE Hindrance [B.10] and NVR [E1.101]
(Assuming Infantry and mutual LOS in this case.)

query:
Defensive options for AFVs?: So we're playing an early war scenario where there are a bunch of Pz I's versus superior (in terms of armor + gun size) French tanks.  It has proven to give us some good learning questions when an outclassed AFV faces another.

I /think/ we have a fairly good grasp now, but wanted to run this by the consigliere and see what we might have gotten wrong or were missing...

What can the weaker AFV due when confronted by the superior one...
1) Go for Deliberate Immobilization (need hull hit with a +5 DRM, but might be able to DI it in a bad location and then just avoid it)

2) Use defensive smoke dischargers to try to lay smoke during the enemy MPh.  This can be done either before or after a DFF shot (we think) and does NOT count as DFF.  But only get one attempt per enemy MPh.

3) Attempt to go into Motion during the enemy MPh provided the enemy tank didn't start in your LOS and you make the dr.  This has to be done BEFORE any DFF shots, but can be done before or after smoke discharger use.  Only get one attempt per enemy MPh, so make it count.  Not sure if this can be done AFTER the triggering vehicle is done moving and other units have moved (i.e. can you 'come back' to the AFV and declare a Motion attempt at the end of the enemy MPh, provided you haven't DFF'ed?).  If you succeed, remember that you can change your VCA and TCA.

4) Avoid engaging the enemy armor and let your infantry deal with them.  If you /have/ to engage them, look to get point blank rear shots via the 'swarm'.  Consider always staying in Motion since you're essentially rolling for a critical hit anyway.  Intensive Fire to get as many shots as possible when it makes sense.

I think that mostly covers the options (obviously some are going to be very situational and specific to the scenario, so I don't expect this to ever be a complete list).

ground_truth_answer:
A MG can't use Deliberate Immobilization [C5.71]. This takes that option off the table for the Pz I. Also French AFVs will often be small, making the DI shot that much worse.

For the particular pairing you suggest, early war French AFVs vs German Pz Is, the Germans may have some other advantages. Most often the French tanks will be radioless, meaning they are effectively slower because the platoon often has to make the same extra expenditure (crossing a wall/hedge, climbing a hill) multiple times. Often members of the platoon will hinder each others shots and/or prevent itself from having LOS (perhaps a member of the platoon can't make it past an obstacle). The factors make radioless vehicles less effective unit-for-unit. The French tanks are also often RST or 1MT, meaning they must be BU to fire, although that particular advantage is lost vs a Pz I (or Pz II). All this says the Germans should be more maneuverable than the French and more able to gain an advantage by movement.

That said the Pz I is not going to be killing many French AFVs (unless they are FT-17s, and even then). The typical French armor is around four AF, and the Pz I's basic TK# is four. Even with range and rear target that's not a recipe for slaughter. Based on this the German is probably looking for opportunities to use his tanks against infantry, and looking to avoid the French tanks using his superior maneuverability.

A9.223, "The MG malfunctions whenever its Fire Lane Residual FP attack DR is also an Original Malfunction DR." This is unlike regular residual, where the residual attack is completely disassociated from the unit/weapon that made the attack. For this reason it can be pretty scary to put down a firelane with B11 or worse weapons.

As another matter of trivia, the MG has to be "Good Order." "Good Order" for a weapon means it is fully manned (no lone leaders putting down firelanes), not malfunctioned (that's pretty much a gimmie) and not subject to Ammo Shortage. The last doesn't come up that often but for example if you are playing a CG and have isolated setup areas it can be a factor.

title: Alternate Hex Grain Fire Lanes and Hard Hindrances
raw_question:
LMG in 17U5 can try to create either of these two Alternate Hex Grain Fire Lanes, correct?

Are both dropped down to zero Fire Power because of the Orchard in 17V5?

Correct for the right alternate-hexgrain. For the left alternate-hexgrain all hexes in the firelane would get the +1 (hard) hindrance DRM. Per A9.222, "Because Fire Lane Residual FP is always traced from its source, the effects of Hindrance/hexside/bridge DRM are resolved as DRM to the Residual FP attack." Even though this says, "Residual FP attack," it is in the context of firelanes only.To be clear - as the example of my answer showed - "left" was from the point of view of the image, not of the MG.
U6, V7, W9 and X10 are not affected by the orchard in V5.

To be clear I always consider the alternate hexgrain naming left or right as based on which hex the firelane exits the firing unit. The alternate hexgrain firelane exits from U5 either through V5 or U6. The "left" alternate hexgrain would be the one that exits through V5; the "right" alternative hexgrain would be the one that exits through U6. I base this definition on A9.221, "Whenever that LOF lies along a hexside, the Alternate Hex Grain includes the hex either to the left or to the right of that hexside." This remains the same no matter how the picture is rotated. For your definition if the board would be inverted then left and right would switch.

I would apply the reasoning that prisoners not in the act of escape are not units because they don't have the ability to move independent of their guard [index: unit definition]. It is not super clear that prisoners in the act of escape are units, but at least in your case it seems likely that the DM would come off.

If in the act of escape they might be units or not, but when they make a CC attack vs the guard that would put the DM on [A10.62].

On further search there's the other reason the DM would come off and not be put on, even if ADJACENT to an escaping prisoner: A10.62, "A broken unit is also automatically under DM whenever a Known armed enemy unit is ADJACENT to it (even if it does not end the phase ADJACENT to it)." A prisoner is not armed, even an escaping one. If a prisoner attacks its broken guard in the CCPh, the guard becomes DM, but that would not be sufficient to DM a broken unit in the same hex or an ADJACENT hex that was not attacked.

ground_truth_answer:
Lou is correct.

Anything that provides a positive TEM/Hindrance DRM means that the hex is NOT 'Open Ground' per the definition in Rout (see A10.531).  Note that things like the unit being CX, BU MA, Pinned, in Motion, etc. also prevent a unit from Interdicting (basically anything that adds a DRM or halves the unit's attack strength negates the unit from being an Interdictor per A10.532).

In your case the unit could expend one MF (as non-assault movement) to enter an open ground Location as its first expenditure. That expenditure might be subject to Defensive First Fire, which in turn would benefit from FFNAM and might benefit from FFMO. Assuming the unit is attacked, survives and the attack places residual, the unit could now spend a MF to search. The Residual would attack first with FFMO and FFNAM applying. Then other units could also attack using Defensive First Fire; the would get FFNAM and possibly FFMO as appropriate.

If there are DFF options, is it resolved before resolving the search dr ? 

The search action "completes" on announcing the expenditure regardless of the result of any DFF. Most actions complete on announcing the expenditure. One major exception is placing a DC, where the unit must survive any DFF unbroken and unpinned [A23.3].

my opponent thinks if I declare searching MF, he can DFF before search happens ... I said you resolve the MF first i.e., search and all search casualties etc first ?

query:
Rowhouse question from CSW: Not sure if people also follow CSW here, but thought I'd share this here before I consider submitting an errata request to the eASLRB maintainers.

Someone had a situation with two Soviet squads in SEPARATE, but adjacent rowhouse hexes (i.e. they both were in rowhouse hexes, but of distinct and separate rowhouse buildings).  By a strict reading of the rules, they could not form a FG together because they both were in rowhouse hexes and didn't have another unit in the FG who wasn't in a rowhouse hex.

Note that this is distinct from the movement rules (rowhouse hex to rowhouse hex), in which the rule explicitly calls out 'of the same building'.

The general consensus was that the FG /should/ be allowed, since they are not in the same rowhouse building.  IMO, it makes sense either way (one could 'zen' it that rowhouses don't have as many openings for supporting fire, so units in rowhouse hexes...same building or not ... wouldn't be able to effectively coordinate fire.  But one could also 'zen' it that the intent was adjacent and in the same rowhouse building, NOT separate buildings altogether.  Thoughts?
title: Rowhouse question from CSW
raw_question:
Not sure if people also follow CSW here, but thought I'd share this here before I consider submitting an errata request to the eASLRB maintainers.

Someone had a situation with two Soviet squads in SEPARATE, but adjacent rowhouse hexes (i.e. they both were in rowhouse hexes, but of distinct and separate rowhouse buildings).  By a strict reading of the rules, they could not form a FG together because they both were in rowhouse hexes and didn't have another unit in the FG who wasn't in a rowhouse hex.

Note that this is distinct from the movement rules (rowhouse hex to rowhouse hex), in which the rule explicitly calls out 'of the same building'.

The general consensus was that the FG /should/ be allowed, since they are not in the same rowhouse building.  IMO, it makes sense either way (one could 'zen' it that rowhouses don't have as many openings for supporting fire, so units in rowhouse hexes...same building or not ... wouldn't be able to effectively coordinate fire.  But one could also 'zen' it that the intent was adjacent and in the same rowhouse building, NOT separate buildings altogether.  Thoughts?
ground_truth_answer:
The relevant sections you are referring to are:
A7.5 FIRE GROUP (FG): Two or more units/weapons joining together to 
make a combined fire attack are a FG. Two SMC manning the same SW are 
not a FG as they are considered one combined firing unit. A FG may consist 
of units from more than one Location only if each participating unit occu-
pies a Location ADJACENT to another participating unit of the same FG. It 
is possible to have a FG composed of a virtually unlimited string of ADJA-
CENT Locations; provided each Location in the FG contains a unit that is 
participating in the attack. ... 

and

adjacent (hexes are considered adjacent if they share a common hexside): A.8

ADJACENT (Locations [and units in them] are considered ADJACENT if 
any Infantry unit in one Location could conceivably—ignoring any enemy 
presence—advance into the other during the APh and a LOS exists between 
the two Location ...  

and

 part of B23.71 Infantry in a Rowhouse may move/rout/ad-
vance/Withdraw-from-CC directly into another Rowhouse hex of the same 
building only at the ground or Rooftop (23.8) level; if at the ground level they 
must specify which side of the building they are “bypassing”. Such units mov-
ing/routing on the ground level expend three MF (one to “bypass” in the hex 
it is leaving where it would be attacked by any OBA/Residual-FP and two to 
enter the building), and can be Interdicted or Defensive First Fired upon with 
FFMO/FFNAM DRM by any unit capable of doing so that can trace a LOS 
to the vertex of the hexside crossed by the moving/routing unit on that side of 
the building. ... Units in different Rowhouses may not form a FG unless each is ADJACENT to 
another unit that is not in a Rowhouse but that is part of that FG. Each hex of 
a Rowhouse building is always considered a separate building for Rout and 
Mopping Up purposes but not for Building Control.

So, I don't think your comment is correct.  Units in adjacent rowhouse hexes at the ground or Rooftop levels ARE 'ADJACENT', as they can clearly advance to the adjacent rowhouse hex of the same building at 3 MFs.

And the FG text requires two conditions... the 'ADJACENT' as you note, plus "not in a Rowhouse but that is part of that FG".  Note that the FG text never includes the 'of the same building' clarifier that the move/advance/rout language uses.  One uses 'Rowhouse' and the other uses 'Rowhouse hex', which might be the nuance that covers this??  I honestly don't know.

query: ROF and a FF Squad ?: I First Fired a Squad along with its LMG.  The LMG kept Rate.  Does the fact that the Squad has already First Fired limit the LMG's options to fire only at the nearest in distance enemy?
title: ROF and a FF Squad ?
raw_question: I First Fired a Squad along with its LMG.  The LMG kept Rate.  Does the fact that the Squad has already First Fired limit the LMG's options to fire only at the nearest in distance enemy?
ground_truth_answer:
it just can't combine with the squad's firepower any longer.
The LMG can combine with the squad's inherent SFF, but if it does it will be treated as if using SFF/sustained fire itself. A8.3, "Whenever a unit uses Subsequent First Fire, it must use all MG/IFE in its possession (up to the unit's normal operation capabilities; 7.35-.353) as Subsequent First Fire or forfeit their use for the remainder of that Player Turn (barring FPF)."

There aren't many circumstances when a player might choose to do this. Ordinarily in such a situation the player will fire a MG without the squad's inherent SFF until the MG runs out of ROF. One case where you might consider it is if an 8-3-8 possesses a MMG. The MMG would fire at four FP without the squad but the 8-3-8 (SFF) and the MMG (forced to use SFF per A8.3 above) would fire at six FP even though the MMG is also using sustained fire. I can't think of a case where you might do this with a LMG but perhaps someone else can come up with one.

raw_question:
Hi there,
we are investigating on that question so hardly since 1-2 hours:

In the above mentioned chart it says:

16: (...) 1-hex range (2-hex range +1) +2

and

2: 1-hex range vs. stopped vehicle (2-hex range: -1): -2 (...)

Those both somehow should apply to stopped targets or moving firerer

A) What the hell should that mean? I really can't interprete that rule precisely. Somebody have an explanation?
B) I also searched in the GOB but couldn't find a referring rule in Chapter C5/C6. To which rule of FullASL does that ASLsk-Rule refer?

Thanks for answers guys!
ground_truth_answer:
I thought it is somekind of Calculation (1-hex range....) but it actually means "A hex range of 1"

Correct, it should not be read as, "One minus the hex-range vs stopped vehicle..." It should be read as, "One-hex (with a dash joining the two words) range vs stopped vehicle..." 

The basic idea for ASL is that the TH chart is divided into six-hex-range segments (0-6, 7-12, 13-18, although the first is actually seven hexes), but in fact there is a substantial improvement at ranges of one hex and two hexes. In ASL this is adjusted by having a -2 TH Point Blank Range DRM at a range of one hex and a -1 TH DRM at a range of two hexes. In ASLSK the designers decided to change the way this was calculated (but not the end result) by having separate segments for range one and range two on the TH chart for infantry target type. So far so good, but when a vehicle is the target there is no special columns for ranges one and two, so the #25 DRM is added. This means that ASLSK is in a half-way state, where the ASL DRM is an ASLSK DRM when using the vehicular target type but baked into the TH chart when using the infantry target type.

And there is a further complication that when the firing vehicle is not stopped, the Point Blank Range DRM does not apply. This is handled in the #25 DRM by the parenthetical for the vehicular target type, but when using the Infantry Target Type the adjustment baked into the TH table has to be subtracted out by the #16 TH DRM.

Note that you can't be using the ASLSK#2 chart for all this. None of these adjustments are necessary in ASLSK#2 because there are no vehicles. You must be using the ASLSK#3 (or later) chart.

Personally I think the ASL way is simpler when there are vehicles. I suspect that when the designers created the ASLSK#2 TH chart they didn't realize they were going to have to jump through so many hoops to get the right values in ASLSK#3. But that is speculation.

query: Berserk and the APh: So my opponent just Defensive Fired at my Adjacent Russian Squad, making them go Berserk.  Reading 15.431, my newly Berserk Squad, which had previously Prep fired, cannot Advance into Combat?  They have to wait until their next Mph?  Is there some significance for that?
title: Berserk and the APh
raw_question: So my opponent just Defensive Fired at my Adjacent Russian Squad, making them go Berserk.  Reading 15.431, my newly Berserk Squad, which had previously Prep fired, cannot Advance into Combat?  They have to wait until their next Mph?  Is there some significance for that?
ground_truth_answer:
The reason for not advancing is fairly obvious. They're represented as doing all-out charge at their target, with 8MFs, which matches the maximum any infantry unit will ever go (possible EXC - downhill skiers), without ever going CX. Advance is supposed to be a more cautious creeping forward (back, sideways...) that can't be shot at. For simplicity's sake, units can occasionally be denied a charge at all when they go berserk at an odd time. I'd think some sort of exception for guys going berserk late in their own turn would make a certain amount of sense, but then you'd have to remember that this one hasn't charged yet, and possibly let guys fire at them (since it is a charge)... and you'd tie the turn sequence in knots fast.

On ambushing, I'll also note that you have a potential ambush whenever someone advances into appropriate terrain. So, if someone charges into a hex, and then someone else advances into the same hex (easier now that the defender is too busy to fire), you can have an ambush with berserk units. Have fun with the +1 berserk modifier though.

title: Concealment issues
raw_question: Having a rules meltdown with Concealment.  We are setting up 126 Commando Schenke.  The Russians get 13 Concealment counters in their OOB.  How does that work again?  All the Russians will set up in buildings (concealment Terrain), so will they be Concealed automatically and 6 Dummy Stacks may then be placed on board?  Or do the 13 OOB given Concealment counters go on the real Squads?
ground_truth_answer:
So since the Germans set up on map as well, if I wanted to create 2 or 3 Dummy Stacks, I would use whats left of the OOB given Concealment counters to Conceal real squads, leaving the ones that won't be seen after the German set up to be concealed then, correct? And if I leave a real squad up close and in LOS of a German Squad, even though in Concealment terrain, they would not be automatically given a Concealment counter? Correct?
Correct on both counts. A unit in LOS at start can't get a free "?", disregarding HIP for Guns, but can have an OB-granted "?" placed on it if in concealment terrain.

You can also leave units unconcealed where they won't be seen to gain free "?" after all setup is done. Your opponent can see the top counter, but can't peel apart the stack. This sometimes suggests stacking things in odd ways at start, for instance a stack with a halfsquad, a HMG and a 9-2 leader might be set up with the HMG possessed by the 9-2 and the halfsquad on top. You just have to remember to exchange the HMG to the halfsquad in the first turn RPh. You could even fake this by putting a halfsquad on top of two OB-granted "?".

ground_truth_answer:
I have a question about the British Carrier A with a BMG as MA, and the British Mark VIB with a CMG as MA
If I use those MGs can I:
-	make a TH attempt on the VTT, and after I have exhausted ROF make a IF shot? 
-	make a IFT shot(first fire) on a squad who moved 2 hexes, and if I exhausted ROF also make a subsequent first fire shot if I wish?

You may use IF (q&a below) but not SFF. SFF is only available to Infantry. Per A9.3 it could use sustained fire in the DFPh.

"C5.6 May a vehicular-mounted MG/ATR/light-MTR use Intensive Fire?
A. Yes, if it is MA. Such a weapon is considered a Gun (C2.1). [An93a; An95w; An96; Mw]"

Note: there is a q&a saying an IFE Gun may use SFF: "C2.29 May an IFE-capable Gun that has exhausted its Multiple ROF use IFE again as Intensive Fire?
A. No; it could only use Sustained Fire, and only if also using Subsequent-First/Final-Protective Fire or Final Fire (since the use of Sustained Fire is permitted only to a DEFENDER MG/IFE-Gun and only during the MPh/DFPh). [An92; An95w; An96; Mw]"

It's not clear if this also applies to an IFE-capable Gun on a vehicle (i.e. not infantry-manned). It's also not clear if this extends to MGs. Even though the IFE/MG kwould be a Gun (as in the first q&a), A8.3 only grants SFF to Infantry. I would say the q&a does not grant license to a vehicle to use SFF, but a q&a might easily prove me wrong.

query:
WP in a hex with ground and 2nd lvl units: We had this come up in our last session and we weren't sure of the answer.

Basically, a US MTR fired WP at a concealed unit on the 2nd lvl of a building.  There were also concealed units on the ground level of the hex, but these were out of LOS of the MTR.

The MTR rolled a successful hit versus the concealed stack on the 2nd level.  Since these were the hardest to hit units in the MTRs LOS and given that Area Target Type effects the entire hex, we felt that this also meant the units on the ground level were hit.  This seems to be supported from C3.33.

However, in looking up the Smoke rules, it states that Smoke is /placed in the ground level/ of the hex (exception for interior buildings but this wasn't the case for us).  We get that this means the smoke hindrance extends from Ground level up to lvl 4 for the WP (versus from lvl 2 up to lvl 6), but we weren't sure if this means that ONLY the concealed unit at ground level is subject to the NMC and loss of concealment.

I.e. does the unit on the 2nd lvl also suffer the effects of a "Hit" by WP?
title: WP in a hex with ground and 2nd lvl units
raw_question:
We had this come up in our last session and we weren't sure of the answer.

Basically, a US MTR fired WP at a concealed unit on the 2nd lvl of a building.  There were also concealed units on the ground level of the hex, but these were out of LOS of the MTR.

The MTR rolled a successful hit versus the concealed stack on the 2nd level.  Since these were the hardest to hit units in the MTRs LOS and given that Area Target Type effects the entire hex, we felt that this also meant the units on the ground level were hit.  This seems to be supported from C3.33.

However, in looking up the Smoke rules, it states that Smoke is /placed in the ground level/ of the hex (exception for interior buildings but this wasn't the case for us).  We get that this means the smoke hindrance extends from Ground level up to lvl 4 for the WP (versus from lvl 2 up to lvl 6), but we weren't sure if this means that ONLY the concealed unit at ground level is subject to the NMC and loss of concealment.

I.e. does the unit on the 2nd lvl also suffer the effects of a "Hit" by WP?
ground_truth_answer:
If the only in-LOS unit was at level two and there were out-of-LOS units at levels one and zero, after a hit on at least one in-LOS unit, the WP would drop to ground level and cause a WP NMC there, but the unit at level one would only be hit and affected if the hardest-to-hit in-LOS unit were hit.

One of our players pointed to A24.31 as the reason why the 2nd level actually does NOT suffer the NMC... pointing to the first red-font text below. 

 24.31 CASUALTIES: The chemical agents in WP caused discomfort and 
could result in demoralization/casualties. All units (including friendly ones) 
except a non-CE, CT AFV in a Location with a WP counter must take a 
NMC when the WP is placed (by any means) [EXC: non-moving units in 
First Fire] in that Location (not when it drifts or they move into it) or when 
hit by ordnance WP [EXC: if the WP does not rise to that elevation (24.4)]. 
See C1.71 for OBA. The NMC causes DM status (10.62), and also causes loss 
of concealment if the affected unit is in LOS of a Good Order enemy ground 
unit. Leadership, CE DRM and TEM apply as negative DRM to the NMC 
(treating grenades as if a Direct Fire attack for TEM purposes). However, if 
a CH (or Air Burst when using Indirect Fire) is obtained with WP, TEM are 
applied to the NMC as positive DRM instead. A CH with WP grenades oc-
curs if the colored dr of the MC DR is a 6.

Specifically, the language of 'in a Location with a WP counter' combined with the fact that the COUNTER is placed at the Ground Level made him feel that only the ground level person would suffer the WP NMC (and regardless of whether he was 'hit' by the original TH roll, as A24.31 never says they have to be HIT by the WP...only that they are 'in the Location with a WP counter').

However, the second red-font text made us confused because that implies that ALL levels 0 - 4 of a building would be impacted by the WP ... otherwise, why have the "exception: if the WP does not rise to that elevation" clause?  Since the WP clearly rises to levels 1 /and/ 2 of the building, it would seem to us that a successful Hit on the level 2, which then "places" the smoke at ground level per C8.52, also would impact ground level and 1st level ("8.52 SMOKE ammunition is always placed at ground level in any target hex which is hit on the Area Target Type, except Interior Building hexes, even if the only visible part of that hex is the upper level of a building. ").

As a follow-on quiz, what would happen if there were *no* non-HIP units in LOS on the second level, but there was an unconcealed unit out-of-LOS at the first level and a concealed, small Gun out-of-LOS at ground level. What are the possible results if the attacker is a MTR or a non-MTR firing WP or HE with LOS only to the second level? What are the DRM to the attack (for the target hex only; assume there are no out-of-hex DRM like hindrance, CA change, etc.)?

Per C3.33, if firing HE there would be no effect ... this is actually covered by the bocage example referenced in B9.521, as there are no 'hardest to hit' target available.  If firing WP, the DRM would actually be BETTER for them (as they wouldn't apply the +2 for concealment ... a rule I hate, fwiw) and it would effect ground level (for sure) and still-to-be-debated, level 1 :).

A truck carrying a crew and towing a Gun enters a hex and stops. Defensive First Fire against both the truck and the crew (D.8 Collateral Attack) is ineffectual but leaves Residual FP. 

The crew unloads and attempts to unhook the Gun. The crew will be attacked by the Residual FP with -1 FFNAM (and possibly -1 FFMO since the truck is unarmored). The truck is also attacked by the Residual FP. I *think* this is resolved with one DR on the IFT.

If the truck is destroyed then the Gun is also destroyed but the crew is not affected because they are Infantry not PRC (D5.43). If the crew is pinned or broken then the Gun remains hooked to the truck. Any unpinned Good Order MMC (or five SMC) can attempt to unhook the Gun not just the original crew (C10.111)

ground_truth_answer:
Perhaps I should have phrased it like this instead: "Is advance movement a form of assault movement"?

As answered above, no. Assault Movement is a form of MPh movement. Advance is a change of one Location in the Advance Phase. Although they share many features, in particular changing Locations and having to think about MF costs for such a change, there are many, many differences. You can't Recover SW in the APh, for instance. There's no enemy attacks in the APh beyond passive attacks like minefields and OBA FFEs. You don't exactly expend MF in the APh; rather you consider the cost and if it exceeds a particular amount you have to use Advance vs. Difficult Terrain. In the rules you don't see the phrase "advance movement" in general; instead "movement" or "movement in the MPh" is contrasted with "Advance." See A.3 for example. So although Advance is akin to movement in the MPh in that infantry units can translate their position on the board (and, for the purposes of this thread, the concealment loss rules are somewhat similar), there are a large number of differences between the two.

1) The Germans will get a shot during their portion of the turn (either during MPH or their AFPh).  We cannot go CE, but could attempt to go in Motion or attempt to use smoke (either our smoke pot for a DR<= 3 (sP 5 -1 for BU, -1 for Hatten Special Rule) or a smoke grenade (dr=1). Can only do one. The smoke grenade would dissipate at the end of the enemy MPh. In that case the German would likely wait until the AFPh, assuming he has timed his MP expenditures correctly and come into LOS in the last two (or three) MP. If he hasn't the smoke grenades may force him either to take a premature shot or to spend more MP than expected in LOS. The smoke grenade is slightly higher odds but the sP has slightly better coverage. No clear winner.

2) Assuming we don't go in Motion or get smoke /and/ the JPZ IV misses its AFPh shot at us, the turn ends and we get to the US player turn.  This is where I'm somewhat uncertain as to our options and how they play out.  We can't Prep Fire because we're BU, so during our MPh what exactly are our options?

Correct, can't Prep.

- If we declare going CE and firing before starting the tank and leaving the hex, what happens?  Does this result in a Gun Duel option for the JPZ IV?  Would our lower die be doubled or would we just have to add +2 to our To Hit roll and not qualify for Acquisition?

Declaring a shot without expending MP *does* allow the rarely seen DEFENDER Gun Duel. The lower dr is not doubled for the attack because you are not non-stopped, and in any case the doubling does not apply to the Gun Duel calculation [C2.2401]. The attack would be liable to both case B & case C DRMs (case B *always* applies when any case C does except case C³), and because the M18 is not eligible for a Gyro, that means a minimum +4 TH DRM for the Gun Duel. Unless the JgdPz IV has done something really stupid (e.g. it has to change its CA), it wins the Gun Duel.

- If we start up (1 MP), then the JPZ IV gets to shoot at us with no Moving/Motion vehicle DRM, correct?  As we haven't left the hex yet so we are not technically 'Moving'.  We could go CE or not, but if we expend the start MP then the JPZ IV is always going to get the first shot on us.  Or is this another "gun duel" opportunity (this time for us)?

The Moving Target DRM (case J) does not apply. On the other had if the JgdPz IV has moved in close, point blank range (case L) no longer does.

This would be a Gun Duel opportunity for the ATTACKER this time but again the DRM are such that the DEFENDER wins. In both cases if the unit wanting to declare Gun Duel has to change CA, it can't declare a Gun Duel.

Obviously if we managed to go into Motion the previous MPh, we could move out of the JPZ IV's LOS before he could get a shot on us during our MPh ... but chances are the JPZ IV would only expend 2 or 3 MPs in our LOS, so not a guarantee of being able to go into Motion.
If the JgdPz IV has not moved to point blank range your best bet may to to go CE and attempt to throw smoke grenades. The sP is lower odds.

I assume you know that an AFV must use its entire MP allotment. If it stops and has not expended all its MP it is assumed to spend the rest of its MPh in Delay, which will increase the chances of a successful Motion dr. If your opponent is not careful he may make a mistake. If he does not, in the words of the great American armor leader, Captain Dezi Arnez, "Lieutenant Lucy, you got som' 'splainin' to do."

I 've played it like this : berserk enters the melee location - there is no any defensive fire form the melee location - in the AFph the bersekers fire TPBF/2 vs all enemy and friends - in the CCph the bersekers join the melee , not sure if they have to attack and defend alone or they may add their FP to friendly units ....  and they remain locked in melee and berserk until eliminate all or are eliminated. Correct regarding the choice of target and lack of DFF/DF. Although the Berserk unit may attack in the AFPh it is not required to do so [A15.432]; if it does all Melee units would be attacked. Berserk units may not be part of a multi-location fire group [A7.54] but by their nature CC attacks are never multi-location, so that restriction does not affect Berserk units' attacks in the CCPh. Like other units, a Berserk unit might come out of Melee in other ways, e.g. if an outside attack or SAN eliminated the enemy unit holding it in Melee, or an outside attack eliminated it, or if the enemy unit was a vehicle, and it decided to drive away, or some other unit also in the CC/Melee eliminates the enemy. But most often you are right the Berserk unit will remain in Melee until the Melee ends "normally." It cannot attempt to withdraw while Berserk [A11.2].

Here is my attempt to answer your very abundant question (I would suggest that you asked more synthetic questions, so that one doesn't get lost in the maze of detailed descriptions):

You don't roll for Ambush in a Melee.
A concealed unit which advances into a Melee Location will only retain concealment if not in Open Ground (A12.14).
A concealed unit in a Melee is not held in Melee as long as it remains concealed - i.e. it doesn't attack (A12.14 again).
A11.19 explains how concealed units are dealt with during CC.

Therefore, a concealed unit may wish to decline its CC attack opportunity in an effort to save its concealment. Upon losing its “?” such a unit in a Melee Location is immediately held in Melee]

ground_truth_answer:
Infantry (Defender) is concealed in a jungle hex (for instance), while an AFV (Attacker) is bypassing the hex. How does it work?  

1. Should the Defending Infantry unit take a PAATC as soon as the AFV bypasses their hex? Or is the AFV considered as occupying neither of the adjacent hexes?
2. Can an AFV OVR a concealed unit?
3. Can a bypassing AFV OVR a defending unit occupying any of the adjacent hexes?
4. Can the Defending Infantry unit CC Reaction Fire the bypassing AFV during its MPh? How does it work then? Is the CC then sequential and should the Infantry roll first? Does the defending Infantry stay in their hex afterwards, as they would in a street fight?
5. Is there any Ambush option available when a defending Infantry unit CC Reaction Fire a bypassing AFV during its MPh?

1. Not necessary unless the defender wants to CC-RF. Per A12.42 a vehicle using bypass does not force a unit in the hex to PAATC to retain concealment. See below regarding what hex the vehicle occupies.
2. A vehicle may OVR a concealed unit in general. The timing for declaring the OVR differs if all defenders are concealed [D7.1].
3. A vehicle in bypass may not OVR any hex, including its own [D7.13].
4. Yes. 

It is important to understand that a unit bypassing is actually in one of the two hexes. When there is only one hex on a hexside that the vehicle (/infantry unit) could be bypassing (i.e. one hex on the hexside has building/woods and the other doesn't have either), it's obvious which hex the bypassing unit is in. If bypass on the hexside is ambiguous the player has to declare which hex the bypassing unit is in. This is important for things like range and in this case, for whether the vehicle can be attacked in bypass. If the vehicle is bypassing in the hex with defending infantry, they can potentially CC-RF. If the vehicle has a choice of which hex to bypass and is bypassing the other one, the defending unit may not attack [EXC: village streets, B31.132]. The infantry have to pass a PAATC, and if they do they attack on using CC. They get the "street-fighting ambush DRM" for bypass even though it isn't street fighting. When using CC against a vehicle in bypass infantry do not move to the hexside; they remain as they were. During the MPh the vehicle cannot return the CC attack. Only the CC-RF unit attacks.

5. Not during the MPh, but against a bypassing unit an infantry unit gets the "street-fighting ambush" DRM [A11.8].

One additional thing to note: if the vehicle ends its MPh in bypass the units in the hex automatically lose concealment [A12.42].

query: Multi level building: When a multi level building is attacked,are all the levels attacked at once by a fire group or only one specific level?
title: Multi level building
raw_question: When a multi level building is attacked,are all the levels attacked at once by a fire group or only one specific level?
ground_truth_answer:
Correct on Steeples, yes.

It is worth looking at A2.8 Locations: "A hex may contain separate subdivisions within itself (i.e., units may occupy the same hex but still be in separate Locations within that hex). The most common application of this is when additional vertical levels exist within the horizontal dimensions of a hex."

And A7.4 Target Determination: "Except during Defensive First Fire (8.1), all the Personnel-units/unarmored-vehicles/Vulnerable-PRC in the same Location are considered targets of fire that does not have to specify a particular target, with the outcome of such fire affecting all those enemy (or Melee) units in the target Location (except those to which the LOF is blocked, such as being entrenched behind a wall [B9.21], Area Target Type [C3.33], or non-Crest units in a Depression [B20.92])."

So the target of of a fire attack will be one Location in a hex (which could be the only Location in the hex...). DFF of course only affects the moving units in a Location. ATT generally hits all Locations in a hex, Spraying Fire can affect two adjacent Locations, OBA usually affects all Locations in a group of seven hexes... and the extra fun one is canister shot, which can affect three locations—usually a group of ground level ones, but can be three levels within one hex.

We are playing Scouts Out scenario in ASL Journal 1.  Lines 522-524 show a critical hit and multiple hits occurring together.  Any help appreciated.
ground_truth_answer:
e.g. his Panther rolled snake eyes on the To Hit roll vs the "Motion" TD... even with Motion, would have still been a hit, I believe...just not a critical

If the TH DRM mean that only a TH DR of two will hit, then after rolling a TH DR of two you roll a subsequent dr. On a dr of one, it's a Critical Hit. On a dr of two or higher it's a normal hit [C3.7]. This does not have a name.

If the TH DRM mean that even a TH DR of two is not ≤ the modified TH DR, a TH DR of two is an Improbable Hit [C3.6]. On a subsequent dr of one it's a Critical Hit, two or three is a normal hit and four or higher is a miss.

So it's always possible to get a Critical Hit on the Vehicle Target Type, but sometimes it requires a subsequent dr.

title: Intensive Fire
raw_question:
In our latest game session on VASL we had some uncertainty about Intensive Fire.
As I've understood you can only use it after your ROF has been used up as a kind of final additional shot you get once per player turn with penalties.
In which Fire Phases can it be used then? 
As I think:
-Defensive Fire Phase: 
1)First Fire: possible after ROF has been used up. 
2)Subsequent and Final Protective Fire: not possible since this is an ordnance weapon (AT gun) which doesn't have IFE.
3)Final Fire: possible or not? I should say only if it didn't First Fire and only started to fire in the Final Fire segment? Is that correct? And only after ROF has been used up? I suppose it only gets a Final Fire counter after it First Fired? Not if it didn't?

-Advance Fire Phase: only possible if it was marked as an Opportunity Firer according to the rules.

-Prepare Fire Phase: not mentioned in the rules but I should say possible since it can do it in the Advance Fire Phase as an Opportunity Firer?
ground_truth_answer:
Intensive Fire is allowed during the enemy MPh with penalties but no range limitations. In contrast SFF & FPF have limitations on range, e.g. within normal range, not when there is a closer known enemy unit for SFF, and adjacent only for FPF. You are correct that SFF & FPF can't be used by Ordnance attacks, i.e. attacks involving a TH DR. 

During the Defensive Fire Phase per A8.4, "Any such units/weapons that are marked with a First Fire counter may also fire again (by flipping their First Fire marker over to the Final Fire side) ... only at units in an adjacent (or same) hex." During DFPh there *is* a range limitation to Intensive Fire, i.e. only against adjacent units. Also during the DFPh if a weapon is not marked with a First Fire counter, it can attack until it loses ROF at which point it is marked with a *Final* Fire counter [A3.4], i.e. a weapon can't make both normal attacks and Intensive Fire attacks in the DFPh.

As you note during the AFPh only if using Opportunity Fire. There is no range limit.

During Prep Fire it is allowed with penalties but without range limitations.

ground_truth_answer:
The PF has a maximum range that changes by scenario date, starting at one hex prior to June 1944, increasing to two hexes through the rest of 1944 and becoming three hexes in 1945 [C13.32]. Scouts Out takes place on 19 November, 1944, in the two-hex range phase.

It would surprise me if anyone took a PF shot at range five. I will speculate the attack is not against AC-E but against AC-C instead. That would be within range and LOS. The DRM would be +2 Case J moving target, +1 small, +1 height advantage, +2 case C³ Backblast weapon in ground level building for a total +6, matching the printed value. It would be a near useless shot as the basic TH# is ten made into a modified TH# of six by the range [C13.33]. With the +6 DRM no TH DR would be ≤ the modified TH# so only a snakeeyes followed by a dr 1-3 would be an improbable hit [C3.6].

Now, about Kevin's reasoning :
So if they were concealed in HiP, they remain concealed... if not concealed in HiP, they remain not concealed.

I have thought a bit more about the formulae, and they are not wrong (once you understand that there are two formulae). But I find those two unintuitive and hard to understand from the rules, as I said. The problem starts with the expression of "2*obstacle height". Where does that "2" come from? The answer is that the formulae use absolute heights, e.g. a case where a unit at level two firing at a target at level zero over a level one obstacle has different parameters than a case with a unit at level three firing a target at level one over a level two obstacle, so you subtract the obstacle height out once to get into relative units.. This misses the commonality that if the observer is two levels above the target and the obstacle is one level above the target the number of blind hexes will be the same (for same range and type of obstacle) regardless of whether the target is at level -1, 0, 1, 2 .... It's the relative heights that matter. I find that a lot more satisfying and it's fairly close to what the rules say and it's actually quick to calculate using the steps I gave.

query: Entering WP Location: do take precedence rule A 24.31 ( no NMC ) OR C 1.51 ( yes NMC ) ? Or there is something I've missed ? many thanks
title: Entering WP Location
raw_question: do take precedence rule A 24.31 ( no NMC ) OR C 1.51 ( yes NMC ) ? Or there is something I've missed ? many thanks
ground_truth_answer:
What amazes me is how people like JR V, Robin, Bruce, etc. have somehow internalized all these rules that they can answer these questions with such nuanced accuracy without spending 45 hours combing through the rules to find all the possible exceptions (and the exceptions to the exceptions... and the exceptions to the exceptions to the ... well, you get it 🙂 ).
In this particular case it's helpful to understand how WP causes casualties. Although it produces unpleasant fumes, they are not so noxious that you will fall over gasping (unless in a very confined space). When a WP shell explodes, it spreads many small particles of phosphorus everywhere. If any of these come in contact with flesh, it causes a very painful burn, and the particles will continue to burn and are hard to extinguish. There's an episode of M*A*S*H where the doctors dig a piece of white phosphorus out of a wounded soldier. It looks very unpleasant. After the initial explosion the WP continues to generate smoke but it would be hard to become injured by it unless you rolled over a piece of it or picked it up or something. Hence when the WP counter is placed there's some chance of injury, but after that there isn't. Except in the case of OBA where there is assumed to be a continuous rain of shells. Note that this is actually pretty much the same as HE. When you are done your shooting, other units can move through that Location without effect (EXC: residual FP), and again an exception for an HE FFE.

One thing to thing consider about ASL the game vs. the simulation is that if you have an on-board gun and you fire at a target PFPh & DFPh turn after turn, you are more-or-less doing the same thing as OBA, but the two behave very differently in terms of stopping movement through the Location.

ground_truth_answer:
Regarding Depletion Numbers. How to use them actually? The rule mentions the "original" TH DR? How to understand "Original"? The first one being rolled? The unmodified roll (no DRM involved)? Or am I just overthinking the matter?
Should the very first TH DR being rolled determine if the special ammo is available for the whole scenario (or not)?
Or should the Depletion Number be considered each time a new TH DR is being rolled? And the special ammo would be available until rolling higher than the Depletion Number?

Per the Index, "Original DR/dr: a DR/dr prior to any applicable modification by DRM/drm of any kind."

For Depletion Numbers, per C8.9 "the firer announces his intention to use Special Ammunition prior to a To Hit DR." If the TH DR is < the Depletion #, that attack uses the depletable ammo and the weapon has more of it. If the TH DR is == the Depletion #, that attack uses the depletable, but the weapon has run out. It can't attempt to use that particular type of ammunition. If the TH DR is > the Depletion # that weapon does not have that type of ammo and the attack is not considered to have happened (EXC: Low Ammo, Malfunction). Note that for a HIP weapon, announce the shot and make the TH DR *before* putting the weapon on board. If the weapon does not have the Ammunition it remains HIP, and it's kind of a bummer to spoil the HIP position if you don't have the ammo.

LATW firing options: Can't LATW ever fire more than once per turn? They can't obviously Subsequent First Fire (as they aren't MG) nor Intensive Fire (only ordnances seem to be allowed to). So my guess is they can only be fired once per turn.

Are they marked with a First Fire counter when used during an enemy MPh?
title: LATW firing options
raw_question:
Can't LATW ever fire more than once per turn? They can't obviously Subsequent First Fire (as they aren't MG) nor Intensive Fire (only ordnances seem to be allowed to). So my guess is they can only be fired once per turn.

ground_truth_answer:
Can't LATW ever fire more than once per turn? They can't obviously Subsequent First Fire (as they aren't MG) nor Intensive Fire (only ordnances seem to be allowed to). So my guess is they can only be fired once per turn.

Are they marked with a First Fire counter when used during an enemy MPh?

Some LATW have ROF, for example the Japanese 20L ATR. Otherwise LATW can't fire more than once. As you say they can't use SFF/FPF because they are not MGs. But LATW, even ones with their own TH table (e.g. BAZ, PF) *are* ordnance. Per the Index, "Ordnance (any weapon which must score a hit on a To Hit Table before rolling again on the IFT or To Kill Table to resolve that hit)." Per C5.6, "Intensive Fire is available only to Guns (not SW)."

There is one additional time SW can fire more than once without ROF, FPF non-CC Reaction Fire [D7.221]. A SW that is subject to OVRs can fire as long as its owner passes the FPF MC.

Once they fire they can be marked with a First Fire counter. If the unit holding the weapon is a squad it can still fire its inherent FP (or another SW) as First Fire. Once the unit holding a SW is marked with Final Fire, all of its possessed weapons are also marked as Final Fire.

Certain LATW have ROF, in particular for ASLSK the Japanese 20L ATR that comes in ASLSK#4. But as you point out they can't use SFF/FPF as they are not MGs. LATW, even ones with their own TH table (BAZ, PF, etc.), *are* Ordnance (in general, but ATRs vs. infantry). Per the 2.0 definitions, "Ordnance: A Gun, SW (Mortar or LATW), or vehicle MA that must first secure a hit via the To Hit process prior to resolving an attack via the IFT (6.0) against Infantry or prior to the To Kill process against a vehicle (7.9)," and also 4.4, "LATWs are Ordnance SW." They can't use Intensive Fire because, per the 2.0 definitions, "Intensive Fire: After losing ROF a Gun or vehicle MA may make one final attack (3.2.4)," and "Gun: Any non-vehicular Weapon on a 5⁄8˝ counter." LATW are on ½-inch counters and so cannot use Intensive Fire.

Note that ATRs that aren't 20mm weapons (i.e. most ATRs) can't fire at infantry using TH/TK; they instead fire using their one FP directly on the IFT (4.4.4).

query:
When do you mark a Gun Prep Fire?: Ok, ok ... its not just "In the Prep Fire Phase" 🙂 .  The question is as follows:

We have a US Lt MTR that wants to fire WP (1945). It needs a 5 or less to secure a hit due to Hindrance, range, etc. and has a WP7 number, with a ROF of 3.  It rolls a '2' (colored die) + '5', meaning it had WP, but failed to secure a hit, but also kept ROF.  If no other unit wanted to fire SMOKE, this would be all fine and dandy, we would just keep firing the Lt MTR until it lost ROF and we would mark it with a Prep Fire counter then.

But we have other Guns that want to attempt to fire SMOKE.  Looking at the ROF rules in both A and C, we saw nothing that prevented us from swapping over to other Guns/Lt MTRs to fire SMOKE, then coming back to the first Lt MTR to fire HE.  We did believe that if we chose to have the Lt MTR /not/ fire HE, it would still be marked Prep Fire (as it had successfully attempted to fire WP), even though it did not lose ROF.  

Q) Is this correct?  That one can fire a weapon during a phase, NOT mark it as fired in that phase if it kept ROF, fire other units/weapons, and then come back to that first weapon to finish up its firing (or just to mark it as fully fired)?  Or must the unit/weapon be immediately marked Prep Fire after it has fired at least once, even if it has not exhausted its ROF at that point?

Rules we felt were involved:
A3.2 (Place a Prep Fire counter on those units which fire);

A9.2 (If that colored dr is ≤ the MG’s applicable ROF, the MG retains its Multiple ROF and may be fired again during that phase (A.15). ... Once a MG has lost its Multiple ROF, it is marked with an appropriate Prep, First or Final Fire counter.); and

C2.24 (However, a number encased in a square on the counter indicates a Multiple ROF equal to that number, thus conceivably allowing it (and certain ordnance SW such as light mortars and some ATR, as well as MG making TH DR) to fire many times during a Player Turn. If the Original colored dr of its TH (or IFE IFT) DR is ≤ its ROF, that weapon may fire again during that Player Turn unless otherwise prohibited. If the Original colored dr of the TH (or IFE IFT) DR is > the firing weapon’s ROF, it is marked with an appropriate fire counter (Prep, First Fire, etc.) and may fire no more in that Player Turn (EXC: Sustained/Intensive Fire if so allowed).)

This is independent of ROF when that is applicable. For instance in the enemy MPh if an enemy unit spent two MF entering a Location, a DEFENDER could fire on it once then another DEFENDER could fire on the enemy unit once then the first DEFENDER could fire again (as ROF, SFF or FPF) then the second DEFENDER could fire again (as ROF, SFF or FPF). Or the first DEFENDER unit could fire twice then the second DEFENDER unit fire twice, or the first DEFENDER unit could fire once then the second DEFENDER unit could fire twice then the first DEFENDER unit could fire again.

Per A3.2 units that fire in the PFPh are marked with a Prep Fire counter. There are other places where you can also determine that units that fired in the PFPh cannot move or fire in the AFPh even if they kept ROF, but A3.2 is the simplest.
