Fellow ASL'ers

I have a bad memory ... please help ...

An AFV fires (DFF ) it's cmg at moving Infantry a few hexes away .. VCA/TCA identical 
Q1: does this lock the TCA for the MA firing later in the same DFF Ph ?
Q2: Vice-versa if MA fires first then cmg separate target ?

ground_truth_answer:
As per previous answers, if there is a Known target (and there are no terrain restrictions), no. In your case the target might be Known or not. Firing at a target where there is no Known Enemy unit *does* lock the CA. This is because of some "sleaze" you can perform here. The TCA (VCA) change DRM for a particular shot does *not* "remember" and accumulate with previous TCA (VCA) changes [D3.51].

So for instance assume there is a unit that you really want to take a shot at (with CMG or MA) but currently you have to change TCA three hexspines to get the desired target in CA. You can change CA two hexspines and take a shot at a KEU using the weapon you don't want to use, then take a shot with a one hexspine change at the target you really want to attack. The CA change DRM for the second TCA change is only the cost of one hexspine, i.e. the previous two hexspine TCA change is "forgotten". But if the target of the first TCA change attack is not Known, the TCA is frozen. This reduces the opportunity for sleaze somewhat, even if it doesn't eliminate it.

As a follow-on, you can't use this trick using a mix of the VCA and the TCA. While a second TCA change makes the unit forget its first *TCA* change, a mix of VCA and TCA changes are cumulative. Only the most recent TCA and VCA change as above, but that is usually enough to make it not especially good to mix them.

query: My AFV can be Moving Target on my turn but need not be on Opponents?: Am I right that, despite player turns being simultaneous, an AFV that starts my turn Stopped, moves to new hexes, then stops is a Moving Target on my turn but when we flip to my Opponent's turn the AFV is no longer considered a Moving Target? I can't find anything in C.8 that contradicts this.
title: My AFV can be Moving Target on my turn but need not be on Opponents?
raw_question: Am I right that, despite player turns being simultaneous, an AFV that starts my turn Stopped, moves to new hexes, then stops is a Moving Target on my turn but when we flip to my Opponent's turn the AFV is no longer considered a Moving Target? I can't find anything in C.8 that contradicts this.
ground_truth_answer:
Having thought about this some more, I think the friendly player turn may comprise more "actual time" of the friendly player's forces than the enemy player turn. All of movement is stuffed into the friendly player turn along with most of the "serious" attacks (the PFPh). Although the player can also use the DFPh for "serious" attacks, skulking makes it definitely the second-best for such attacks. So if a Game Turn notionally represents two minutes of "real time", perhaps 90 seconds of that "real time" is spent in the friendly player turn and 30 seconds in the enemy player turn. As far as "game time" is concerned a friendly player turn is just as long as an enemy player turn, but they map to different amounts of "real time". The friendly player turn has all the friendly actions that are performed not in reaction to the enemy force's activities, and the enemy player turn has all the actions that are primarily in reaction to the enemy force's activities.

I don't mean the numbers or ratio given, 90 seconds:30 seconds, to be a scientific statement. The ratio may vary depending on circumstances. For instance if a scenario has two sides move onto the board in such a way that they don't gain LOS to each other the first Game Turn, the friendly player turn may represent 100% of the actual time and the enemy player turn 0%. What I am suggesting is that more of the "real time" for the friendly player may be spent in the friendly player turn, i.e. that each side's experience of "real time" is not 50:50 between the two player turns of a game turn.

query:
Bocage B9.53 - AA Gun CA change: Review the attached image. Q: Russian MPh, Can the AA Gun first fire at the Russian AFV in L2, maintain ROF and then change CA and fire at the 2nd Russian AFV in H4 through the Bocage? Clarify specific aspects of the rule about a Non-Vehicle Gun changing CA when firing through Bocage.

The first attack is irrelevant. B9.53 "A non-vehicular Direct-Fire Gun may not both change CA and fire through a bocage hexside in the same fire phase (counting Defensive First Fire and Final Fire as one phase—A.15)." The Gun may not both change its CA and fire through the I4-J3 hexside, assuming hedges are Bocage. It could not make the attack if that were the only attack it wanted to make.
title: Bocage B9.53 - AA Gun CA change
raw_question:
Review the attached image. Q: Russian MPh, Can the AA Gun first fire at the Russian AFV in L2, maintain ROF and then change CA and fire at the 2nd Russian AFV in H4 through the Bocage? Clarify specific aspects of the rule about a Non-Vehicle Gun changing CA when firing through Bocage.

The first attack is irrelevant. B9.53 "A non-vehicular Direct-Fire Gun may not both change CA and fire through a bocage hexside in the same fire phase (counting Defensive First Fire and Final Fire as one phase—A.15)." The Gun may not both change its CA and fire through the I4-J3 hexside, assuming hedges are Bocage. It could not make the attack if that were the only attack it wanted to make.
ground_truth_answer:
Why is the First Fire Irrelevant? Does the Rule prohibit the AA Gun from making the second shot even if it retained ROF? It could make the First Fire shot and if retained ROF, it still could change CA and fire at another target just not through the Bocage hexside, correct or no? It would seem to me, if a turret on a AFV can change CA and fire through the Bocage, how is that different from an AA Gun?

The Gun could change CA and fire at a target as long as it does not fire through a Bocage hexside, whether the attack is a first DFF attack, an attack after retaining ROF, a Sustained or Intensive Fire attack, or even an OVR Prevention attack. It could turn its CA from K2 to L3 and, say, fire on L3 or K4. I believe it could even turn its CA to H3 (an "unnecessary" extra hexspine) and fire to H2 as long as walls are not Bocage in the scenario. Note that the Gun could not change CA during the enemy MPh in response to movement in H4 because any change of CA during the enemy MPh would have to be part of an attack. The Gun would have to wait until the DFPh and use a "free" CA change to turn toward H4 (unless it found a reason to change CA to fire in that direction where it did not fire through a Bocage hexside).

You would have to speak to the rule designer to get an authoritative reason why this is so for Bocage. My made-up, how-would-this-work-in-a-ww-ii-movie explanation is that when firing through Bocage "changing CA" actually requires some physical translation of the gun, i.e. it is not pure rotation. A vehicle can perform this in-hex translation quickly enough in game terms to be allowed to both change CA and attack. A non-vehicular gun isn't quick enough. It would be like taking a 32-pound gun from a broadside gun port of HMS Victory and moving it to a bow chaser port. It can be done but it would take a while. But that is 100% guess and worth exactly what you paid for it. What ever the reason, the rule is clear. If the hexside is hedge, you can change CA and fire through it. When it is Bocage and you have a non-vehicular Gun, you can't.

query:
Overrunning a Gun: Continuing from my previous post about thinking about VBM freeze of a HMG, we instead chose to have the T-34 M41 overrun a 75* Italian ART that was peppering some of our troops.

Tank B moved up the BB row and overran the gun in BB1.  Our understanding of the way this worked was as follows:
1) Tank B expends a MP to start and rolls for mechanical reliability (not a 12). ART takes a shot at deliberate immobilization on Tank B and fails to achieve a Hull Hit (our understanding is that one needs a Hull Hit and applies the +5 DRM to the To Hit roll). The gun is marked First Fire.
2) The tank precedes to move up to BB10, then enters BB1 declaring an overrun.  The MP expenditure so far is 1 (start) +3 (move to BB10) +5 (cost to enter BB1) +5 (OVR cost) = 14 MPs.
3) Upon entering the hex, the Gun can declare either CC Reaction Fire by the crew alone or Non-CC Reaction Fire by firing the Gun.  This is where we were a bit unsure of things ... we resolved the Non-CC Reaction Fire /before/ the OVR (no effect) and marked the Gun with an Intensive Fire counter.  We then resolved the OVR at 13 FP (6 MG x3/2 = 9 + 4 for base), with a +2 TEM for emplacement in the out of season orchard.  We only ended up Pinning the crew.  The tank is then marked with a Bounding Fire counter (so cannot fire again).
4) We then spent 1 MP to rotate CA and exited to hex CC2, where we spent our last MP to change CA to face the AT Gun (turret facing both AT and ART), staying in Motion.

The plan is to then OVR either the AT Gun or ART (there is another 75* gun behind the AT gun, now in hex AA4).  Should we OVR the AT Gun, the way it would work would be:
1) enter BB2 for 10 MPs (5 + 5 for OVR) and resolve OVR at 12 FP +1 (+2 for Emplacement; -1 for FFMO).  Hopefully survive CC Non-Reaction Fire (AT Gun is pointed facing Z2 now, if that matters)
2) enter AA3 for 1 MP (11 total)
3) enter and OVR AA4 for 6 MPs (1 + 5 for OVR) (17 MPs total) and resolve OVR at 12 FP -1 (open ground, gun no longer emplaced).
4) end in Motion in AA4.

Alternatively, we could move to CC3 and not OVR the AT gun, and just OVR the second 75* at 12 -1, but seems like we /should/ be able to get both, right?

The big questions we had were
Q1) When exactly does a gun conduct Non-CC Reaction Fire?  Before or after the OVR is resolved in its hex?
Q2) What are the To Hit DRMs for the Gun against the tank in its hex?  Seems like Case E does not apply, so it would be pretty darn easy for the Gun to Hit, correct?
Q3) If the Gun hits, it is /always/ a rear target facing, right?
Q4) If the Gun is marked Intensive Fire and gets OVR, the crew is mandated a FPF CC Reaction Fire (and corresponding NMC with same DR), correct?  So one really doesn't want to INT Fire /before/ being OVR if that is a possibility.

ground_truth_answer:
Check A12.41 and D7.1. If there are no KEU the MP to enter and OVR can't be combined. Otherwise they must be combined.

D'oh..its right there explicit in D7.1 ... I must have read right over it :(.

D7.23 is clear that is mandatory, using the provisions in C5.64. What's not clear is if C5.641 is also mandatory. If used, it uses the provisions of C5.64, but maybe the unit is not forced to do it. Maybe there's a Q&A?

D7.212 also uses the term 'must', so seems like units subject to FPF of D7.212 or manning a gun as marked in C7.23 clearly MUST do an attack after the OVR has been completed, where the attack also functions as a NMC.  If Pinned, this attack would be at -1 CCV, but would still occur.

So it sounds like the way it would work would be:
1) Gun could fire at vehicle prior to entering its hex, either keeping ROF or being marked First Fire.  Let's assume the latter.
2) When vehicle enters its hex, per C5.64 the Gun /MAY/ conduct one IF shot. This appears to be optional from my reading of C5.64 "...entitled to the possibility of one more shot..." versus the use of "must" as in D7.212 and D7.23.  If taken, this shot would apply Case A and E, IF -2 DRM, be subject to random location for the hit, and be a NMC versus the crew.  If the NMC results in a Pin or Broken status, the To Hit is cancelled.  The Gun would be marked with "No Fire" (unless it was not previously marked First Fire).
3) The OVR would be resolved.
4) Then, per D7.23, the crew would make a mandatory CC FPF attack against the vehicle per D7.23; using IF if marked First Fire from the previous shot or using FPF CC Reaction Fire if marked 'No Fire'.  This shot would also function as a NMC and would be mandatory.  In our situation, the crew being Pinned from the OVR, they would be forced to make a FPF CC Reaction Fire attack at -1 CCV.

What I don't get is when does D7.22 apply?

Looking at the OVR Flowchart, I follow up to 'Defensive Fire Options Before OVR', where the Gun heading has superscripts d,i,o; with o seeming to indicate that this TH DR always functions as a NMC for the crew due to OVR prevention/Non-CC Reaction Fire (pointing to C5.64 and D7.23).

We then resolve and go to "Defensive Fire Options After OVR: (Reaction Fire)".  Gun has superscripts e and n.  So THIS seems to point to D7.22, noting that Rear Target Facing always applies (and mentions not using Cases A and E in the other superscript).  From the chart, if the Gun is unmarked (which would occur, I suppose, if ROF was kept during the first Non-CC Reaction Fire), this occurs as regular Non-CC Reaction Fire per D7.22.

If the Gun was marked First Fired, 'l, m, o' all apply, which is mandatory FPF effects.
If the Gun was marked Final or IF, then the 'l,m' still applies, but the crew must make a CC Reaction Fire attack (i.e. can't use the Gun).
If the Gun is Pinned, it depends whether it needs to change its CA and cannot (note that, in most cases, the CA would already have changed earlier ... so what this means is that if the inability to change CA prevented DF before the OVR, it will also prevent the fire /after/ the OVR ... I think).  If it can't change CA, then the crew attacks as CC Reaction Fire.  If it can change CA, then it follows above depending on how it was marked.

Seems like only the attack AFTER the OVR is mandatory... and almost always as a FPF-type attack.

query:
Smoke options for AFVs: What are the available options for AFVs to drop Smoke (and timing)?

That's how I understand it:

1. Any ordnance (including AFVs' MA) may attempt to fire Smoke at the start of their owner's PFPh/DFPh as an Area Target Fire. A full +3 5/8" Smoke counter is to be placed if fired during the PFPh. A dispersed +2 5/8" Smoke counter is to be placed if fired during the DFPh. 

2. An AFV may attempt to drop Smoke during its MPh, according to the Vehicular Smoke Dispenser capability available on the back of its counter (each following a specific set of rules regarding placement). A successful DR is to be rolled (with a +1 DRM if BU). A dispersed +2 5/8" Smoke counter is to be placed if successful.

3. What about Smoke Grenades? Smoke placement may be attempted via inherent SMOKE grenades by any Infantry squad having a SMOKE Placement Exponent and still capable of movement during its MPh at a cost of two MF if the attempt is to place SMOKE in an ADJACENT Location, or one MF if the attempt is to place SMOKE in its own Location. Can AFVs drop 1/2" Smoke counters that way? Is it how a "s8" info on the back of an AFV counter is supposed to be understood for instance?

2. An AFV may attempt to drop Smoke during its MPh, according to the Vehicular Smoke Dispenser capability available on the back of its counter (each following a specific set of rules regarding placement). Can AFVs drop 1/2" Smoke counters that way? Is it how a "s8" info on the back of an AFV counter is supposed to be understood for instance?
ground_truth_answer:
1.

There is also WP ammo. WP can be placed in any fire phase, which means it can fire in the AFPh too. It can also be fired as DFF per a q&a as long as there has been no regular DFF yet.

Provided the AFV is WP "capable" I guess.

It has to have a "WP" depletion number, just like a weapon firing Smoke has to have a "s" depletion number. The Americans preferred WP over Smoke. The Japanese used it too. 

2.

The "s8" and similar (e.g. WP9) are standard depletion numbers for the MA Smoke ammunition [C8.5]. You will find numbers like "s8" on the back of ordnance too. 

That's the depletion number one would use when rolling their TH attempt (Area Target Type), right? 

Correct. Standard use of special ammo depletion .

3.

Smoke grenades are assumed inherent in all AFVs per D13.35. Since the usage drs are the same for all vehicles, it was not put on the counter. The usage is mostly similar to other smoke dispensers. A vehicle can use a smoke dispenser or smoke grenades but not both.
From the rulebook A 24.1 : The Smoke Placement Exponent is the numerical exponent of a squad's FP rating and is the highest number the unit can roll with one die and still place Smoke during that Player Turn.

Where to find the Smoke Placement Exponent on an AFV counter? Where to find that info? In chapter H?
Do AFV drop Smoke grenades exactly the same way Infantry would, ie spending MP and targeting their hex or any adjacent one then rolling a single die once per turn?

The Vehicular Smoke Grenade rules are covered in D13.35. There is no indication for them on the counter or mention in chapter H. They do cost a MP but unlike Infantry Smoke Grenades the MP is spent only if the Smoke is placed. They can' t be placed in an adjacent hex only in the vehicle's.

4.
5/8” Smoke Counters are flipped/ removed at the start of the next friendly PFPh phase.
1/2” Smoke Counters are removed at the end of the current MPh.
Correct?

Correct, and per my previous reply this might be good or bad. If you want to do some fire in the AFPh having the Smoke go away quickly is a good thing.

query:
ROF, follow-up attacks, and broken units: We had a situation where a moving unit expended 1 MF and was fired on by a MG (dashing across a road).  The MG kept ROF and the unit broke in the road.  We knew that they no longer get the dash benefits, but what confused us was the language in A8.14.

8.14 FOLLOW-UP ATTACK: A unit broken or pinned by Defensive First
Fire can be fired on again in its current Location by other same-phase De-
fensive First Fire attacks, but is attacked in its broken or pinned state. A unit
that survives a Defensive First Fire attack with no effect can be fired on again
in that same Location during its MPh before expending additional MF/MP,
but only by different attackers or if it expended at least two MF/MP in that 
Location (see 9.2). A moving unit subject to FFNAM/FFMO which breaks 
is still subject to those DRM in that Location for subsequent Defensive First 
Fire attacks until its MPh ends, even if previously pinned (see 4.61 for As-
sault Movement).

Specifically, the use of two different qualifiers when talking about units that were broken and those that were not (red vs blue).  9.2 is the ROF section, which makes sense for the non-broken units.

Our understanding was that since the MG would still be making a Defensive Fire Fire attack (as it had maintained rate), it could fire on the broken unit in the road, at the -2 FFMO/FFNAM and without halving for dash.  Just wanted to make sure we interpreted this correctly.

In other words, does the J2 DRM (Defensive First Fire vs Moving Vehicular Target; <1 MP in firer's LOS) automatically add up to the change of CA DRM when firing at a moving enemy vehicle (hence a +4 DRM, to be added to the already painful change of CA DRM)?

In other words, does the J2 DRM (Defensive First Fire vs Moving Vehicular Target; <1 MP in firer's LOS) automatically add up to the change of CA DRM when firing at a moving enemy vehicle (hence a +4 DRM, to be added to the already painful change of CA DRM)?
ground_truth_answer:
Is a GUN CA change supposed to occur right before the shot? In other words, does the J2 DRM (Defensive First Fire vs Moving Vehicular Target; <1 MP in firer's LOS) automatically add up to the change of CA DRM when firing at a moving enemy vehicle (hence a +4 DRM, to be added to the already painful change of CA DRM)? 

Not 100% sure what you are asking here. Guns can change their CA as part of an attack (unless using Bounding First Fire). If a Gun does so, the Case A DRM applies. Say a vehicle starts the MPh in Motion and also in LOS. It enters a hex that requires a one hexspine CA change for a NT Gun. The TH DRM would be +3 case A change CA &+2 case J Moving Target.

If the vehicle entered LOS from out-of-LOS (e.g. it entered from off board), the DRMs would be +3 case A change CA, +2 case J Moving Target and Case J² ≤ 1 MP in LOS.

Note that "limited time in LOS" DRMs (J¹ & J²) do not apply if the vehicle started the MPh in LOS and has not left LOS. They only apply when the moving vehicle either moves out of LOS then back in or starts its MPh out of and enters LOS.

Note also that case J Moving Target DRM does not apply unless the vehicle either begins its MPh in Motion or has entered a new hex. If in the EX above the vehicle had started the MPh Stopped and then expended one MP (even to start), the DRM would be +3 case A change CA. The +2 Case J Moving Target would not apply (yet, until it entered a new hex).

ground_truth_answer:
From D 5.6 CREW SURVIVAL (CS) 
How can a crew possibly become broken? There is no such result following a collateral damage (general or specific) suffered by an AFV CE. As far as I know. Maybe with unarmored vehicle, or OT? 

In certain circumstances inherent crews are more vulnerable than normal. In those circumstances inherent crew suffers results as if Personnel and not as inherent crew, i.e. KIA, K/#, MC with break, etc.

D5.311 "The Inherent crew (as well as each Passenger) of a vehicle receiving fire (including Fire Lane Residual FP) [EXC: Sniper attack] through an unarmored Target Facing/Aspect (C3.9; including any OT AFV receiving either Air Bursts or fire from a higher elevation whose elevation advantage is > the range [5.31]—and, vs mines, the PRC of any AFV with a hull AF of 0 [B28.43]) is Vulnerable even if BU, and receives no (or a reduced; 5.31) CE DRM. Consequently the crew is not susceptible to Stun/Recall from such an attack; it is instead subject to PTC/MC/K/KIA results."

Unarmored vehicle crews always take attacks as if Personnel. OT vehicles do in special circumstances, i.e. when receiving air bursts or attacked when range < elevation advantage. The other two exceptions are very rare in my experience, although partially armored vehicles show up in valor of the guards, so if you play that a lot you might have a different experience.

title: Placed DC attack vs entrenchment/pillbox that are beneath wire
ground_truth_answer:
You raise some interesting issues. The first thing you have missed is B30.2, "Units in an adjacent, ground-level Location within a pillbox's CA are treated as being ADJACENT to units in the pillbox (and vice versa) for purposes of Point Blank Fire, FPF, DM, rout, and for DC Placement vs the pillbox.." There is also a q&a:
"A23.3, B26., & B30. Can a same level unit, in an adjacent ground level hex place a DC which will affect the occupants of a pillbox if the pillbox hex also contains a wire fortification?
A. Yes, essentially ignore the Wire."
There is another q&a:
"A23.3 & B30.4 Does a unit trying to Place a DC against a pillbox have to pay the extra 1 MF for pillbox entry?
A. No."

My understanding of how DC placement is commonly played against pillboxes is that the unit has to be ADJACENT to the Location the pillbox is in, not to the pillbox Location itself. The placing unit pays the cost to enter that Location containing the pillbox as if it were placing the DC in that containing Location but the pillbox Location is attacked instead of the Location the pillbox is in. The placing unit might instead choose to attack the containing Location, at the same MF cost, in which case the pillbox and its contents are not attacked. The pillbox is treated as if it were a special unit in its containing Location and attacked similar to how an AFV is attacked by a placed DC.

On more careful reading of the rules I would have to say the way DC placement against pillboxes is commonly played does not seem to match what is written in the rules, even beyond your questions about wire.

First a placing unit in the NCA of a pillbox is not ADJACENT to that pillbox Location, ignoring Bunkers. That should mean that the DC can't be placed (or thrown) against the pillbox Location from an adjacent hex. However B30.31 says, "If Placed/Thrown from any other adjacent hex it is modified by the NCA Defense Modification," suggesting (but not saying) that a pillbox can have a DC placed/thrown against it from an adjacent hex even though the pillbox Location is not ADJACENT. This is in line with my understanding of how pillboxes work with DCs, i.e. that in order to attack the pillbox you have to be ADJACENT to the Location the pillbox is in even if you are not ADJACENT to the actual pillbox Location. The two q&a also seem to fit with my understanding of how DCs work against pillboxes.

Second per A23.3, "A unit may not Place (or Throw; 23.6) a DC to an adjacent Location out of its LOS (7.21)." Per B30.6, "LOS from inside a pillbox may be traced only within its CA [EXC: the pillbox Location and the same-level Location outside the pillbox are ADJACENT; 30.6].." So this too would suggest that a DC can't be placed in the pillbox Location from an adjacent NCA hex.

I will fully acknowledge that it would be difficult to arrive at my understanding from the rules as written, unless I have missed some rule. Still I believe it is how DCs are intended to be played. I would be very glad if you sent in for a q&a because I would like to see the questions about the attacks from the NCA answered. I believe that B30.2 resolves the question for DC attacks from the CA, and the q&a above also answers your question about the effects of wire.

Small Arms Fire and MG vs AFV CE: 1. How to resolve a Squad's (for instance) Small Arms Fire attack directed towards the CE (Crew Exposed) of an AFV (Armored Fighting Vehicle)?
1.1 Necessarily as a collateral attack? Hence there's no way to kill (reduce) a CE with a Small Arms attack, only Stun/STUN them?
1.2 As any other Small Arms Fire attack directed against any Infantry Unit on the battlefield, resolved on the IFT, and applying KIA, K/#, MC results as normal?

2. What if the Squad was handling a MG? Should the MG attack be resolved first against the vehicle (To Hit procedure and TK number), then resolve a collateral attack against the CE using the same DR result and the MG IFP? What about the squad IFP then?

3. Is there any other DRM than the "inherent" +2 from "sitting" in the AFV (or the Hex TEM, whichever the better) when targeting a CE with a Collateral Attack?
title: Small Arms Fire and MG vs AFV CE
raw_question:
1. How to resolve a Squad's (for instance) Small Arms Fire attack directed towards the CE (Crew Exposed) of an AFV (Armored Fighting Vehicle)?
1.1 Necessarily as a collateral attack? Hence there's no way to kill (reduce) a CE with a Small Arms attack, only Stun/STUN them?
1.2 As any other Small Arms Fire attack directed against any Infantry Unit on the battlefield, resolved on the IFT, and applying KIA, K/#, MC results as normal?

2. What if the Squad was handling a MG? Should the MG attack be resolved first against the vehicle (To Hit procedure and TK number), then resolve a collateral attack against the CE using the same DR result and the MG IFP? What about the squad IFP then?

3. Is there any other DRM than the "inherent" +2 from "sitting" in the AFV (or the Hex TEM, whichever the better) when targeting a CE with a Collateral Attack?
ground_truth_answer:
Per A7.307, "Small Arms and non-ordnance attacks [EXC: FT, DC, MOL, ATMM] have no effect vs armored targets but may leave Residual FP. Any Vulnerable PRC in or on such vehicles are affected normally as Personnel". "PRC" are "Passengers, Riders and Crew". Thus Small Arms will not (in general) affect an AFV directly, i.e. there is no way for such weaponry to turn an AFV into a wreck. The second sentence does not say that the crew are "attacked collaterally," but that is what is meant. For Small Arms the attack is a General Collateral Attack, and other eligible soft targets would also be attacked. As mentioned above the collateral attack vs the CE crew will affect the behavior of the vehicle game piece, i.e. it may Stun/STUN the inherent vehicle crew, which affects the performance of vehicle. But such a result does not affect the vehicle itself, e.g. if a Stunned crew were to abandon the AFV and a non-Stunned crew were to re-man it, the vehicle would perform with no impairments.

While inherent the crew is affected by attacks per D5.34 and following, i.e. there is no way normally to KIA an inherent crew in the same way as an Infantry unit. The inherent crew continues to exist even after a K/# or KIA result is applied to it. This also applies to temporary crews, i.e. it is not just caused by being a 1-2-7. It is because the crew is inherent. If the inherent crew received a KIA (STUN) result, it and its vehicle would be Recalled. If it were then immobilized it would abandon the vehicle, coming out as a 1-2-7 (or if a temporary crew, whatever temporary crew got in) [D5.341].

title: Infantry vs Vehicles : A comprehensive combat procedure

ground_truth_answer:
Assuming that by "infantry fire" you mean the inherent FP of a personnel counter (Small Arms) and by "vehicle" you mean an AFV:

1. An AFV cannot by harmed by Small Arms (D1.2) and the crew of a BU AFV cannot be harmed by Small Arms

2. If the crew of a CE AFV fails a MC they are Stunned (D5.34). If they are Stunned again (i.e. they were CE in a later turn and failed another MC), they are STUNNED and the AFV must leave the map (Recall). This also happens if they were KIA/K-ed, they rolled a "12" (Casualty), MC, they were hit by a Sniper "1", etc

3 and 4. Infantry can destroy an AFV in CC if they roll less than their CCV (A11.5). If the AFV is CE, there is a -1 DRM to the attack (A11.61)

ground_truth_answer:
What my brain is having a hard time parsing is the following:  Let's say I set up the 9 MMC HiP and the other 24, one per hex.  Each of these hexes gets a free "?" counter, right?  Leaving me 33 "?" to use as fake stacks, adding to these current 24 to make them look like they are multiple MMCs, etc., right?  I don't have to use the 33 granted 'Dummy' "?" to conceal my non-HiP units.  And the free concealment applies to non-MMCs, as well; e.g. vehicles or non-AT Guns (the AT Guns getting to set up HiP for free).

Although the rules aren't especially explicit on the matter, you should consider the thirty-three "?" counters given given by E1.2 as OB-designated "?" [A12.12]. These can be placed in any Location, including Locations with real units. Once the OB-designated "?" are placed, you then place a "free" "?" on Locations *without* an OB-designated "?". OB-designated "?" cannot have a "free" "?" placed on top. As a matter of terminology, I define a dummy as a "?" that is covered by other "?" counters, while a concealment counter is a "?" that is not covered by any other "?" counters. These are non-official definitions but are useful. If you are given thirty-three E1.2 "?", you can have at most thirty-two dummies out of that (by setting them all up in one Location).

You might use E1.2 "?" on a real unit in order to puff up the stack. For example if you put a halfsquad in a Location then put three of the E1.2 "?" on top so the hex looks like it has three squads (you might use a three-squad foxhole if you have one) when in fact it has a halfsquad, two dummies and a concealment counter. You *could* put a single E1.2 "?" on a stack of real units. It would be legal but a waste of E1.2 "?" counters because at night all non-HIP units get "free" concealment.

Other units can set up concealed if not HIP. Note that *all* emplaced guns set up HIP, not just AT Guns [A12.34]. How an American M1 8-in. Howitzer could possibly be HIP is a question that is beyond the scope of ASL. By rule it can, including during daytime.

Only one radioless AFV left in a platoon: Question about platoon movement and D14.22, which says "If an AFV… uses non-platoon movement… it is no longer considered part of the Platoon… If only one AFV is remaining, it is free from platoon restrictions for the remainder of its current MPh."

Suppose I have platoon of two Stopped radioless AFVs, and it's the start of my MPh.

Before the platoon expends any MP, one of the AFV attempts an NTC by D14.23 because "it wishes to break off from its platoon".

Situation A: The NTC is successful, and the first AFV tootles off to the other side of the board using non-platoon movement. (1) Does the second AFV, now left alone, have to make a successful NTC in order to move?

ground_truth_answer:
Question about platoon movement and D14.22, which says "If an AFV… uses non-platoon movement… it is no longer considered part of the Platoon… If only one AFV is remaining, it is free from platoon restrictions for the remainder of its current MPh."

Suppose I have platoon of two Stopped radioless AFVs, and it's the start of my MPh.

Before the platoon expends any MP, one of the AFV attempts an NTC by D14.23 because "it wishes to break off from its platoon".

Situation A: The NTC is successful, and the first AFV tootles off to the other side of the board using non-platoon movement. (1) Does the second AFV, now left alone, have to make a successful NTC in order to move?

Situation B: The NTC fails, and the first AFV must Delay its remaining MPs. (2) Is the second AFV still in a platoon with the first AFV? (3) Can it move by non-platoon movement? (4) Does it have to make a successful NTC in order to do so?

In this case the platoon is not starting its MPh. Instead one of the vehicles that was part of a platoon in a previous turn starts its MPh (and ends its MPh). If the second AFV also wants to move it cannot move as part of a platoon and so must pass a NTC. But once a platoon is announced and begins its MPh, avoiding the non-platoon movement NTC, it is too late to break off.

If there had been a third tank adjacent to the second that had previously been organized in a platoon of three, those two could form a platoon, or they could try to move separately. My understanding is that a platoon is not a persistent organization. Vehicles can form and re-form platoons during each MPh without regard to previous platoons.

query:
Rarely used rules that distinguish experienced players from newer players: I've dabbled about starting a thread on this for a while, but JRVs recent post about CA changes made it jump to the forefront of my thoughts ... so here goes.

I don't consider myself an expert at ASL in any way, shape or form ... and didn't sleep in a Holiday Inn Express (for those Americans who get the commercial reference...), but recognize that there are some rules that experienced players will occasionally pull out of their bag of tricks that an 'average Joe' just wouldn't know about.

I'm trying to avoid rules that most people playing ASL would know (e.g. Fortifications can set up HiP, as well as Guns) or rules that come up very frequently (it costs 2 MPs to lay SMOKE to an adjacent hex, using special ammo to get two To Hit rolls, etc).  In no particular order, some that I can think of are:

1) Any time a non-AA weapon could fire without Intensive/Sustained Fire, one could use that opportunity to change its TCA or VCA (some restrictions apply). I've used this occasionally when I've moved a vehicle and didn't want to risk ESB to get the necessary CA changes, so I'll stop with the wrong CA and then just flip CA during the upcoming AFPh.

2) AT/INF Guns <=76mm may set up on an upper level if that level is fortified.

3) Any time there is a scenario DEFENDER (usually Night scenarios only, but occasionally other scenarios), one can use Bore Sighting.

4) Unless prohibited, if the US player has 3 M2 light mortars, they can exchange this for a special light mortar OBA module.

5) One can use Spraying Fire to place residual FP in multiple hexes.

query: Entering a pillbox hex: I can't seem to find this specifically addressed in the rules.  Can a unit MOVE into a hex containing an enemy-occupied pillbox?  I know a pillbox is a separate location, but CC is also allowed between units inside and outside the pillbox, so I'm a bit confused by this.
title: Entering a pillbox hex
raw_question: I can't seem to find this specifically addressed in the rules.  Can a unit MOVE into a hex containing an enemy-occupied pillbox?  I know a pillbox is a separate location, but CC is also allowed between units inside and outside the pillbox, so I'm a bit confused by this.
ground_truth_answer:
Yes, indeed.  But moving in via the CA of the Pillbox can be hazardous, I think subjecting you to TPBF.

A friendly unit entering via a pillbox CA hexside can be attacked by an enemy unit IN the pillbox using DFF [B30.2], but the attack uses PBF, not TPBF. In order to be eligible for TPBF the two units would have to be in the same Location, which of course they are not [B30.44].

query:
Tip: Change CA without firing: Recently an opponent changed his CA by firing his weapon at an empty hex, just for the purpose of changing CA. While the idea is sound, it is unnecessary to actually fire the weapon. Per C3.22 (and D3.51) any time a weapon is capable of firing without using Intensive Fire/Sustained Fire it can change CA at the end of a Fire Phase (but not the MPh) without firing. This has the obvious benefits of avoiding triggering a SAN as well as malfunction.

For non-vehicular Guns this is most useful to bring your CA to bear when the enemy will be approaching from a direction other than the one at which the gun is pointing. Vehicular Guns can change CA for the same reason, but less obviously they can use this rule to get "free" MPs. For instance if a vehicle is driving somewhere and knows it will need to chance CA either in this turn or the next, it can drive further forward in the current MPh and use the free change in the AFPh to change CA "for free." Obviously this does not work if the vehicle is unarmed or is armed only with a AAMG or has used BFF. When applicable it is a neat trick to squeeze an extra MP or two out of the vehicle.

Further to the above: don't let your opponent use an AAMG to get this free CA change!

D3.12 ... The TCA may change as a result of firing a turret-mounted weapon outside its current TCA and the VCA may change for firing a turret/bow-mounted weapon outside its current VCA (Case A), or at the end of any friendly fire phase in which the AFV is eligible to fire (a turret-mounted weapon for TCA or turret/bow-mounted weapon for VCA) without using Intensive Fire (as per C3.22). ...

D1.83 ... for rules purposes it is considered neither "turret-mounted" nor "bow-mounted" (3.51) ...

Also, a bow-mounted weapon that is not otherwise permitted to fire when HD (D4.223), cannot be used for the free CA change if the vehicle is currently HD across the applicable CA.

query: AFV MA and SA: Please provide an simple example of play of using the SA of a Russian T34 FT  and it's MA of how and when you can use both. Can you fire the FT and also fire the MA at the same target in a friendly fire phase or can you only fire one or the other.
title: AFV MA and SA
raw_question: Please provide an simple example of play of using the SA of a Russian T34 FT  and it's MA of how and when you can use both. Can you fire the FT and also fire the MA at the same target in a friendly fire phase or can you only fire one or the other.
ground_truth_answer: As others have said, in general the SA is treated as just another weapon in the AFV's kit, like CMG or BMG. The same standard rules apply to SA as to other weapons, so if you are using Bounding First Fire, you have to fire all weapons from the same hex (except ROF) [D3.51] and if not using BFF, all the weapons must fire in the same phase. If there are special exceptions for the behavior of SA they will be listed in the vehicle notes, so for instance with the US M3 Medium Tank and its British cousin the SA can use the vehicle's ROF instead of the MA. I don't think there is any special treatment for any bow-mounted SA FTs, but I could be wrong.

query:
Help with Crests: Background: I'm a 50+ year old gamer who started with SL back when I was around 12-15 years old. We "learned" Crests wrong way back then and have been playing them wrong for a long time (you can do the math).  Yinz have corrected us on how Crest lines work, but now I'm trying to understand how VASL is doing them and could use some commentary...

In the image above, red lines are LOS that are fine according to VASL and blue are ones that VASL indicates are blocked.  These are:
Ok LOS lines
AA4 -> FF6
DD6 -> CC6
DD6 -> BB5
BB7 -> BB6
BB7 -> Z6

Blocked LOS lines 
DD6 -> AA6
BB7 -> BB5
BB7 -> Y6

What I understand
I get the AA4 -> FF6 LOS, as the crest line in AA4 is that unit's crest line and the crest line in EE6 is within 4 hexes of the higher elevation unit, so does not generate a blind hex.

I get DD6 -> CC6 as they are adjacent across a Crest line (same for BB7 -> BB6).

I get Z6 -> BB7 since the crest line in Z6 is that unit's crest line.

What I don't quite understand 
1) Why can a unit in BB5 see DD6 but a unit in AA5 cannot?  It would seem that neither unit (BB5 nor AA5) should be able to see DD6 due to the crest line not being at a lower elevation and not being adjacent to the unit (crest line being in hex CC6).

2) Applying the above understanding, it would appear that the Y6->BB7 and BB5->BB7 LOSs would be blocked for the same reasons (the crest line is not at a lower elevation and not in the hex of the higher elevation unit).

It makes me think the VASL LOS for BB5 -> DD6 is in error, but just wanted confirmation on that (and, if not, then explanation on what I'm missing).

It seems that there are two concepts to be applied.  The 'pankcake' effect, meaning a unit not in a crest line hex only has visibility to same or higher elevations past any crest line of their same level; e.g. a unit in AA7 can only see other hexes if they are at level 1 or higher due to having no crest line in its hex.

And the newly learned "within 4 hexes" aspect of a crest line, where a LOWER LEVEL crest line does not generate a blind hex unless at 5+ hexes from the higher elevation unit.

I realize these are generalizations/simplifications, but just wanted to see if there was anything we were missing on this...

More Night Rules questions: So we started Taking the Left Tit and I /think/ we got things fairly correct.  #1 - #7 are more background, as I think we got all these correct.

1) 1st Player Turn (US), the US Player had his MTR spotters tried to dig foxholes while the MTRs were reassembled. Neither of these place Gunflash markers, even though both occur during the Prep Fire Phase.  Seems pretty obvious.

2) Rest of US Forces moved up, with 3 Straying due to 6 on colored die and 3-6 on white. Straying fairly inconsequential due to direction rolls and no doubles, though. At one point the US player spent extra MFs moving along a road so that when the unit first left the adjacency of the road, they'd have less MFs available should they stray (to avoid entering NVR of nearby Germans). Seemed legit to us (note, not talking about 'pausing' in a hex for infantry, but rather entering an extra hex that really isn't necessary to get where they want to go.  I believe 'pausing' is only for vehicles, correct?).

3) US Players decided to stop all movement at 4+ hexes from Germans on first turn, so no StarShell opportunities were generated.

4) During first German player turn, pretty much nothing much happens.  No rally phase stuff desired/needed (could deploy, I suppose, but no broken units or wpns to recover, etc). No Prep Fire, since no units within NVR. No IR able to be fired by the US MTRs, since we're under the 'First Illumination' rules and the US units don't have any Germans within 3 hexes either (the NVR).

5) During turn 2, US units start moving within NVR of the Germans. They remain Cloaked, but the Germans are allowed to attempt StarShell placement. They are also allowed to fire at them at half FP (concealed). If a Cloaked unit is moving down the road in the open w/in 3 hexes (NVR) of a German and the German 4-6-7 fires at them, the attack would be a 2 FP attack w/-1 DRM net, correct (assuming Non-assault movement).  -2 for FFMO/FFNAM and +1 for LV. BUT, the German would not gain Freedom of Movement until the US units came out of concealment (so would need at least a PTC on a non-Dummy Cloak/"?").

6) Once the first German unit fires (in our case, during the DFPh, not MPH ... because I completely forgot that I could fire and still get the -2 FFMO/FFNAM), then ANY German unit can attempt StarShell placement. However, chances are they would have to use option 1 (same hex) or option 3 (3 hexes away).

7) We placed our first starshell and it illuminated a bunch of cloaked US units (DFPh). These units remain cloaked unless I generate at least a PTC, they fire, or if any other Concealment loss activity occurs (e.g. they advance into a minefield and break, etc). Simply being illuminated while in Open Ground does nothing.

Now into the questions...
8 ) So after placing that first Starshell in the DFPh of turn 2 (US player turn), we saw nothing in the rules that prohibited other German units from attempting starshell placement due to there being a friendly Gunflash in that same player turn. I.e. the prohibitions after the first gunflash seemed to be all about subsequent player turns ... but, applying a COWTRA principal, these subsequent starshells aren't "the first star shell" ... so are they allowed to be fired due to a friendly gunflash?  Was moot in our game, as both attempts rolled > usage # ... but we weren't 100% certain whether to follow the language "The first star shell" or the language "during subsequent player turns".

9) Units firing at illuminated hexes, but outside the NVR of all enemy units, would fire but remain concealed (if cloaked, they would lose cloaking, but gain concealment).  Presuming we did this correctly, how do people generally handle this? Do you temporarily reveal what is firing, resolve the fire, then return the units under a "?" counter? Do you just say "I have 8 FPs attacking from this hex" and the other person takes you for your word ( the advantage of this is that one does not have to reveal if they have any SWs that aren't firing or a leader in the hex that isn't participating, which would be kind of obvious if one were to remove the "?" counter, even in VASL[i/]). 10) Along the same lines, though I think we got this correct, we had cloaking units enter hexes with a HiP Wire. If they said 'no', I would tell them that they needed to remove the unit, but wouldn't tell them why (e.g. whether it was wire, mines or a HiP German). query: Civilian Interrogation: Unusual situation. The random location chosen for civilian interrogation was occupied solely by and AFV. The final result on the information table was false information. So theoretically the AFV would be marked TI. I don’t think an AFV can be marked TI. Not sure?
title: Civilian Interrogation
raw_question: Unusual situation. The random location chosen for civilian interrogation was occupied solely by and AFV. The final result on the information table was false information. So theoretically the AFV would be marked TI. I don’t think an AFV can be marked TI. Not sure?
ground_truth_answer:
A4.8 : "... TI status is incurred by Infantry..." seems to exclude vehicles.
E2.41 speaks of "ground units", which includes vehicles indeed.
Another approximation of chapter E, I am afraid

G5.5 Huts can Pin an AFV when they collapse, even though A7.8 excludes vehicles, but with some exceptions ("Cavalry, vehicles, units in Water Obstacles, and units that are berserk, Heroic, Aerial, or Climbing are not subject to pinning [EXC: a Minimum Move (4.134) pins berserk/heroic Infantry, as might a PF check (C13.31); see G5.5 for Collapsed huts]. ")... 
The TI rule evokes no exception.

query: OVR and first fired BAZ: My Squad has a BAZ which has first fired. An enemy AFV enters the hex and OVRs. Can I non-CC Reaction Fire the BAZ at the AFV?
title: OVR and first fired BAZ
raw_question: My Squad has a BAZ which has first fired. An enemy AFV enters the hex and OVRs. Can I non-CC Reaction Fire the BAZ at the AFV?
ground_truth_answer:
Thanks everyone. I understand where you are coming from but it appears to me there is at least one case where I can fire the BAZ a second time-- if I am marked with a Final Fire counter instead of a First Fire counter? 

In this case, D7.221 FPF NON-CC REACTION FIRE says 'Each DEFENDER Personnel unit eligible to use Non-CC Reaction Fire, and marked by a Final Fire counter when OVR by other than an unarmored vehicle with no PRC, must use (as per 7.22) TPBF, an ordnance SW, a FT or a Thrown DC vs that vehicle [EXC: if pinned, it cannot use FT or DC (A7.81); if otherwise allowed, it may use CC Reaction Fire (7.212) instead]. '

My reading in this case is that if I was marked Final Fire I not only may but must use TPBF or ordnance SW. (If a BAZ can't be used here, what 'ordnance SW' does it mean?)

So if I'm right, I could fire my BAZ when marked Final Fire. Therefore I would have had the option of firing my inherent FP at the oncoming AFV (although unable to affect it) just to get the Final Fire marker on the squad and its SWs, then I could have used the BAZ in non-CC Reaction Fire (albeit with the TH roll counting as a NMC on me).
I think you could fire the BAZ if if was marked Final Fire - but only if it has not yet fired in the turn.

query:
Wrapping my head around MA/MG usage for AFV: Hi everyone !

As I'm slowly discovering the full ASL world, and playing some games, I'm still having difficulties being sure about when to use (or may be "not use") the MA/MG on an AFV.
I browsed the rules and came with a summary, could it be possible to have some help on it from you ASL veterans ? 🙂

As an ATTACKER : MG and MA have to be used in the same phase during the turn, and using one forfeits the possibility to use the other in a subsequent phase.

- Firing in the PFPh : full FP for MA and MG, but the AFV can't either move or shoot during the rest of the ATTACKER turn ;
- Firing in the MFPh : Bounding First Fire territory, depending on stopped/non-stopped status, MG FP are 1/2 or 1/4, and MA has DRM (cases B, C1, C2 or C4) ;
- Firing in the AFPh : if MA has not been used yet, or if only MA (not MG) has been used previously and ROF has been maintained, it can be fired again as Bounding Fire (cases B, C or C4), and MG can be used at 1/2 FP (stopped) or 1/4 FP (motion).

As an DEFENDER :
- Firing in the ENEMY MFPh : MA can be used as First Fire, if it maintains ROF it stays without a counter and can keep First firing. When ROF is lost, a First Fire counter is on it. It can fire once more as Intensive Fire, and becomes Final Fire. 
MG is used "like an infantry SW" as First Fire, Subsequent First Fire and Final Fire (<= this I'm not sure at all).
- Firing in the DFPh : MA can be used normally if not marked First Fire, however if already First Fire, it can be used as Intensive Fire but only on ADJACENT hexes. MG can be used if not used in a previous phase, full FP or 1/2 FP if in motion.

So for now this is all I could gather from rules and forum discussions, but I know I’m missing some cases here.. If someone could help, thanks a lot in advance!!

query:
Night Rules - Taking the Left Tit Scenario: Ok...so we're taking a break from CGs and trying to learn Night Rules.  We've read some excellent stuff on-line.  We've read the rules a few times and have set up Taking the Left Tit (ASL20) to try to learn things.  We are using the errata that adds the 9-1 and 2x 4-6-7s, and clarifies the victory conditions.  I'm going to list a series of statements that we THINK are correct... if any are wrong, please let us know where we are going off the rails...

1) The US is the Scenario Attacker per SSR and, as such, can use Cloaking.  The SSR specifies may set up Cloaked, so - unlike in the actual rules - they are not required to have all units set up Cloaked; e.g. they could have the MTRs set up outside of Cloaking counters.

2) If they set up the MTRs (and HSs with them) outside of Cloaking, these units would begin Concealed as being set up outside of LOS (>3 hexes due to NVR of 3) of all Germans.  The MTRs would still begin dm though, as that is how they are listed on the setup card.

3) The Germans are the Scenario Defender per SSR and, as such, are subject to Freedom of Movement rules and Bore Sighting.  The latter only applies to the HMG and MMG.  For them, this means two things: fire into the bore sighted hex gets an additional -2 IFT DRM for Def First Fire attacks only, unless using Spraying Fire or Snap Shot (C6.44) - and - a FL can be established to this hex even if no enemy unit is present under specific conditions (E1.71).

4) The Germans set up, get 25% (2 squads) + stacked with SMC/SW HIP and get 8 concealment counters.  If in appropriate terrain, they may freely set up in 1S Foxholes (per Squad/HS in the hex).  One cannot place a 3S Foxhole in a hex with only 1S.

5) The lead German leader is the 9-1.  This remains the case even if he is wounded, but not if eliminated or ELR fails (while wounded would reduce his game effects to an 8-0 leader, it does not change him to such).  This is important for Freedom of Movement (E1.21).

6) We assume the following is correct (see graphic): 
- The US player declares cloak L is moving.  They may a Straying roll, which is a DR looking first at the colored die.  If a 6, they then look at the white die.  If >=3 (Normal units on both sides), the unit Strays unless an exception applies (in which no roll would be made).  Let us assume the roll was '5' and '4'.  No Straying.
- NVR is 3, so the Cloaked unit begins out of LOS of the German.  No Illumination has been done yet.  He moves as indicated.
- Entering FF8 costs 1 MP and is still out of NVR of the German in CC6. Entering the Brush costs 2 and is in a blind hex created by the level 1 hill in DD7 (LOS goes through the hill in DD7, so this is correct, right?  VASL shows LOS as clear, though...).  Entry of hex DD7 is within the NVR of the German unit and gives the German unit options.

7) At this point, the Cloak L is /not/ a Known enemy unit to the German player (even though in the NVR).  If hex DD7 was Illuminated before the Cloaked L enter it, the Cloaking would be lost and the contents placed on map unconcealed and, at that point, they WOULD be a Known enemy unit.  If the German unit in CC6 successfully places a Starshell that illuminates DD7, the contents of Cloak L would /not/ be placed on map unless Cloak L continues moving.

8 ) The German player decides to fire on the Cloak L in DD7.  His attack is a 3.5 factor attack with a net -1 DRM (-1 FFMO, -1 FFNAM, +1 LV).  If he rolls low enough to get at least a PTC, the contents of Cloak L are placed on the map unconcealed and Cloak L is permanently removed.  He is marked with a FF counter (gunflash) and is now visible to all units that can see hex CC6, regardless of range.  He is NOT "Illuminated" (E1.8).  Let us assume he failed to remove the Cloaking and lost ROF.  A 1 Residual Fire marker would be placed in the hex (attack on the 2 column, no other hindrance other than the LV, which does not shift Residual Fire Power).

9) When Cloak L enters hex CC7, the German player could Final Fire, again on the 2 column (MG would be using Sustained Fire).

10) Before firing on Cloak L in DD7, the German player could have this MMC attempt to fire a Starshell per the 2nd bullet of E1.91 (a friendly unit capable of firing a Starshell; i.e. the German MMC; has an LOS to an enemy unit; i.e. does not have to be a KNOWN enemy unit).

11) After firing on Cloak L in DD7, /any/ German unit could attempt to place the first Starshell per the 3rd bullet of E1.91 (a Gunflash; i.e. the one on the German in hex CC6; is placed due to an attack vs an enemy unit; i.e. against Cloak L.  This would occur even before Cloak L gets to continue moving from hex DD7.

12) As long as hexes DD7 and CC7 are not Illuminated, Cloak L does NOT lose its Cloaking unless it is fired on with a result of at least a PTC or performs some other Concealment loss activity (e.g. placing Smoke Grenades).  Simply moving in the open in NVR of an enemy in a non-Illuminated hex is not sufficient to cause loss of Cloaking and Concealment.

13) Cloaking and concealment is only lost by using non-assault movement in an already Illuminated location, entering an enemy location (barring successful Ambush in CC), attacking in any way other than a successful Ambush, or via a successful Sniper attack on that hex. 

9) Let's say that the Germans in hex CC6 are Illuminated by a Starshell in hex BB5.  Instead of moving, the US player decides to have the units in Cloak L fire at the Germans during the PFPh.  They are placed on the map under both a Concealment marker and a prep fire marker.  The former because they are not in the NVR of the German, so are not in the Germans LOS.  The Gunflash marker (Prep Fire marker) merely allows the German to make an attack against that hex at 1/2 FP (not 1/4 due to the US concealment).

10) Cloak L contains a single 6-6-6 squad. If the US player ends his move in CC7 and Advancing Fires at the German player in CC6, he attacks at a strength of 8 (6 halved to 3 for movement, +1 for assault fire, then doubled for PBF to 8 ) at either +1 DRM (height advantage) or +2 DRM (foxhole), since the LV +1 does not apply to the Germans given their terrain being at least 1 level higher than CC7.  If the German had not yet fired, this would be a 4 strength attack due to the German still being concealed.

11) Assuming the US player does the above attack, the 6-6-6 is now marked with a gunflash (Adv Fire) counter.  If IR/Starshells had not yet been placed, this would allow the US player to subsequently fire IRs, BUT NOT Starshells, in this Adv Fire phase - assuming the MTRs were assembled.  Neither player may fire Starshells during the AFPh, even as a first use.

12) If the US player does not fire, during the subsequent German Movement Phase, only the 4-6-7 in CC6 and any other Germans that can see CC7 can gain Freedom of Movement and, even then, ONLY IF the US units were removed from the Cloaking counter (i.e. become Known enemy units).

13) If the US player attacks with the 6-6-6 in hex CC7 and fails to do anything to the German in hex CC6, the US unit does NOT gain concealment as it is in the NVR and LOS of the German in CC6.  If a subsequent US unit had been out of concealment in hex GG7 (4 hexes from CC7), they WOULD gain concealment (but not Cloaking), as they would be out of LOS of the German in CC7.

14) If the US player /does/ fire, during the subsequent German Movement Phase, the 4-6-7 and any German units that can see CC7 gain Freedom of Movement as they have been attacked (the 4-6-7) by a non-OBA, non-Sniper attack or have LOS to a Known enemy unit (the 6-6-6 in hex CC7).  This attack/visibility is irrelevant to the existence or cloaking status of the 6-6-6 in CC7 at the moment of movement, but merely has to have been at 'some point' in the scenario (i.e. upon the US attack). 

15) Furthermore, once the US has made their first attack that is not a successful Ambush, the 9-1 Leader may attempt to gain Freedom of Movement regardless of his on-map location by rolling a 2 or less (ELR of 3).  If he is successful, he can provide FoM to any unit that begins THE movement phase stacked with him (e.g. all units in his hex.  Contrary to at least one publication out there, one cannot 'chain' leaders or have a single leader grant FoM to multiple hexes in the same MPh...it is only if the units begin THE MOVEMENT PHASE with the Leader (E1.21).

15) A unit granted FoM does not HAVE to move.  E.g. if the Germans have a 4-6-7 stacked with the 9-1 leader and the 9-1 leader gains FoM, the 4-6-7 should be indicated as having FoM even if he chose to Prep Fire and the 9-1 leaves the hex during its MPh (assuming it did not direct the fire).

16) If the 4-6-7 wanted to fire a Starshell at the US Cloak L in hex DD7, it would have 3 options: it could fire it at its own hex, with a scatter of 1 hex; it would fire it at CC7/DD6 or DD7 (target hex) with a scatter of 1-3 hexes (dr, FRU); it could fire it at EE8 or DD8 (among others) that are exactly 3 hexes away from it.  No LOS is needed to these hexes.

17) A MTR firing IR must first make a dr<=4, then a 'to hit' roll, though only checking for malf.  No LOS is needed to the desired target hex.  No ROF is allowed.

18) Once the first Starshells/IR round has been placed, subsequent turns limit them to: Starshells by non-leaders must be placed at the start of the PFPh or MPh before the ATTACKER commences firing/moving.  A leader may attempt to fire a Starshell at any point in the PFPh or MPh.  IR can be attempted in any phase that the mortar could fire (PFPh; enemy MPh; DFPh; AFPh).

10) Before firing on Cloak L in DD7, the German player could have this MMC attempt to fire a Starshell per the 2nd bullet of E1.91 (a friendly unit capable of firing a Starshell; i.e. the German MMC; has an LOS to an enemy unit; i.e. does not have to be a KNOWN enemy unit).

11) After firing on Cloak L in DD7, /any/ German unit could attempt to place the first Starshell per the 3rd bullet of E1.91 (a Gunflash; i.e. the one on the German in hex CC6; is placed due to an attack vs an enemy unit; i.e. against Cloak L.  This would occur even before Cloak L gets to continue moving from hex DD7.

12) As long as hexes DD7 and CC7 are not Illuminated, Cloak L does NOT lose its Cloaking unless it is fired on with a result of at least a PTC or performs some other Concealment loss activity (e.g. placing Smoke Grenades).  Simply moving in the open in NVR of an enemy in a non-Illuminated hex is not sufficient to cause loss of Cloaking and Concealment.

13) Cloaking and concealment is only lost by using non-assault movement in an already Illuminated location, entering an enemy location (barring successful Ambush in CC), attacking in any way other than a successful Ambush, or via a successful Sniper attack on that hex. 

9) Let's say that the Germans in hex CC6 are Illuminated by a Starshell in hex BB5.  Instead of moving, the US player decides to have the units in Cloak L fire at the Germans during the PFPh.  They are placed on the map under both a Concealment marker and a prep fire marker.  The former because they are not in the NVR of the German, so are not in the Germans LOS.  The Gunflash marker (Prep Fire marker) merely allows the German to make an attack against that hex at 1/2 FP (not 1/4 due to the US concealment).

10) Cloak L contains a single 6-6-6 squad. If the US player ends his move in CC7 and Advancing Fires at the German player in CC6, he attacks at a strength of 8 (6 halved to 3 for movement, +1 for assault fire, then doubled for PBF to 8 ) at either +1 DRM (height advantage) or +2 DRM (foxhole), since the LV +1 does not apply to the Germans given their terrain being at least 1 level higher than CC7.  If the German had not yet fired, this would be a 4 strength attack due to the German still being concealed.

11) Assuming the US player does the above attack, the 6-6-6 is now marked with a gunflash (Adv Fire) counter.  If IR/Starshells had not yet been placed, this would allow the US player to subsequently fire IRs, BUT NOT Starshells, in this Adv Fire phase - assuming the MTRs were assembled.  Neither player may fire Starshells during the AFPh, even as a first use.

12) If the US player does not fire, during the subsequent German Movement Phase, only the 4-6-7 in CC6 and any other Germans that can see CC7 can gain Freedom of Movement and, even then, ONLY IF the US units were removed from the Cloaking counter (i.e. become Known enemy units).

13) If the US player attacks with the 6-6-6 in hex CC7 and fails to do anything to the German in hex CC6, the US unit does NOT gain concealment as it is in the NVR and LOS of the German in CC6.  If a subsequent US unit had been out of concealment in hex GG7 (4 hexes from CC7), they WOULD gain concealment (but not Cloaking), as they would be out of LOS of the German in CC7.

14) If the US player /does/ fire, during the subsequent German Movement Phase, the 4-6-7 and any German units that can see CC7 gain Freedom of Movement as they have been attacked (the 4-6-7) by a non-OBA, non-Sniper attack or have LOS to a Known enemy unit (the 6-6-6 in hex CC7).  This attack/visibility is irrelevant to the existence or cloaking status of the 6-6-6 in CC7 at the moment of movement, but merely has to have been at 'some point' in the scenario (i.e. upon the US attack). 

15) Furthermore, once the US has made their first attack that is not a successful Ambush, the 9-1 Leader may attempt to gain Freedom of Movement regardless of his on-map location by rolling a 2 or less (ELR of 3).  If he is successful, he can provide FoM to any unit that begins THE movement phase stacked with him (e.g. all units in his hex.  Contrary to at least one publication out there, one cannot 'chain' leaders or have a single leader grant FoM to multiple hexes in the same MPh...it is only if the units begin THE MOVEMENT PHASE with the Leader (E1.21).

15) A unit granted FoM does not HAVE to move.  E.g. if the Germans have a 4-6-7 stacked with the 9-1 leader and the 9-1 leader gains FoM, the 4-6-7 should be indicated as having FoM even if he chose to Prep Fire and the 9-1 leaves the hex during its MPh (assuming it did not direct the fire).

16) If the 4-6-7 wanted to fire a Starshell at the US Cloak L in hex DD7, it would have 3 options: it could fire it at its own hex, with a scatter of 1 hex; it would fire it at CC7/DD6 or DD7 (target hex) with a scatter of 1-3 hexes (dr, FRU); it could fire it at EE8 or DD8 (among others) that are exactly 3 hexes away from it.  No LOS is needed to these hexes.

17) A MTR firing IR must first make a dr<=4, then a 'to hit' roll, though only checking for malf.  No LOS is needed to the desired target hex.  No ROF is allowed.

18) Once the first Starshells/IR round has been placed, subsequent turns limit them to: Starshells by non-leaders must be placed at the start of the PFPh or MPh before the ATTACKER commences firing/moving.  A leader may attempt to fire a Starshell at any point in the PFPh or MPh.  IR can be attempted in any phase that the mortar could fire (PFPh; enemy MPh; DFPh; AFPh).
ground_truth_answer:
You seem to be mostly correct.

6: Hill crest lines have a base of 0 blind hexes, instead of 1 for normal obstacles. That's why LOS to EE8 is clear. (B10.23)

Wow... we've been playing this wrong for probably 30+ years... Assuming this existed when AH first published ASL.  I'm glad I asked!

 15 (both): Note that the 9-1 would make his FoM roll during the German MPh, and if he fails it can also be attempted on subsequent MPh. Despite the rules, it is probably best to think in terms of the restriction of the No Move counter than benefit of FoM. A unit with FoM can act like any regular unit, moving or not, firing, ect, as a normal unit. A unit still on a No Move counter... cannot move.

Good point about 'restrictions' of No Move versus 'benefits' of FoM.  I'm glad we are mostly getting these right!

 16: You only fire a starshell 'at' (towards) a unit under option 2. Note that that requires LOS to a gunflash or KEU, so if the only thing nearby is Cloak L, then that option isn't allowed, and the only choices are 1) in his own hex (with one hex drift), 3) three hexes away (no LOS needed) with a full scatter (which can land it up to six hexes from its target).

Right ... 'along the LOS' towards the unit.  Completely missed that it had to be a KEU though!  So, yeah, he could only fire it to his own hex or a hex 3 hexes away from him (which then has full scatter, so who knows where it will end up.. ...  "Heinz!  Why did you shoot the Starshell backwards!  Yyyyooouuu know nothing!"

18: I'd missed that leader EXC in the middle of E1.921; I think many others have as well. Do note that only one attempt may be made per hex, so a squad making an attempt at the start of MPh would keep a leader stacked with him from making an attempt later. So, you see a lot of leader attempts at the start of the phase.

Agreed.  They /could/ try to fire in both phases from the same hex, as the limit is one attempt per hex per phase, but I can't see that happening very often.  I do think having hexes with leaders not fire right away during the DFPh is probably smart, since that gives you the most flexibility on the timing of firing a Starshell (or 'attempted' firing, I guess...).

 Note that units in an Illuminated Location can only have LOS to other Illuminated Locations and gunflashes (and the latter doesn't reveal units). This can mean an adjacent unit is out of LOS (botched starshell placement is a great source of this situation).

Ahh, yes..  We had talked about this when we were kibitzing last night.  I can see the US dropping IR rounds on the Germans to, effectively, 'blind' them ... unless they can illuminate outside hexes.

Do IRs scatter?  I'm thinking that they do from the language in E1.932 that they use "method 2" or "method 3", which lists scatter of dr halved (FRU) and full dr, respectively.  So no one is really gonna know where illumination will be as these things go off given the scatter.

query:
VBM and Reaction Fire - what did we do wrong/right?: Ok... my brother and I are continuing our ASL adventures with Elst.  We're in CG day 2, with full ASL rules, and slogging away around the center of the town.  Due to routing, etc., he ended up with a huge nest of nasty SS in a single stone building.  Due to me being a fool, I ended up with multiple tanks with broken main armaments.  A match made in heaven for VBM to allow my grunts to move up, obviously (ok... probably not versus SS Germans, but ...hey... we're still playing around to learn what is 'good', 'bad' and 'just plain st00pid').

We're looking at hex FF13 in Elst: .

The starting situation is: .  I've left off other units, etc. to make the question/situation clearer, just FYI.

During the Prep Fire phase, I successfully fire smoke onto FF13.  I then activate the tank in DD14 and move as follows:
start (1 MP); CA change CCW (1); VBM into EE14 (DD13-EE14 edge, for 2 MP); activate sD (succeed even with +1 for BU, for 1 MP)*; CC change CW (1)**; VBM still in EE14 (EE13-EE14 edge, for 4 MP)*** ... then it got confusing for us.  This put him at 10 MPs expended.  He wanted to move into FF13 along the EE13-FF13 hexside.  Since FF13 also had SMOKE, the cost would be 4 MPs to enter that hexside, but he needs to change his CA for another 1 MP.  That puts it at a total of 15 MPs, so he needs to do ESB.  I roll a 9, +1 for the extra MP +2 for British and he is immobilized.  He stays in VBM in EE14.  This I think we got correct.  The question that we had was ... what is his CA???  Is the 1 MP CA change considered part of the VBM 'cost' to enter FF13?  Or is the CA change done first?  Or did we screw  up and he didn't need a CA change, even though he wasn't entering the obstacle in FF13, but was 'turning' to VBM it along the EE13-FF13 hexside?  We ended up ruling that the CA cost was part of the total MP cost to enter the hex, so his CA remained facing FF13: 

NOTES:
*) In hindsight, depositing smoke here was stupid..I should have done it at the EE13-EE14 hexspine.
**) We weren't certain if CA changes in Smoke are effected... i.e. 1 MP or 2 MP per CA change.  No change to a 'new location' so we went with just 1 MP.
***) We really weren't sure if the Smoke changes the VBM cost.  The VBM movement rules certainly imply that Smoke cost impacts VBM (and is clear that the +1 is doubled to +2). But is the vehicle actually entering a 'new location'?  Smoke is +1 MP/MF upon entering a NEW LOCATION.  We thought it made sense that it should double the cost (so total cost = 4 MPs), but we were quite uncertain.

So I then activated a second tank (also with broken MA) and tried, again, to get into VBM into FF13: .

He came dashing in and made it to FF13 where he then faced the onslaught of German defenders attempting to eliminate him so that he didn't prevent their fire to outside their own hex.  The Germans had three squads and a 9-1 leader: .

First, he had the leader direct the PSK, stepping out of the building to avoid everyone suffering the 1 IFT roll.  We felt his too hit roll was: 11 (0 hex range) -3 (SMOKE) -1 (firing out of SMOKE) -2 (Moving Vehicle) -2 (avoid backblast) +1 (size) +1 (Leadership), or needing a 5 or less.  He rolled a 10, x10'ing the PSK.  He then decided to attempt CC Reaction Fire with the squad + leader.  He passed the PAATC and attacked in CC.  No Ambush as not Street Fighting and no response by tank (?? we weren't sure on this, but didn't think so).  We determined his CCV as: 5 (squad) +1 (leader) +1 (leadership) -2 (moving) = 5.  He tried for an ATMM, but failed.  He rolled an 8, so no effect.  We marked them First Fire and CC (correct?).

He then had the other 6-5-8 attempt a PF check.  He succeeded and we determined his To Hit roll as: 10 (0 hex range) -3 (SMOKE) -1 (firing out of SMOKE) -2 (Moving Vehicle) -2 (avoid backblast) +1 (size) = 3.  He rolled a '4'.  He then tried to have that squad CC Reaction Fire on the tank, but failed the PAATC (leadership could not apply, as not part of same FG, correct?).  The last 4-4-7 missed both its PF check and PAATC.  Both these squads were marked First Fire and Pinned (correct?).

We stopped here, but some follow-up questions.
1) If I end my vehicle in Motion, he does not put the enemy into Melee and if I advance any squads in (I have 2 squads and a HS in DD14 that have yet to move), I would have to roll for Ambush with the Germans having a net +2 DRM (BU vehicle vs Pinned), correct?

2) If I spend a top MP with the vehicle (which would require another ESB check *gulp*), would it put a Melee on the hex NOW?  Or only at end of CC Phase?  I think the latter, right?  So stopping doesn't prevent an Ambush roll if I advance in later :(.

3) If I don't stop, his squads are not prevented from leaving that hex during his MPh, so they could assault move to FF12 to get out of the SMOKE, etc. ... unless I advance in squads and don't have them all killed by his CC fire.

4) If the German Squads had fired 2 PFs (or the PSK and then a PF check), would they also have been able to conduct CC Reaction Fire?  The Overrun Flow Chart implies 'yes' (they'd have been marked First Fire after the second SW, and the flow chart seems to imply  that units marked First Fire can still conduct CC Reaction Fire, but would be at a -1 CCV DRM due to halved FP...correct?).

5) The charts list an ATMM as a 'support weapon', but how does that apply if a squad uses one in CC?  The one German CC failed to generate one, but we weren't sure if it mattered that he already fired a PSK earlier (i.e. the ATMM would be a 'second SW usage' by that same squad)?  Do ATMM actually /count/ as a SW usage?  The ATMM rules don't seem to imply this, but the '1G' on the Support Weapons Chart made us wonder (though I see now that it does NOT have note A or B associated with it, which is clear that those prohibit, potentially, inherent FP).  So I think we got this right ... that using ATMM never impacts inherent FP.

Comments on anything that we did wrong (or just 'yeah, that looks like you played it right') would be appreciated.  This one series of movement probably took us an hour, lol... as we had to read back up on the CC Reaction Fire, check the Overrun Flow Chart, etc.

query:
Pinned unit withdrawal in close combat: We had a disagreement concerning pinned units in close combat.

From what I gather from the infiltration rule (A.11.22) : "Any Infantry/Cavalry unit(s) attacked by an Original 12 CC DR may likewise withdraw from CC immediately thereafter, assuming it has not been eliminated by that 12 CC DR"

So, when in close combat the opponent get an original CC DR of 12, you can withdraw "any infantry". It then references to the ambush withdrawal rule A.11.41.

But the ambush withdrawal rule referenced state A.11.41 states that ambush withdrawal is non available for pinned unit.

"Any Infantry (unless pinned/berserk/Disrupted)..." 

Should we consider "any infantry" from A.11.22 or  "Any Infantry (unless pinned/berserk/disrupted)" from the rule A.11.41 it referenced ?

Therefore can I withdraw my units out of this combat?

Thanks.
title: Pinned unit withdrawal in close combat

Q&A:

A11.22
It seems to me that the literal reading of A11.22 says that a pinned unit may withdraw from CC if the opponent rolls a 12. Can
they? Or is the intent of A11.21 (and other related rules) that a PINNED unit can never withdraw from CC?
A. A pinned unit may never withdraw.

query: Cloaking loss during APH: If a cloaked & Concealed unit Advances into a Shellhole, in LOS of a enemy Unit in a illuminated hex, do they loose Cloaking and concealment ?
title: Cloaking loss during APH
raw_question: If a cloaked & Concealed unit Advances into a Shellhole, in LOS of a enemy Unit in a illuminated hex, do they loose Cloaking and concealment ?
ground_truth_answer:
You cannot be "cloaked and concealed".  It's one or the other.

E1.31 LOSS: An Infantry unit loses Cloaking/"?" at night if it uses Non-Assault Movement in a Location that is already Illuminated when that unit expends MF in it, or if it enters an enemy-occupied Location during the MPh. Otherwise, it does not lose Cloaking/concealment at night when moving/advancing.

It doesn't matter whether it's Open Ground or not.  It doesn't matter whether it's Illuminated or not.  It doesn't matter whether anyone has LOS or not.  What matters is: it's the APh.

Units do not move during the APh.  They advance.

The only circumstance I can think of where you might lose Cloaking/"?" during the APh in a Night scenario is if you advance onto an A-P minefield (or into a FFE), and the resulting attack causes at least a PTC, and you are within NVR (which includes being in an Illuminated Location) and LOS of a Good Order enemy unit.
