ground_truth_answer:
1. Does the A8.3 mean:
A squad with a MG are all under the First Fire counter. If the squad take SFF alone, the SFF chance of the MG surely will be forfeited. But if the player claim to use MG SFF only, will the squad also be considered as SFF, so they will under Final Fire counter too after the MG SFF?

Yes. In SFF, inherent firepower and MGs are bound together. The reason to forfeit MG usually is because of fear of potential breakdown.

So in this situation, if we want to maximize the MG and squad FP, we can:
1. Attacker spends MF
2. First Fire MG
3. Attacker spends another MF
4. First Fire Squad
5. Attacker spends another MF or if Attack is adjacent, wait until Defensive Fire Phase.
6. SFF both Squad and MG.

2. Another assumption:
MG First Fired but the squad did not. Can the squad use the MG to SFF only (then turn the counter to Final Fire), but hold its own FP and remain clear of  First/Final fire counter?

No.

3.What does 7.353 imply to? I can't imagine such condition this rule can apply.

It actually refers to 8.3.
7.351 and 7.352 says the inherent FP can be used only once and can add to MG, even if the MG retains ROF. This case applies to Prep Fire.
7.353 says that inherent FP can be used again in the same Movement/Defensive Fire Phase in forms of SFF, FPF and FP to adjacent target. All of these use 1/2 inherent FP.

The Index is your friend :

	
Hooking Up Guns: C10.11 [CMD DR: S16.35] [Towing on Narrow Street: B31.124]

C10.11 HOOKING UP: A Stopped vehicle not in Bypass may hook up a Gun (if the vehicle's T# ≤ the Gun's M#) by spending half (FRU) of its MP/MF allotment [EXC: if the Gun's M# is circled (e.g. M(6), the vehicle must expend two-thirds (FRU) of its MP/MF allotment] in that Gun's hex (in addition to any required MP/MF cost to enter the hex), provided a crew (as per 10.111) is on foot in that hex. That Gun is then placed on top of that vehicle to indicate that it is in tow. Neither that Gun, its crew, nor that vehicle/its PRC can fire during that PFPh/MPh and all are TI for the rest of that Player Turn. That crew may also load into that towing vehicle at no extra MP/MF cost as it hooks up that Gun, but if it expends > half its MF allotment in pushing/entering that Gun's hex, that Gun cannot then be hooked up by that unit in that MPh. A non-QSU Gun (10.23) must first be limbered (10.21) before it can be hooked up. See 10.31 for pushing and hooking up a Gun in the same MPh.

It would charge the last known location in LOS that an enemy unit occupied before leaving LOS.

RPh actions: recombine + transfer?: Is it legal in the RPh to recombine two HS into a squad and then transfer one SW from this just recombined squad to a different squad in the same Location?

title: RPh actions: recombine + transfer?
raw_question:
Is it legal in the RPh to recombine two HS into a squad and then transfer one SW from this just recombined squad to a different squad in the same Location?

I'm asking because I don't know if these two actions (recombine and transfer) count as two different actions and thus cannot be done by the same unit in the same RPh.
ground_truth_answer:
Yes, I believe you can.  Recombining (A1.32) is described as an action.  But transfer (A4.431) says during RPh, in the same location "Stacks may be freely rearranged to change possession of SW/Guns...".  And does not call transfer an action.

Deployment, Recombining and Recovery are clearly specified as sole actions during the RPh.

Transfer is not so specified, so it could be a free action. But I'm not really sure.

Hi Jonathan,

Dealing with your questions in turn:

1) No, a unit which suffers CR in CC is not broken as well

query:
A way to enter minefield covered buildings?: Playing Red Barricades we have had a discussion regarding a way to enter buildings covered by minefields.

The issue is about rule B24.74, the last part:

Good Order Infantry may enter a Known minefield hex free of minefield attack by placing a partial TB, provided they expend their entire MF allotment to do so, become TI, and attempt to clear the minefield at the end of their CCPh. Unless the minefield is cleared, these units may exit the minefield free if minefield attack only by the hexside through which they entered. No other units may use the partial TB. The partial TB counter is removed if they are eliminated or exit the hex.

We agree that if the minefield is in an Open Ground hex, if a squad enters it using this rule it can only exit the hex using the same hexside or they will be attacked by the minefield.

But if the minefield is in a non-interior building hex that belongs to a multi-hex building, if a squad enters this hex using rule B24.74, what happens?

A. Player A says that this squad is inside the building and thus after the Clearance DR, whether they succeed or fail, they are free to move to other parts of the building using building hexisdes, without being attacked by the minefield.

B. Player B says that until they succeed to clear the minefield they are in the minefield part of the hex and they can only move back using the partial TB or they will be attacked by the mines.

Question 1: Who is right?

If Player A is right, then using this method is a quite effective way of moving in the Red Barricades map through the minefield covered hexes, isn't it?

Question 2: If a unit that enters a minefield using rule B24.74 is subsequently broken in that Location before rolling for Clearance, can they exit the minefield without being attacked using their Partial TB or they lose their Partial TB when they are broken?

Thanks.

But if the minefield is in a non-interior building hex that belongs to a multi-hex building, if a squad enters this hex using rule B24.74, what happens?

B. Player B says that until they succeed to clear the minefield they are in the minefield part of the hex and they can only move back using the partial TB or they will be attacked by the mines.

Question 2: If a unit that enters a minefield using rule B24.74 is subsequently broken in that Location before rolling for Clearance, can they exit the minefield without being attacked using their Partial TB or they lose their Partial TB when they are broken?

Thanks.
ground_truth_answer:
I'd say the rule is clear enough  -  those units may exit the minefield free of attack by either successfully clearing the minefield, or by using their partial trail break counter to return to where they came from.

Ok in a non-building situation.

If they exit to another building hex without clearing the minefield, they'd get attacked by it.

Bute the minefield rules say:

28.412 A unit is considred to be in the minefield hex which attacks it when the attack is resolved.

28.41 Whenever a unit enters/leaves a minefield hex, the owning player must announce a minefield attack vs the unit (as per A12.11) on the IFT

B28.44 MINEFIELDS IN BUILDING/TRENCH HEXES: Minefields are allowed in non-Interior Building Hexes but do not attack units entering/exiting those hexes through a building hexside unless using Bypass Movement.

These rules are higher numbered than B24.74 so they take precedence. The unit attacked is inside the hex as there is no separate Location for the minefield. The attack only takes place as a unit enters or leaves the hex. A building hexside is an exception that allows units to move avoiding the minefield attack.

This is the point discussed. Do these rules create an exception for B24.74?

The only slight ambiguity is the use of the term hex instead of Location (a common problem in ASL rules). As written, they could go up to the 1st level (suffering an attack when they leave the minefield), and the trail break (only usable by them) would remain on the map until they leave the hex.

I don't think there is much ambiguity in the ASLRB between hexes and Locations. If a unit inside an Open Ground Location enters a Pillbox there, they enter a different Location but they are not attacked by the minefield because they don't leave the hex, only the Location.

ground_truth_answer: B9.33 ELEVATION EFFECTS: If a non-Aerial firer is at an elevation above the wall/hedge > the distance in hexes to the target hex, reduce the TEM of that wall/hedge hexside by one for each full level by which the height exceeds the distance (to a minimum TEM of 0). HS & SW usage: A7.352 states that a HS that uses a SW loses its inherent FP until CC or the end of the Player Turn. But where does it say that a HS that uses its inherent FP loses the subsequent use of its possessed SW? or is this just assumed by reciprocity of A7.352?

Also, the wording of A7.353 confuses me..is it just saying that if a HS uses a SW in D1F it can still use it's inherent firepower in SFF, FPF or FF?

I raise this issue as I had a situation where a HS with an ATR D1F at an enemy MMC with it's inherent FP. Then later in the MPh I went to fire the ATR at an AFV but was told I couldn't do this because the HS had all ready fired its inherent, but I can't find a rule that explicitly prohibits the use of a SW after a HS fires its inherent FP. So the citing of any rule that states this would be most helpful for me.

Thank you...
title: HS & SW usage
raw_question:
A7.352 states that a HS that uses a SW loses its inherent FP until CC or the end of the Player Turn. But where does it say that a HS that uses its inherent FP loses the subsequent use of its possessed SW? or is this just assumed by reciprocity of A7.352?

Also, the wording of A7.353 confuses me..is it just saying that if a HS uses a SW in D1F it can still use it's inherent firepower in SFF, FPF or FF?

I raise this issue as I had a situation where a HS with an ATR D1F at an enemy MMC with it's inherent FP. Then later in the MPh I went to fire the ATR at an AFV but was told I couldn't do this because the HS had all ready fired its inherent, but I can't find a rule that explicitly prohibits the use of a SW after a HS fires its inherent FP. So the citing of any rule that states this would be most helpful for me.

Thank you...
ground_truth_answer:
This is definitely one of the trickier parts of the ASL rules to learn.

A7.352 states that a HS that uses a SW loses its inherent FP until CC or the end of the Player Turn. But where does it say that a HS that uses its inherent FP loses the subsequent use of its possessed SW?
There is no rule that says that, because a HS using its inherent FP does not necessarily prohibit the subsequent use of its SW during defensive fire.

What A7.352 is actually saying is that when a HS fires, it must choose to fire either its inherent FP or a SW; it cannot fire both.

Also, the wording of A7.353 confuses me..is it just saying that if a HS uses a SW in D1F it can still use it's inherent firepower in SFF, FPF or FF?
Yes.

Here's an example of how this all works:

A HS with MMG will D1F at a moving enemy unit. It chooses to use its inherent FP in this attack. After resolving the attack both the HS and the MMG are marked with a First Fire counter. (The MMG cannot make a D1F attack of its own, from A7.352.)

The enemy unit now expends another MF, so the HS declares a SFF attack. Once again it must choose to use either its inherent FP (x 1/2) or the MMG (FP x 1/2 + Sustained Fire). Regardless of the choice made, both the HS and the MMG are marked with a Final Fire counter after resolving the attack.

Note especially that the use of the HS's inherent FP in the D1F attack does not prevent the subsequent use of the MMG in other SFF/FPF/FF attacks. And, had the HS used the MMG in the D1F attack, that would not prevent the use of its inherent FP in other SFF/FPF/FF attacks.

The enemy unit now moves adjacent to the HS, so the HS declares a FPF attack. The MMG must be used in a FPF attack, so the HS's inherent FP cannot be used (unless the MMG malfunctioned in a previous attack).

I raise this issue as I had a situation where a HS with an ATR D1F at an enemy MMC with it's inherent FP. Then later in the MPh I went to fire the ATR at an AFV but was told I couldn't do this because the HS had all ready fired its inherent, but I can't find a rule that explicitly prohibits the use of a SW after a HS fires its inherent FP.
When your HS makes its D1F attack, both it and its ATR would be marked with a First Fire counter, because A7.352 states that a HS cannot fire both its inherent FP and a SW. This then prevents the ATR from firing for the remainder of the MPh, because only Small Arms/MG/IFE can use SFF or FPF, and only Guns can use Intensive Fire.

But if you had fired the ATR in a D1F attack, you could still use the HS's inherent FP for subsequent SFF/FPF/FF attacks.

query:
Rules summary for Partially Armored vehicles: To make my life easier when playing with partially armored vehicles, I'm summarizing some rules concerning them

From what I've gathered from the rulebook and G&A, partially armored vehicles handles the following situations like this:

TH/TK C7.11
If hit in the * facing, treat as unarmored.

Small Arms and MGs QA
If the fire originates from the * side (even if only the turret is unarmored), the vehicle is treated as unarmored. TH process is not necessary for MGs.

Pin result A7.82
If the fire originated from the * side, treat as OT vehicle (meaning, the PRC just pins, but they keep their CE/BU status).

Driving into Residual FP D5.31
If the side is armored (usually) then the vehicle is treated as armored. Otherwise as unarmored (SdKfz 10/5).

Fire lane D5.311
Depends where the fire is coming from.

DC C7.346, QA
If placed through the * side, make an IFT (rather than a To Kill) DR vs the vehicle as if it were unarmored. DC position DR needs to be made.

Minefield QA
Unarmored only if the hull AF is 0, or if both its sides and rear are unarmored (SdKfz 10/5 again).

Close Combat A11.61, QA
Just the -2 DRM against it, even if it's also OT (not -3).

Sniper A14.22, 14.3
Treat as unarmored.

What about Aerial AF?
Depends on where the fire is coming from.

Behind a wall B9.36
If the fire originates from the * side:
- Small arms: The vehicle itself gets +2 DRM from the wall (cannot be hull down), but the PRC gets no protection.
- Ordnance: The vehicle is HD. If hit in the * turret, treat as unarmored.

Infantry and TPBF
This question is still unresolved and is currently discussed in GameSquad.
What do you think? I think it makes most sense if the unarmored facing is automatically assumed, but I can't back it up from the rules.

How does this look? Need to add anything?

ground_truth_answer:
I am about to start some of the scenarios in FKaC and many of them use gliders so I read the glider rules last night.

There are two references to "US Vehicle note 51 (LVT4)" if you transport vehicles on a glider. Is this info in Yanks?

Mark, here are the relevant bits from US Vehicle note 51:

51. LVT4: 

(snipsnipsnip - this is a looong vehicle note!)

PP CAPACITY: The LVT4 may transport any combination of the following items, with the total indicated PP applying to the LVT’s PP Capacity (D6.1):
  	
  Item	                       PP Cost
• Vehicle of ≤ 2 tons	         15
• Vehicle of > 2 but ≤ 4 tons	 30
• Non-MTR Gun with M# of ≥ 10	 10
• Gun with M# of 6-9	         20
• MTR of 76-107mm	          0
• Ammunition	             4 or 8 (1,3)
• Inherent vehicle crew	          0
• All other Personnel/SW     normal (2,3)

(1):	As per C10.13 (i.e., 4 PP for a Gun of ≤ 99mm, or 8 PP for one ≥ 100mm). This applicable PP cost is also used for a dm 76-82mm MTR, as well as for a 107mm mortar
(2):	As per their normal Passenger/Rider PP cost.
(3):	EXC: the PP cost of units/SW/ammo are reduced to zero if they are Passengers of a vehicle that is itself a Passenger.

VEHICLE: Unloading a Passenger vehicle consists of driving it off the LVT4 into the LVT’s Location at a cost of one MP for starting, plus one-fourth of the Passenger vehicle’s MP allotment, plus COT. There is no MP cost for entering the LVT’s Location (D2.14), but Overstacking will apply. Loading is the reverse of this procedure; i.e., the vehicle first enters the LVT’s Location if necessary (paying one extra MP; D2.14), and then expends one-fourth of its MP allotment plus one MP for COT to load onto it, plus one MP to stop. Otherwise, the normal principles of D6.4-.5 for (un)loading Passengers apply, including the “simultaneous expenditure” of each 25%-segment of movement allotment by both the Passenger vehicle and the LVT4 during the turn of (un)loading. An allowed vehicle can (un)load while towing a Gun (unless using Reverse movement; C10.1) by paying the extra MP for towing. A Passenger vehicle or Gun may not change its CA relative to that of its LVT. Since the LVT4’s ramp is at its rear, a vehicle’s VCA must coincide with the LVT’s VCA (or “rear” VCA) so that the vehicle is properly aligned for forward or reverse entry/exit onto/from the LVT. Overstacking does not occur due to a vehicle’s being a Passenger on an LVT4. A vehicle that is also a Passenger cannot claim or retain Motion status independently of the LVT4.

GUN: (Un)loading an unhooked Gun from/onto an LVT4 follows the same procedure as (un)hooking it from/to a towing vehicle (C10.11 & .2). A Gun may be (un)hooked from/to an allowable vehicle while both are Passengers on the LVT (any resulting TI status does not apply to the LVT).

SURVIVAL: If an LVT4 is destroyed (but does not burn) while on land, all unarmored vehicles and Guns aboard it are also destroyed; all vehicular PRC roll for survival using the LVT’s CS#. If an AFV is aboard such a destroyed LVT4, repeat the original attack, using its Original DR but now vs the AFV and adding an extra +2 TH (or IFT for non-ordnance) DRM as well as all other DRM applicable to that AFV. If the AFV survives it is bogged but may freely unload in a subsequent friendly MPh if it first passes a Bog Removal DR. The AFV’s PRC automatically survive the LVT’s destruction, but if the AFV does not survive they must roll for survival using the AFV’s CS#; if they survive they are placed on foot in the hex in the normal manner.

Hope this helps - enjoy!

JR

Tactical Analysis: Dreil Team by Matt Shostak

The British can only cross the stream at 4 points. These are the

You only spent 1 MF, so each defender with LOS may only fire once. A4.8 says nothing about TI status increasing your vulnerability to Defensive First Fire, so the normal rules will apply.

Yes, of course. You expended MF in a Open Ground hex.

Yes. Assault Movement is NA if you intend to search (A12.152).

ground_truth_answer:
... if a squad it must be capable of firing its inherent as First Fire too.

Does this mean, contrary to the opinions above, that a squad cannot do a MOL check in Final Fire if it has fired inherently in First Fire? If so, what is the meaning and significance of the references to First and Final Fire in A22.611 quoted above. Fogged.
A squad that has fired its inherent FP could make a MOL check in DFPh if it had not used a SW yet.
That doesn't seem compatible with what you said earlier:
Use for DFF is not prohibited. A MOL attack has to be made by a unit which has neither fired its inherent nor fired a SW, and if the unit is a squad it must use its inherent also at that same time [A22.611]. The unit must be capable of firing a SW it has not yet fired as First Fire, and if a squad it must be capable of firing its inherent as First Fire too.

Parsing the relevant sentences in A22.611:
Using a MOL in a PBF/TPBF attack entitles the firer to add four FP to that attack, even if it occurs as part of a Final Fire or TPBF attack. The MOL 4 FP bonus is always added after any modification of FP; i.e., it is not subject to modification.
These say a MOL always adds 4 FP--no more, no less.

A MOL Check dr can be made in neither Subsequent First Fire nor FPF, nor in both Defensive First Fire and later in Final Fire whether MOL were actually used in First Fire or not. {I presume this applies per unit, not per Location or per player turn.}
This says no MOL use in SFF/FPF. And a unit can't use a MOL in both DFF and Final Fire.

A MOL Check dr counts as use of a SW, ...
Self explanatory: a MOL Check doesn't need to succeed in order for it to count as use of a SW.

A squad which makes a MOL Check dr may not fire any other SW and must add its inherent FP to the attack.
A squad that fires a MOL has to combine the MOL's 4-FP with its Inherent FP. So a squad firing a MOL fully exhausts its fire capabilities (A7.351): 1 SW + Inherent FP.

Further assumptions:
--When a squad uses a MOL, the MOL has to be added to its full Inherent FP. (It can't be added to Inherent FP that is halved as Area Fire because the squad is marked with a First Fire counter.) [a statement refuted by the Perry Sez posted by JRV in the next post]
--A HS that fires anything in DFF cannot try for a MOL in Final Fire. [the correctness of this assumption is pending]

Conclusions:
--A MOL check cannot be made by a unit marked with a First Fire counter. 
--A MOL check cannot be made by a unit that possesses a Gun/SW that is marked by a First Fire counter (this also disqualifies any unit that has used--or has attempted to use--an Inherent SW).
--If a squad fires anything in DFF, it can't use a MOL in Final Fire.
--If a HS fires anything, it can no longer use a MOL.

AFV in INDEX = D1.2 = partially armored is still an AFV

E7.42 = mentions that C7.21 & C7.22 are always used

query:
Hexsides and hindrance, hexsides and mines: 1. If a LOF goes along a wall which happens to be a hindrance hexisde, can a target unit claim both thE wall TEM (if able to) and the hexside hindrance?

2. A unit Advances into a ground level building Location from outside the building. The Defender reveals A-P mines in the Open Ground part of the hex and solves them. Some Attackers survive. The Defender reveals then that the building is Fortified and occuppied to expell the Attackers. Is this correct or were the MF expended outside and the mines should not have attacked? title: Hexsides and hindrance, hexsides and mines
raw_question:
1. If a LOF goes along a wall which happens to be a hindrance hexisde, can a target unit claim both thE wall TEM (if able to) and the hexside hindrance?

2. A unit Advances into a ground level building Location from outside the building. The Defender reveals A-P mines in the Open Ground part of the hex and solves them. Some Attackers survive. The Defender reveals then that the building is Fortified and occuppied to expell the Attackers. Is this correct or were the MF expended outside and the mines should not have attacked? If correct, do the expelled units suffer a second mine attack?

Thanks.
ground_truth_answer:
B.6 INHERENT TERRAIN: Certain terrain depictions (orchard, crag, graveyard, shellholes, etc.) and counter contents of a hex (SMOKE, Bridge, rubble, AFV, wreck) [EXC: Bypass AFV/Wreck (D9.4)] identify the entire hex (inclusive of hexsides) as having the characteristics of that terrain type. It is not necessary that a LOS actually cross such a symbol to be affected—mere entrance of the hex (even if only to trace a LOS to or through a vertex of such a hex) or a LOS exactly along one of its hexsides (A6.1) suffices. A LOS traced exactly along such a hexside is considered to have passed through only one such hex—not two—even if that hexside is shared by another LOS Hindrance hex. If the Hindrance DRM of two such hexes differ, the larger of the two Hindrance DRM is used.

	

B9.3 TEM: The TEM of a wall is +2; the TEM of a hedge is +1. Fire traced through a wall/hedge hexside or hexspine may be subject to a TEM for that wall/hedge if the target is in the Location formed by that hexside/hexspine. If the LOS crosses the wall/hedge hexside through a road depiction (such as 6W9-X9) the wall/hedge TEM can only apply if the target is a non-moving unit. PRC [EXC: Motorcyclists] never receive a TEM for a wall/hedge. The wall/hedge TEM is NA for DC attacks [EXC: if thrown across a wall/hedge hexside, the TEM applies to both the target and thrower’s Locations; A23.6].

	

B9.31 The wall/hedge TEM is not cumulative with positive TEM of other terrain in that hex, although it is cumulative with LOS Hindrances and SMOKE. A target unit claiming WA (9.32) does not receive in-hex TEM [EXC: Runway (7.3); Air Bursts (9.34)], but receives wall/hedge TEM if applicable [EXC: it may elect instead to receive appropriate TEM for Emplacement or for a friendly AFV with which it shares WA (D9.3)]. A target unit not claiming WA receives only in-hex TEM, but may instead use wall/hedge TEM vs enemy units which do not have WA over the hexside. In any case the wall/hedge TEM applies on as per 9.3. In order for a wall to justify firing HEAT at Infantry/Cavalry (C3.81), those units must be claiming-WA/receiving-Wall-TEM. The amount of Residual FP left by an attack that crosses a wall/hedge hexside is reduced by that hexside TEM (A8.26) if hexside TEM could have been claimed against at least one firing unit—even if the moving unit is not claiming hexside TEM. See 9.36 and D4 for wall-TEM/HD-status for vehicles.

query: Sunken road (hex 41W7): What does it cost for infantry to move from W7 to V6? Is it an abrupt elevation change (first up, then down)?
title: Sunken road (hex 41W7)
raw_question: What does it cost for infantry to move from W7 to V6? Is it an abrupt elevation change (first up, then down)?
ground_truth_answer:
I'm going to have to disagree with the consensus.

COT is the cost to enter the hex, not leave it.

B4.41 Infantry/Cavalry entering a Sunken Road hex through a non-road hexside do so at a cost of two MF. There is no cost for leaving a Sunken Road hex other than the normal penalties (10.4) for moving to higher elevation.

When moving to V6, you are not moving to a higher elevation, so the cost would be 2 MF.  While moving from W7 to V7 would be 4MF (2MF doubled).

Check out the B10.5 Abrupt Elevation Change examples I listed above that are also "same level."

12Y4/Y5 is gully to gully with no connecting hexside, so up-down.**

15BB8/AA9 is level 2 hill to level 2 hill with a level 1 "slice" along the hexside, so down-up.

Like 41W7/V6 these both start and end at the same level, but still meet the definition of AEC because the unit "enters two or more levels while crossing one non-cliff hexside."  Net elevation change doesn't matter, only the gross number of levels changed, be they all up, all down or up/down or down/up.   (Think of it as absolute value rather than net value if that helps you)

Another gotcha on this...  If you were playing this with snow, you'd have to pay twice on that hexside because you've changed elevation twice.  There are a couple spots in AP23 Agony at Arnautovo where movement gets really ugly on account of this*.

*I just really read Roundhill's post...he already said this.  Tip o' the cap, sorry for scan-read, Roundhill.

**Also noted by Roundhill, this is explicitly shown in B19.4 and is highly analogous.

S

Each group (or stack) of aircraft beneath a CC/Melee counter is termed a Dogfight.

Comment: I underlined what I think let's both players do this. But, let's give 3 FBs to both sides. Player A wants to form three 1 on 1 Dogfights. Player B wants to gang up 3 to 1 and leave the other 2 planes alone for now. Which player's decision takes precedence? You can't please both because of the definition of a Dogfight (a stack of aircraft under a CC counter).

I think this could be the main problem of this whole mess. If only the ATTACKER could form the Dogfights then it would be neat and simple.

Step 2, resolve the Dogfights (E7.22 continues)
In each CCPh, the ATTACKER's aircraft in each Dogfight attacks one enemy plane in that Dogfight in sequential CC. All ATTACKER planes resolve their attacks (including any additional attacks allowed by retained ROF; 7.222) before any surviving DEFENDER plane can return fire. The DEFENDER'S plane cannot attack back if eliminated.

Also E7.221 DOGFIGHT RESOLUTION:
Aircraft in each Dogfight must predesignate their initial targets (ATTACKER first); i.e., a plane may not await the outcome of earlier attacks in its Dogfight to determine which opposing plane in that Dogfight to attack. A plane can attack only one opposing plane at a time -- regardless of the number of enemy planes in that Dogfight.

Comment: I underlined what I think reinforces that this whole process takes two steps. In step 1 Dogfights are formed, in step 2 each Dogfight is resolved separately, Attacker first.

(Step 3, which handles the outcomes of these Dogfights, would come next but is irrelevant to this discussion)
As written, the phrase "a player" combined with "the CCph" instead of "his CCph" is clear. Either player. The rules, including earlier in E7.2, consistently use "a player" and "his" to mean ATTACKER. 

Allowing both players makes sense game-wise as it allows defending FBs a chance to intercept enemy bombers before they can drop their load. (Not an argument this is correct, just a possible reason why the rule might be intended this way). Unfortunately that leaves the glaring hole of possible conflicting assignments with nothing I can see in the rules to help.

It's possible this is a mistake in the rules and it's supposed to be "his CCph". That would fix the assignment problem.

Either way there is a flaw in the rules:
If E7.22 is correct as written then there was an oversight in not specifying whether ATTACKER or DEFENDER assigns first. DEFENDERs do get a chance to intercept new planes before they can make ground attacks.

If E7.22 should say "his CCph" instead of "the CCph" then the written rule is incorrect but there is no need for further clarification. DEFENDERS do not get a chance to intercept new planes before they can make ground attacks.

In the absence of a clear statement of error I prefer to assume the written rule is correct and that a side-effect (possible assignment conflicts) was overlooked do to its rarity.

Until an official clarification I would play ATTACKER declares first because it is their turn, and they are resolving first so seem to have initiative as it were. No rule basis for that. If argued I would dice for it.

One more thing...what about an IFT shot an open-topped, armored vehicle?  

Armored vehicle means IFT shot has no effect on the vehicle itself.
If the crew is CE, the IFT shot will affect them with their CE TEM, usually +2.

5.31 CE DRM: ...An OT AFV’s normal (usually +2) CE DRM can be reduced by Elevation Effects as per 6.61, and by Air Bursts (B13.3); see 5.311....

5.311 UNPROTECTED CREWS: The Inherent crew (as well as each Passenger) of a vehicle receiving fire (including Fire Lane Residual FP) [EXC: Sniper attack] through an unarmored Target Facing/Aspect (C3.9; including any OT AFV receiving either Air Bursts or fire from a higher elevation whose elevation advantage is > the range [5.31]—and, vs mines, the PRC of any AFV with a hull AF of 0 [B28.43]) is Vulnerable even if BU, and receives no (or a reduced; 5.31) CE DRM. Consequently the crew is not susceptible to Stun/Recall from such an attack; it is instead subject to PTC/MC/K/KIA results. If it breaks it must rout from the vehicle using normal Infantry rout procedures [EXC: it expends all its initial-RtPh MF to be placed beneath the vehicle]. In this event, the +2 CE DRM applies but is reduced by one for each full level elevation advantage > the range (to a minimum CE DRM of 0) as per 5.31, and even BU Passengers may return fire...

Again that friendly Gunflash. Does this mean that if only one side has fired a shot, then only that side can be affected by the Jitter Fire?

I'd say 5 MF from I11 (4 + 1 for elevation change through an unplowed road hexside but + 0 for entering a concealment terrain through a road hexside), and 6 MF if entered from J10 (no 4 + 1 + 1).

query: The roads in A5/A6 and GG5/GG6: Where are the roads in these hexes supposed to be? In only one hex, in both hexes...? My question arises from entering units from off-map from these hexes, as I'm not sure if I can use the road for both hexes or only one of them.
title: The roads in A5/A6 and GG5/GG6
raw_question: Where are the roads in these hexes supposed to be? In only one hex, in both hexes...? My question arises from entering units from off-map from these hexes, as I'm not sure if I can use the road for both hexes or only one of them.
ground_truth_answer:
2.51 OFFBOARD SETUP: Units designated by a scenario as having to enter the mapboard (rather than setting up on it) must still be set up offboard on the turn of entry as the first act of the RPh of that Player Turn. This is done by placing any randomly chosen unused board(s) adjacent to the mapboard edge(s) the ATTACKER’s units are to enter. The offboard player then places all forces scheduled to arrive during that turn on any whole hex(es). If only part of a board is in play, only the actual road hexes on the unused portion are “off board” road hexes. Fire and LOS between the mapboard and any setup board is not allowed (including the overlapping Blast Area of a FFE). However, offboard units may move normally on the offboard map so as to enter the mapboard on a hex which is not adjacent to the one they set up in, provided they were not scheduled to enter via a specified hex which is not blocked. All terrain on an offboard setup map is considered Open Ground except for off-map half-hexes which are butted against a half-hex of some other terrain type and hex rows Y, Q, and I which are road hexes if the board is butted lengthwise. If the board is butted widthwise, all offboard hexes with a coordinate of 5 are considered road hexes. Roads share the same status as the majority of on-board roads of the adjacent board (i.e., paved, plowed, or muddy). Entrance of an offboard setup hex on the way to entering the mapboard always costs the standard Open Ground MF/MP rate per hex (or standard road movement rate if on a road) except where scenario weather conditions increase the cost of such basic movement.

Only hexes on the offboard map (when aligned so that the A or GG edge is being entered from) with a coordinate of 5 are considered road hexes, so you could use either of the 'on board' (GG5/6, A5/6) hexes as road hexes, but only units which had set up or entered from the 'offboard B/FF-5 hex' would be able to claim road rate.

So both 5 & 6 hexes on map are road hexes, then, and as the share a road depiction in their hexside I could go from one of them to the other one as using the road.

query:
US M5 76.2 mm AT gun Notes Please: Hi All

Looking at a scenario with the above gun in it and do not have the Chp H notes. Could someone please post a summary?

Thanks in advance
title: US M5 76.2 mm AT gun Notes Please
raw_question:
Hi All

Looking at a scenario with the above gun in it and do not have the Chp H notes. Could someone please post a summary?

Thanks in advance
ground_truth_answer:
While the M1 57mm AT gun was being developed in 1941, the Army also decided to start work on a more powerful weapon. To bring it into production as quickly as possible, the designers used the barrel of the 3-in. (76mm) AA gun and the carriage, breech and recoil mechanisms of the 105mm howitzer. The result was rather large and heavy for an AT gun (its weight in action was almost twice that of the German 7,5cm PaK 40), but it worked better than might have been expected from such an improvisation. However, while the M3 3-in. AA gun and the M7 3-in. gun of the M10 GMC had semiautomatic breech blocks, the M5 had a manual breech block which lowered its rate of fire. 2500 were built before production ended in 1944. The M5 was not used as a divisional AT gun but rather in tank destroyer battalions (towed), with four guns (each towed by an M3 halftrack) per platoon. In early 1945 most towed battalions were converted to SP, making the towed gun relatively rare in the last few month of the war. Since the M5 3-in. was used solely in towed TD battalions it was sometimes referred to as a tank destroyer instead of an AT gun. Apparently it was not used in the PTO.

APCR is not available in Italy.

RF for use in the ETO (other than Italy) is 1,3 for 6-8/44,  1,2 for 9/44 - 2/45,  and 1,4 for 3-5/45.

Dates and RF for use in Italy are 11/44 - 5/45 and 1,4.

The gun was not used by U.S. forces in the PTO.

query:
CC, rolling Snake-eyes and effect: Hi,here's the situation:
2 German units locked in melee with 2 Dutch units. No ambush, so both sides roll at same time. Germans roll under kill number but dutch roll snake-eyes (double 1). We re-read rules but I don't think we played it right...

Our result: Dutch kill germans (and created 7-0 leader) and instantly retreat. As is allowed by my reading of the rules. Germans score zip as the Dutch withdraw (as per rules sorry NRBH while Germans don't kill as they are know alone in hex. 

Is this right, my gut says no!
title: CC, rolling Snake-eyes and effect
raw_question:
Hi,here's the situation:
2 German units locked in melee with 2 Dutch units. No ambush, so both sides roll at same time. Germans roll under kill number but dutch roll snake-eyes (double 1). We re-read rules but I don't think we played it right...

Our result: Dutch kill germans (and created 7-0 leader) and instantly retreat. As is allowed by my reading of the rules. Germans score zip as the Dutch withdraw (as per rules sorry NRBH while Germans don't kill as they are know alone in hex. 

Is this right, my gut says no!
ground_truth_answer:
I know it can be a bit hazy. I used to play this wrong because I had learned a bad habbit from Starter Kits and that was rolling the dice simultaneously in CC. You're not supposed to do that. The ATTACKER rolls first so the result to your question depends which one was the ATTACKER. Here's what I wrote in my SKs to ASL guide:

If your CC DR is 2 or your opponent's CC DR is 12, you may immediately withdraw from the CC/Melee. 

Infiltration momentarily suspends the simultaneous nature of the CC, so what happens next depends on if you’re the ATTACKER or the DEFENDER (remember, the ATTACKER rolls first even in a simultaneous CC).
- First, remember to resolve the possible Field Promotion. (A18.12)
- If the ATTACKER rolls 2 he must first choose if he wants to withdraw before the DEFENDER resolves his attack. If he does, the DEFENDER does not get a change to strike back. That DR of 2 is still resolved against the DEFENDER but even if the DEFENDER was eliminated the ATTACKER does not gain control of that CC location. 
- If the DEFENDER rolls 2, he must suffer the ATTACKER’s roll first regardless.
- If the ATTACKER rolls 12, the DEFENDER does not roll for his attack if he chooses to withdraw.
- If the DEFENDER rolls 12, the ATTACKER’s roll is still resolved even if he chooses to withdraw.

So, if Dutch was the Attacker he would have to make a decision before seeing what German rolls. He would either kill Germans, then withdraw immediately or kill the Germans and stay but then the Germans would get a change to roll too and in this case both would have died.

If Dutch were the defender, both would have died because the German rolled first.

The German reveals a Fortified building location and claims that the FP of the first shot wasn't actually enough for NMC, thus no Encirclement.

But, is it too late for the German now because he didn't reveal the additional TEM for the first shot? I'm not sure if there exists some rule that prevents "tinkering the past".

My opinion: No Encirclement for obvious logical reasons, but I just read a Series Replay where Encirclement was placed in this kind of situation but it could have been just that in the 1st ed. rules maybe there were no requirement for NMC and any amount of FP was enough? title: Can claiming TEM of a Fortified building location nullify earlier shots that contributed to the Encircling attempt retroactively?
raw_question:
Good luck trying to decipher the subject lol.

Situation: German squad in a stone building. Russian 447 shoots at it and rolls something high. The German yawns. Then a Russian 627 shoots from the other side and claims that the German is now Encircled. The German reveals a Fortified building location and claims that the FP of the first shot wasn't actually enough for NMC, thus no Encirclement.

But, is it too late for the German now because he didn't reveal the additional TEM for the first shot? I'm not sure if there exists some rule that prevents "tinkering the past".

My opinion: No Encirclement for obvious logical reasons, but I just read a Series Replay where Encirclement was placed in this kind of situation but it could have been just that in the 1st ed. rules maybe there were no requirement for NMC and any amount of FP was enough? Probably the case but still got me thinking about this question.
ground_truth_answer:
I agree with Spencer.

It seems blatantly obvious to me that A23.911 unambiguously states that the existence of the FB is revealed when *it is fired upon*  and it would change a result of said attack.  Negation of encirclement is a change to the result of said attack.  Merely announcing an attack is not actually making the attack.

From a common sense standpoint I would play that it is not encirclement and you can reveal the FB after the second attack die roll. I do not think it is obvious that the rules support this. 

It can be argued that when you try to prevent the encirclement during the second attack (the one that finished encirclement) you are trying to change the effect of the previous attack from "was enough to start encirclement" to "was not enough to start encirclement". Changing the effect of the previous attack is not allowed by B23.911.

It could even be argued that encirclement is not changing the effect of an attack since no single attack causes it. It is an effect of multiple attacks combined, in which case B23.911 does not apply.

Edit: changed A23.911 to B23.911

There are a few cases where the targeted player knows something the the firing player doesn't.

-Concealed unit with a FT
-Hidden fortification when E1.16 is in effect (Night & PTO)
-Fortified location

In any of these cases, an attacker makes attacks that may not be what they announce.  If they announce 4+3 against a Fortified Location, the defender knows it's 4+4.  If they call 4+3 against that FT squad, the defender knows it's 4+2.  They may fire into a jungle hex and anncounce 4+1 (or 4+2 for dense) and the defender knows it's 4+2 (foxhole) or 4+3 (wood pillbox) or 4+5 (stone pillbox) or simply not capable of having an effect (NCA of a pillbox).  In any of these cases, the shot is not what the attacker declared it.  That doesn't change what the shot was and it doesn't create a duty for the defending player to reveal unless the result changes. 

If you allow Encirclement because one player said 4+3 and wasn't corrected, do  you have to forfeit the FT or the fortification later because you didn't correct?  Of course not.  The attacker's declaration of the shot isn't relevant, what the shot actually was is all that matters.

Even if you fire into a jungle hex and announce 4+1 (or 4-1 with a 9-2 leader) and you roll snakeyes, your opponent doesn't have to tell you anything about the pillbox whose NCA you just bounced rounds off.  

Stuff only shows up when it changes a result, not a declaration.  The Encirclement result cannot be changed until the sealing shot, so the Fortified Location shows up at that moment and not before.  That first shot was always a 4+4, whoever might not have known it.

S

The Russian player in Red Barricades is buying some dug-in AFV (D9.54). Can he scrounge any MG from the AFVs? BMG, CMG?
Only non-burning wrecks and abandoned vehicles may be scrounged (D10.5), so the Dug-In AFV would first have to be abandoned (and marked with an Abandoned counter). Once abandoned, only the BMG and AAMG (if present) could be scrounged (D10.51).

A Dug-In AFV is considered HD (D9.54), and a HD AFV cannot fire any bow-mounted weapon other than its MA (D4.223), so the BMG cannot be fired.

Can an unarmored but armed vehicle be captured in CC?: According to A11.52, armored vehicles (AFVs) can't be captured unless abandoned. But unarmed vehicles (I'm thinking trucks) can be captured.

But what about unarmored (non-AFV), but armed vehicles?

Is it no, because unarmed is meantioned as allowed, meaning armed must then not be allowed?

Basically, is the gist here that if the vehicle is in any ways armed, then it cannot be captured? I do know that if the vehicle has an Inherent Crew, it's still armed even it all it's weapons are busted (thus, only an Abandoned AFV can be captured like the rule says).

A11.52 CAPTURE OF VEHICLE IN CC: Infantry may not attempt to capture a manned AFV or a Motion/non-stopped vehicle (or its PRC), but may attempt to capture or eliminate an Abandoned AFV as per 21.2. An unarmed, stopped/non-Motion vehicle without Personnel Escort is captured instantly in any CCPh in which it is alone with opposing Infantry. If an unarmored stationary vehicle has Passengers and the attacker wishes to capture (rather than eliminate) the vehicle, he must first attack and eliminate/capture all enemy Personnel in the Location, but must capture any Passengers. If all the Passengers are captured, so is the vehicle. The attacker must engage these Passengers in normal Infantry vs Infantry CC, but is eligible for both a -2 DRM for his attacks vs these Passengers and a +2 DRM in defending against attacks from those Passengers. This -2 DRM is combined with the +1 DRM for attempting to capture these Passengers in CC.

Edit: I missed it first but the rule also speaks about unarmored vehicles with passengers (blue highlight)... so, can an unarmored vehicle without passengers be captured just like that or must it still be unarmed also (meaning inherent driver only)?
title: Can an unarmored but armed vehicle be captured in CC?

query:
Confused about vehicular IFE: 3.5 VEHICULAR MG/IFE FIRE: The MG/IFE armament of a vehicle, unlike a SW counter (A9.2), may make only one fire attack per Player Turn unless it is the vehicle's MA with a specific Multiple ROF, in which case it and its ROF will be listed as the MA in the lower left-hand corner of the counter.

Umm, so can a MA, with ROF 3 and IFE FP in brackets, make multiple attacks or not?
title: Confused about vehicular IFE
raw_question:
3.5 VEHICULAR MG/IFE FIRE: The MG/IFE armament of a vehicle, unlike a SW counter (A9.2), may make only one fire attack per Player Turn unless it is the vehicle's MA with a specific Multiple ROF, in which case it and its ROF will be listed as the MA in the lower left-hand corner of the counter.

Umm, so can a MA, with ROF 3 and IFE FP in brackets, make multiple attacks or not?
ground_truth_answer:
A vehicular MA MG can fire in the MPh until ROF expires, and it is marked with First Fire.
  Only Infantry can Subsequent First Fire, so the vehicular MA MG cannot fire again in the MPh.
  The rule you quote specifically allows the vehicular MA to use Final Fire in the DFPh against an adjacent or same hex unit.

It's always fun to thrash out how these rules interact!

D3.5 VEHICULAR MG/IFE FIRE states, 
"Non-CC vehicular MG fire is limited to the same fire phase (A. 15) as the vehicle's other weapons or that of its PRC; if any weapon is fired from a vehicle, the remaining weapons must fire in the same phase or forfeit their non-CC fire attack opportunity for that Player Turn" 

I've always interpreted this to mean that, other than the listed exceptions for CC, Multiple Overruns and Bounding First Fire, ALL AFV weapons have to fire and complete their fire in the same phase. 

A9.3 does say "Sustained Fire cannot be used by a vehicular MG [EXC: MA, as per 8.4]" and 8.4 says "Any such units/weapons that are marked with a First Fire counter may also fire again (by flipping their First Fire marker over to the Final Fire side), but as Area Fire and only at units in an adjacent (or same) hex"

When it's all added up I believe a MG MA on an AFV can use sustained fire against an adjacent unit in the DFPh but only if all his fire from that AFV took place during that phase. But I don't believe you can fire during the enemy MPh until ROF is exhausted and then use Sustained Fire in the DFPh since D3.5 clearly prohibits firing AFV weapons in multiple phases of the same turn. 

You're incorrect.  D3.5 references A.15.  

A.15 says: Even though Defensive First Fire occurs during the MPh and Defensive Final Fire usually occurs during the DFPh, qualifying units may fire in both without violating the general rule that no unit can fire in more than one phase per Player Turn (7.1).

Therefore, if you keep ROF, you can fire again in DFPh OR if you have a qualifying MA, you can use Sustained Fire in the DFPh (within within the limits of Final Fire).

ground_truth_answer:
Once you get up to +6 in hindrances, you can longer see the unit.  It is considered blocked.
A multi-Location FG which discovers that one or more of its units' LOS is blocked forfeits the participation of only those units whose LOS was blocked. The FG's other units with a valid LOS must still attack the same target (unless it was eliminated by a previous attack, in which case their attack is forfeit and they are marked with an appropriate fire phase counter) after resolving the blocked firer's DR (6.11), but as a smaller FG or as separate attacks. (A7.52) 

Part of the FG has so many hindrances that they no longer have LOS. You have to resolve a separate DR for the blocked guys. Then the rest of the original FG must still attack the target, but without any hindrances from the blocked guys. It also sounds like if there was more than one remaining unit you can decide whether to do separate attacks or a FG as long as they all attack.

I was surprised by this: both that the blocked guys get a separate DR and that you could then choose to break up remaining units instead of still having to go with the FG you originally committed to.

I have never seen this played correctly.  Wow.  Thanks.  I put the sticky errata in there, but, wow, just...always learning.

S

query:
Half Height LOS obstacle  Question: Ok so a friend and I read somewhere that firing through a half-Level LOS obstacle adds +1 to all fire traced through that hex, provided that hex isn't the target. I am unsure though rereading the section. 

Can a unit fire through a half-level LOS obstacle to a unit 1 hex behind said obstacle? 
EX: a unit is a rubble hex. The hex directly in front of that hex is also rubble. Directly in front of that hex is a enemy unit in open ground. Can the unit in the rubble hex fire on the unit in open ground (assume neither has moved)?

Cheers and thanks for your help in advance.
title: Half Height LOS obstacle  Question
raw_question:
Ok so a friend and I read somewhere that firing through a half-Level LOS obstacle adds +1 to all fire traced through that hex, provided that hex isn't the target. I am unsure though rereading the section. 

Can a unit fire through a half-level LOS obstacle to a unit 1 hex behind said obstacle? 
EX: a unit is a rubble hex. The hex directly in front of that hex is also rubble. Directly in front of that hex is a enemy unit in open ground. Can the unit in the rubble hex fire on the unit in open ground (assume neither has moved)?

Cheers and thanks for your help in advance.
ground_truth_answer:
You seem to have some confusion between obstacle and Hindrance. An obstacle blocks LOS, so in your example, LOS is blocked by the rubble between the two units.

However (1): Grain, or brush is a half-level Hindrance. If it was a grain hex in between, there would be a +1 DRM for the Hindrance.

However (2): Half-level obstacles have no effect if there is an elevation difference. If the firing unit was on the first level of a building, and the hex in between was woods (full-level obstacle), LOS would be blocked. Rubble (or any other half-level obstacle or Hindrance) would have no effect in that case.

Per A6.4, a 2 level obstacle creates 2 blind hexes. Per A6.41, one extra blind hex is created due to range (range of 6 divided by 5, FRD). Per A6.42, the gun only has a one level height advantage and so the number of blind hexes is not reduced.

I and my regular FTF opponent use it quite often.

I have never used it at tournaments but playing FTF with friends we always use it. Have been playing for 10 years and played (BI) it starting with Cross of Iron in the original SL starting in 1984.

and I know the bookkeeping is probably a huge PITA...
The "extra bookkeeping" that some players complain about is laughably trivial and easy.

The game actually provides a chart and chits to track the levels. Just requires a quick calculation up front and casualty and reinforcement tracking with the chart and chits.

and it will unbalance the scenarios etc. etc.

I do not know if battlefield integrity is considered when play testing. I think it does affect a scenario. It prohibits you from throwing your troops away. It is part of the experience level rating (ELR) of units which is just another level of morale. It adds nuanced morale if you will, in my opinion. In the old Cross of Iron you counted all BPV for units including leaders and crews and when you took 40% casualties your morale dropped by one, 60% casualties your morale dropped by two, etc.

Sorry about that, I just made a search about BI in GameSquad forums and heard that a lot. :)
Any opinions you get from GameSquad should be treated with some skepticism. The regulars there tend to think that they represent the entire ASL world, which warps their judgment in some matters.

A couple of examples: (A) None of them use Battlefield Integrity, so they automatically assume that *no one* uses BI, which, of course, is wrong. It may not be a popular rule, but certainly some players do use it. (B) There are very few beginners that are active on GameSquad, so they fear that ASL is dying out... but that ignores the fact that BGG is teeming with beginners eager to learn more about the game.

I have played with some old timers and seen them play non-optional rules wrong so I take them with a grain of salt.

But I also learned that a few people love it for the extra immersion it brings.
(raises hand) I'm one of them; I really like the rule and what it adds to the game.

People who play ASL strictly as a form of competition probably won't care for BI, because it rarely has any effect on the outcome of a scenario. On the other hand, people who enjoy ASL because of the vivid "stories" it can generate may find that BI enhances that effect.

I have played a couple of scenarios with and without BI and BI did have an effect. It seemed to balance the scenarios a little more in my opinion. (Pavlov's House from Valor of the Guards being one of them.)

I've seen scenarios where one side starts with less than 10 squads but gets more later via reinforcements. And it has a BPV value on the scenario sheet meaning it's intended to be used.

The question is:
In that situation, is the BI in use right from the start or does the rule "kick in" when the reinforcements arrive and brings the MMC total over 10?
Can you give some specific scenarios where this occurs? Offhand, I don't recall seeing anything like that.

An example is Sacrifice of Polish Armor (Germans versus Poles). The Poles start with 8 squads on board and a BI of (0). They get more squads as the game progresses. My take on this is that as soon as the total squads (counting from the original without casualties) added in hits 10 or more BI kicks in. Since no casualties have been counted the Integrity Base starts with no casualities. I interpret this from the example in the rule book. So using this method the Poles have 8 elite squads starting. The BPV is 96 (8 squads times 12 point BPV per squad). Say they get the first reinforcement (they get two in random selection order), it has 4 elite squads. They would now have an integrity base of 15 (96+48=144x10% FRU). They would start with the 15 base on the turn that they get reinforcements. My "immersion" interpretation of this is as follows. The ELR of both Germans and Poles is 3. With this method the ELR of the Poles becomes something more like 3.33. This would be in keeping with the quality of the Polish army troops. They were actually better trained troops. They lost because of the quality of German army operational doctrine put into place effectively.

In general, even though I like to use BI, I only use it on big scenarios where it will affect both sides. I don't care to use it when it only affects one side.

We also play cloaking not concealment:cool:. All this explaining why I have very few friends:robot:

Not trying to butt in but wanted to weigh in with my experiences. I think this thread is great and is the best I have found on the net on the topic other than "I don't use it".

ground_truth_answer:
The Index is your friend : it not only gives rules ref. numbers, but global definitions too.

Here is the definition of the US# in the Index:

US#: (Unit Size Number; SMC: 1, Crew/HS: 2, Squad: 3, 5/8" counter: 4, Large vehicle or Gun/its manning Infantry: 5)

Here is the full rule
A1.6 UNIT SIZE NUMBER (US#): Each unit has an inherent Unit Size Number which approximates its relative size in terms of bulk, number of men, and/or difficulty to conceal which is used for certain rules (Concealment, 12.12; Guarding Prisoners, 20.5; Set DC, 23.7). Personnel units have a US# equal to the number of silhouettes on their counter (SMC: 1; Crew/HS: 2; Squad: 3). Horses and all other 5/8" counters have a US# of 4 as do their Riders or attendant crews [EXC: Any vehicle or Gun classified as large or very large (red , AF, or M#) has a US# of 5].

A guy spends hundreds of dollars on ASL products and he literally has no access to the most current rules unless he goes to ebay and spends big money on OOP modules?

query:
From Starter Kits to full ASL. A comprehensive list of rules you need to learn: Click for a Printer Friendly view

Introduction

This article is meant for people moving from ASL Starter Kits to full ASL, to help them in their quest to learn the full ASL rules. It lists all the new rules, and rules that have changed from Starter Kits, that apply to every scenario. In addition to all mandatory new rules (like Concealment) it also lists all the new optional maneuvers available (like the Bypass move).

If you are here just to get a general sense of what the full system might be offering over SKs, I recommend turning to these great articles instead, by Jay Richardson. He does a better job selling the system and lists game features I won't mention in my article:
The Next Step
The Next Step (Part 2)

Obviously this is not a list of all things ASL. I'm not going talk anything about Deep Snow or Air Support because those are Scenario Special Rules (SSRs) and wouldn't apply to every scenario. The same goes for all the new terrain features you'll come across.

This list aims to be comprehensive list of all the new concepts but not a very detailed one. You cannot use this as a replacement for the rulebook nor does this offer any answers to specific rule disputes, such as whether a unit must be Good Ordered or just Unbroken, to be able to do something.
I started this list by listing every single requirement and exception until I realized I was basically rewriting the rulebook, just with bullet points instead of paragraphs. 
What I've done instead is, I give a general summary about all the new rules, maybe with some commonly forgotten rules tips thrown in there, and a more detailed treatment for rules that have changed from SKs. To learn all the specifics you'll have to dig deeper yourself.

How you use this is up to you. I can imagine this will be helpful after you've read Chapter A and your head is spinning and you just want a nice summary of everything new.
Or you can use this to teach a friend who is moving from Starter Kits, to help him learn what's new.
Or this can be helpful during a game when you're pondering about all the new movement options you have available. If this article gives you the "Ah, now I remember" feeling, then I consider it a success.

I've structured this in a similar manner (not identical though) to Starter Kits' Order of (Rules) Presentation. This way it's easier for Starter Kit people to quickly remind themselves of what's new in different phases, for example.

Since there are three Starter Kits, each adding new concepts, so will this article be divided into three parts, each adding to the previous one:

Part 1 is aimed for people moving from Starter Kit 1, but is also a required read for SK2 and SK3 people. It lists all that's new to basic Infantry battles but does not say a word about Ordnance or Vehicle rules since, for Starter Kit 1 people, everything about those are obviously new.
Part 2 is aimed for people moving from Starter Kit 2. It lists what's new to Guns and Ordnance rules.
Part 3 is aimed for people moving from Starter Kit 3. It lists what's new to Vehicle rules.

Parts 2 and 3 do not exist yet.

About formatting

:star: = The rule is new.
:halfstar: = The rule is different from Starter Kit rules or something important is added so it plays different.
Colored rule = This rule is optional, usually something you can do in a game if you want. You can forget all the colored rules during a game and still not play anything wrong.
Below a rule there might be a link to a relevant Play Aid

Any and all suggestions and contributions are highly welcome. Not only error corrections and rules I've missed, but I'm also interested in hearing about commonly forgotten rules from people who have made the jump.

Grammatic or "bad english" corrections are also welcome but I'd rather take them via geekmail.

You can contact me directly via geekmail or email: msohlman at msn dot com
