ground_truth_answer:
Part 1

What's changed from Starter Kit 1

A couple new terms first

TC (Task Check) (A10.1)
Sometimes, to be able to do some action, you need to pass a TC. You're already familiar with the PTC (Pin Task Check) and possibly the LLTC (Leader Loss Task Check) although not by that name in SK1. But there are others. A NTC (Normal Task Check), for example, is needed when Deploying. Failure to pass a NTC just means that the unit is done for the rest of that phase.

Sustained Fire (A9.3)
A MG firing in Subsequent First Fire, or FPF, is called Sustained Fire. The effect (B# decreases by two) remains the same.

Major new Concepts

:star: Concealment (A12)
Concealment basically represents "unknown" or, if you like, "fog of war". It's an integral concept to full ASL and scenarios are often won or lost based on how well you manage concealment.

Here's a brief overview:
- Units with "?" on top of them are concealed.
- There may be Dummy stacks that only contain further "?" counters under the top one. There can also be dummies in a stack with real units.
- Concealed units are not Known units so pay attention. It affects, for example, routing paths.
- Infantry FP is halved for Area Fire against concealed units.
- Concealment has a big effect on ambush an CC, and it grants other benefits as well.
- Concealment can be lost and later gained again.

Hidden Initial Placement (HIP) (A12.3)
- HIP is a form of concealment but instead of being under "?" the units are totally hidden and are not placed on board until revealed.
- HIP only applies to Guns unless invoked by SSR. It's mentioned here because other new rules in this article may refer to HIP units.

:star: Snipers (A14)
Snipers are another totally new thing to full ASL. They are kind of an uncontrollable random nuisance that always seem to nail your best leaders at the worst possible times and they are present in practically every scenario. Be sure to read the Sniper footnote (20) to appreciate why they work like they work.

Overview:
- Most of the scenarios mention something like "SAN: 4" That's your Sniper Activation Number. Your Sniper activates when your opponent rolls that number.
- Important: Snipers can only activate in PFPh, MPh, DFPh and AFPh, but not all DRs count; Only TH, MC, TC, IFT (non-OBA) or entrenching DRs do. (A14.1)
- You can forfeit an effective Sniper attack and instead just move it to a better position. (A14.2)
- If a Sniper attacks you, remember you can try to "eliminate" that Sniper by making a Sniper Check. It doesn't actually remove the Sniper from the game, only reduces its SAN by one. (A14.4)

:star: Heat of Battle (A15)
One of the most fun features of full ASL is the possibility of Heat of Battle. It happens when you roll 2 on any Morale Check or Rally attempt (not on self-rally though, you can get leaders in those if you remember.)

A subsequent DR determines what happens next. Here's an overview again:
:cool: 0-6 = Hero Creation
- Heroes are SMCs similar to Leaders, except they can shoot!
- A MMC can generate a Hero or a leader can become Heroic.
- A Hero doesn't Pin or Cower. It grants -1 Heroic DRM (even to a multi-hex FG!) and is just an all-around bad-ass.

:arrrh: 5-8 = Battle Hardening
- A Battle Hardening improves that unit's Class. So a 2nd line MMC becomes 1st line MMC and so on.
- If a unit cannot be promoted anymore it becomes Fanatic (+1 to Morale and other good jazz (A10.8)).

:angry: 9-11 = Berserk
- Berserk units are out of control. They get some benefits like a godly 10 morale but will recklessly rush straight at the closest enemy.
- If a Berserk unit gets his hands on prisoners, the prisoners will die causing No Quarter and Massacre!

:soblue: 12 = Surrender
- The unit breaks if not broken already and becomes Disrupted. Then it immediately surrenders to an ADJACENT enemy unit if present.
- As you see, Heat of Battle can be detrimental as well.

:star: Prisoners (A20)
Yes, you can take prisoners in ASL. Prisoners grant you Victory Points and you can even make them do some forced labor for you. You can also easily forfeit all this prisoner stuff by invoking No Quarter.

There are three ways to capture prisoners:
- During RtPh when the broken unit cannot safely rout away. (A20.21)
- In CC/Melee by announcing a capture attempt before dice are rolled. +1 DRM to CC DR. (A20.22)
- When Mopping Up a building, broken units are prone to surrender. (A12.153)

Massacre (A20.4)
- Some factions can, and Berserk units will, commit a Massacre by shooting prisoners.
- In addition to causing No Quarter it also raises the ELR of your opponent units by one!

Guards (A20.5)
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 14
- The unit receiving prisoners becomes a guard.
- Not to be confused with Russian Guards (Russian elite units).
- A squad can immediately split into 2 HS leaving the other HS to guard the prisoners. Hint: This is the only way for Russians to Deploy voluntarily.
- A guard can force its prisoners to dig foxholes or Clear rubble/flame/etc.
- A guard can have more prisoners than its own US# (Unit Strength) (max 5 times more), but then it cannot shoot outside its own hex.

Escape (A20.55)
- Prisoners can try to escape during Melee, although they cannot start a CC with the guard unless it's broken.

No Quarter (A20.3)
You can ignore all these prisoner rules by simply refusing to take prisoners. If it's your first game and your head is already hurting from all these new rules, just declare No Quarter and it is Starter Kit rules all over again.
- When an enemy unit is about to surrender, you can immediately declare No Quarter and eliminate the about-to-surrender unit instead.
- Subsequent enemy units will never surrender for the rest of the game.
- Does not cause Massacre.

While it may sound tempting to ignore all the prisoner rules, know that there are two advantages to taking prisoners:
- Victory Point advantage. Every prisoner counts as double VCs.
- Limiting your opponent's routing possibilities. Prisoner rules make it easier for you to deal with opponents units because they must surrender to you if they cannot rout without either taking Interdiction or using Low Crawl. However No Quarter risks that, instead of surrendering, the enemy will successfully rout away, rally, and come back later to haunt you.

:star: Fire, Smoke and Weather (A24) (B25)
Flame/Blaze
Weather
Fires can be set deliberately (Kindling), or by accident as a result of combat (High Explosives and Flame throwers mainly). They start as small Flames that can be extinguished but can quickly grow into Blazes which in turn can spread new Flames.
- Fires can be kindled in PFPh and they grow/spread in AFPh.
- Blazing location makes that location inaccessible.

Where there's fire, there's SMOKE. Those big Smoke counters are used for smoke emitting from Blazing locations (also SMOKE fired by Ordnance). The gray Smoke counters marks drifting SMOKE.
- The level of the smoke means it rises up to that level but not into that level. So level 2 smoke doesn't affect units in a level 2 building location.

Weather usually doesn't play a major role in a scenario. It's considered clear (which affects nothing) unless otherwise specified in which case consult Chapter E3.

Environmental Conditions (EC) and Wind on the other hand can affect fire and smoke.
The main thing is to remember to roll for Wind Change at the start of every RPh.
- Wind affects SMOKE placement attempts and causes drifting SMOKE. It also helps spread fires.
- EC such as Dry or Wet affects how easily fires can be started and how easily they spread.

When the EC is dry and/or there's some mild breeze, consider using fire and smoke to your advantage!

What's changed on the Mapboards

:star: Look out for Rowhouses (B23.71)
A thick black bar between multihex building hexes means it's a Rowhouse with its own rules.
- Basically you can't move directly through the wall from one house to another but instead must pay 3 MF and go around the outside of the building, possibly having to take FFMO etc.

:star: Those little black circles (B8.1)
Sewers
Those are manholes, used for sewer movement. Sewer movement is only allowed by SSR so don't worry about them.

:halfstar: Buildings have multiple stories (B23)
Single hex buildings have only a single story, just like in Starter Kits.

Multihex buildings without a Stairwell symbol (white square) are automatically 2 story houses. They have both ground level and level 1. (B23.22)
- You can switch stories for 1 MF at any building hex.

Any building with a Stairwell symbol (white square) has 3 stories (ground, level 1 and level 2). (B23.23)
- You can switch stories for 1 MF only at Stairwell hexes.

:halfstar: Orchards in Season (B14.2)
- Orchards are in season through April-October.
- They block LOS to/from higher elevation.
- See also Orchard Road. (B14.6)

:halfstar: Plowed fields (B15.6)
- During April-May Grain does not grow but the Grain hexes are plowed. This means the movement penalty is 1.5 MF, but otherwise it's considered Open Ground.

:halfstar: A hex and a Location (A2.8)
Location Primer
A single hex may have many locations. Building stories are a good example. This is important.
- For example there may be Germans and Russians in the same hex but on different levels, therefore there's no Close Combat in that hex.

When you encounter other new features not seen in Starter Kit maps, look them up in Chapter B.

What's new with Line of Sight

:star: Different Levels (A6.2)
LOS Aid Sheet
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 13
Obstacles have different heights, thus you need to be higher than them to see over them.
- Walls and Hedges are 1/2 level obstacles. They block your LOS at ground level but you can ignore them if you're on level 1 or higher (Meaning in a 2-story house or on a level 1 hill. (A6.21)
- Single story houses and woods are level 1 obstacles. If you're on Level 1 you can just see over them but not what's behind them at ground level.
- Multihex buildings are usually 1 1/2 or 2 1/2 level obstacles. You need to be at least Level 2 to see the ground level behind a 1 or 1 1/2 level obstacle, but even then they have at least 1 or more Blind Hexes right behind them which you cannot see. (A6.4)

LOS between levels and blind hexes can be a bit difficult at the start so I recommend watching Russ Gifford's ASL Session 4: LOS or doing the LOS Course at Chapter K.

:halfstar: LOS to some other point than the hex center dot (A6.12)
Sometimes you can shoot at a different point of a hex rather than the center dot. Here's the list:
- Infantry crossing a Road Hexside. (A4.132)
- Bypass. (A4.32)
- Snap Shot. (A8.15)
- Movement between Rowhouses. (B23.71)
- Climbing (if the map has Cliffs). (B11.42)
- Underbelly Hits (against tanks). (D4.3))

:halfstar: Free LOS Checks
LOS checks are no longer strictly restricted to attack declarations only:
- The Scenario Defender (see Index, it's not as simple as the term suggests) can make free LOS checks before setup. (A6.11)
- If a concealed units moves into LOS of your units it can lose its concealment. This means you can make free LOS checks anytime a concealed unit moves and you think there might be LOS to it. Thus, some players forfeit concealment voluntarily just to deny their opponent any free LOS checks. (A12.14)

:halfstar: Two LOS hindrance hexes at the same range to the firer (A6.7)
Clarification:
- If LOS goes through two hexes that are at the same range to the firer, only one of those hexes counts (the one with the highest hindrance if applicable).

New stuff you can do in Setup

:star: Deploy half-squads (A2.9)
You can split 10% of your starting squads (FRU) into 2 HS if you want to. But not if you're Russian.

:star: Bore Sighting (C6.4)
If you're the Scenario Defender (again, see Index) and you have MMGs or HMGs (or light mortars, guns or tanks), you may choose a Bore Sighted Location for each MG. Secretly record which weapon sighted which hex.
- If the enemy moves into that hex and you respond by shooting with a Bore Sighted weapon, you get -2 DRM at that hex which is cumulative with FFMO/FFNAM. 
- However this bonus is available only for Defensive First Fire meaning you won't get this for Prep Fire or even Defensive Fire. This restriction only applies to MGs (and IFE capable guns) so be sure to revisit C6.4 when using Guns and other Bore Sighted weapons.

New stuff related to Fire Attacks

:star: Encirclement (A7.7)
If you fire two or more consecutive shots at the target from normal range from different directions (even above/below) the target might be encircled. Consult the helpful diagram in chapter A7.7.
- Encirclement also occurs immediately when guys are at the upper levels of the building and all the staircases are blocked by enemy units. (A7.72)
- The effects are: -1 to morale, +1 DRM to shooting, MF cost is doubled for first location moved, and easier capture. (A20.21)

:star: Triple Point Blank Fire (TPBF) (A7.21)
In case you ever find yourself in the same location with an enemy unit, and it's your fire phase and you are not in Melee, you can shoot at it with tripled FP.

:star: Spraying Fire (A7.34) (A9.5)
A MG or a squad with an underlined range can use Spraying Fire.
- Targets two locations that are next to each other instead of one. Can shoot vertically as well.
- The firepower is halved for both locations.
- For a squad the maximum range of Spraying Fire is 3 hexes. An MG has no such limit.
- A single DR covers both hexes. Do not roll separately for each.

New stuff you can do in different Phases
ASL Phases Quick Reference

Different phases are color coded in ASL. The text colors on the counters match phases where they are flipped or removed. If you ever wondered why a Pin counter is red, that's because it's removed at the end of CCPh. (A.12)

Rally Phase (RPh)

:star: Wind Change DR (B25.65)
Remember to do this at the start of every RPh.
- DR 2 may affect the wind and DR 12 causes Gusts and collapses Blazing buildings.

:star: Deployment (A1.31)
- A leader can try to make a squad in the same location split into two HS.
- Only ATTACKER has this option in a RPh.
- The squad needs to pass a NTC.
- Russians cannot do this!

:star: Recombine (A1.32)
- A leader can combine two HS in the same location into 1 full squad.
- Both players can do this in a RPh.
- No TC needed.

Prep Fire Phase (PFPh)

:star: Kindling (B25.11)
Flame/Blaze
Any infantry unit with a leader can try to start fires in a location.

:star: Entrenching (B27.11)
Your squads can try digging themselves some foxholes. This is called entrenching.
- It can take several turns to work. Russians are better with shovels.

:star: Opportunity Fire (A7.25)
Instead of shooting with full FP now, you can actually prepare to shoot your full FP in AFPh by declaring Opportunity Fire.
- Mark the unit with a Bounding Fire counter.
- Naturally no shooting or movement is allowed until AFPh.
- This is SK2+ stuff, but with Opportunity Fire you can avoid Backblast. (C13.8)

:star: Mopping Up (A12.153)
Mopping Up is a procedure usually used to deal with the last remaining broken enemy units in a building so that you can secure the whole building for yourself. It can also be used as an alternative to Searching if you suspect there are hidden units or dummies in a building.
- Mopping up cannot be used if there are unconcealed unbroken enemy units in a building or if No Quarter is in play.
- Hidden units are placed on the board with "?". Dummies are removed. Concealed units can keep their concealment.
- If no Concealed units remain, any broken enemy units there will surrender immediately to an unit of your choice regardless of their proximity. You now control the whole building and all its hexes and locations.
- Be wary of Search Casualties (below).

:star: Search Casualties (A12.154)
If a Location is Searched (in MPh, below) or Mopped Up, and it contains enemy units or some other nasty surprises, some casualties may occur to the searching units.

Movement Phase (MPh)

:star: Bypass (A4.3)
Bypass allows you to move through Woods and Buildings without actually entering them. The rule portrays going around them. This is important as it allows you to move much faster than in the SKs.
- You can bypass Woods or Buildings only.
- You pay only the costs for the other terrain on that hex, usually 1 MF for Open Ground. Unless you bypass more than 2 hexsides in which case the cost is doubled.
- Be careful though, the enemy can shoot at you while you're in the open with FFMO and FFNAM.
- If the scenario allows you to exit the board, you can use bypass. In that case pay 1 extra MF in addition to the bypass cost. (A2.6)
- Learn it and love it. 

:star: Dash (A4.63)
Because of the hex system, roads in ASL are way wider than they realistically should be. To simulate the actual narrowness of a road, the Dash rule allows your guys to quickly run across a street from "cover to cover" giving the enemy only a small chance to react.
- Only across a road and only from non-OG to non-OG.
- Costs all MFs.
- The enemy gets to shoot at you only with 1/2 FP.

:star: Minimum Move (A4.134)
If your guys start with at least 1 MF (after reducing all the Portage Points) you can always move 1 hex even if it would cost you more MFs than you actually have. 
- Place under Pin and CX.

:halfstar: Late Double Time (A4.5)
You can CX your guys in the middle of their movement, but then they only get 1 extra MF instead of 2.

:halfstar: Road movement (A4.132)
If you use the road the enemy can trace LOS to the road hexside instead of hex center dot if he so wishes.
- Even if you're moving from a road hex to a road hex you don't necessarily have to use the road itself. You should specify if you don't want to use it. For example if you're moving "along" the road into a hex where the road is on open ground you might as well not use the road in which case the enemy cannot trace LOS to the road hexside.
Or if you're moving on an Orchard Road hex, you can avoid FFMO by specifying you're actually using the orchard portion of the hex.
In both examples you'll be forfeiting the road movement bonus though.
- Interestingly if there's a road and a building in the same hex and you move using the road it only costs 1 MF to enter that building instead of 2 MF.

:halfstar: Moving into the same Location with enemy infantry (A4.14)
You still cannot move into the same Location with an enemy MMC unless:
- You're Berserk or in Human Wave.
- Enemy is Disrupted or Unarmed.

If a single SMC is blocking your way, you can try Infantry Overrun (A4.15)
- Make a NTC and move into his hex.

:halfstar: Smoke and WP (White Phosphorus) (A24)
White Phosphorus
Placing SMOKE: (A24.1)
- If you place SMOKE uphill or up the stairs, it can roll down back to your location on a subsequent dr of 4-6. You can't throw it higher than one level and not up a Cliff.
- In mild breeze, SMOKE can only be placed on the three downwind hexes.
- Cannot be placed at all in Heavy-Winds/Rain/Mud/Deep Snow. (A24.11)
- There's no limit to how many SMOKE counters can be in a hex, but the total maximum DRM they grant is +3. (A24.2)

If you are the U.S. you can place WP instead of Smoke. It follows all the rules of the regular SMOKE except: (A24.3)
- The smoke exponential is lowered by 1 so it's harder to place.
- It causes NMC in the location it was placed. (A24.31)
- Can cause fires when EC is Dry. (A24.32)

:star: Searching (A12.152)
After a MMC has moved, and if it has 1MF to spare, it can Search the adjacent hexes to see if it can reveal some concealed enemy units (or locate minefields)
- Everything is revealed in those hexes, HIP units are placed on board with "?"
- Be wary of Search Casualties (A12.154)

:star: Clearance (B24.7)
You can try clearing away Flame, Rubble, Wire, a Minefield, Set DC or a Roadblock. A final DR of 2 is needed, so be sure to have good DRMs. 
- A Flame is extinguished immediately in the same phase, or just hampered for time being.
- The other obstacles are actually resolved at the end of CCPh.
- It's Hazardous Movement and leaves your guys TI (Task Involved, worse than Pin) so be careful.
- You can clear Rubble and Minefield only in your MPh, but can try clearing other obstacles in your DFPh too.
- You can put prisoners to work. (A20.5)

:star: Human Wave (HW) (A25.23)
Now this is an interesting move reserved only for Russians (and Chinese and Cavalry). In a HW three or more hexes full of Russian units move side by side towards an enemy unit, everyone at once, in a manner called Impulse movement.

Heads up: The HW rules were updated in the Armies of Oblivion module. Get the replacement pages from the MMP homepage.

Read all about it. Here are some tidbits:
- Units in HW have, among other things, increased Morale, are Lax and cannot be Pinned.
- HW is one of the few ways infantry can enter a location containing enemy infantry in MPh.
- Human Wave cannot be ended voluntarily. It ends when the participating units are either dead, broken or have reached an enemy location. Otherwise they continue on until they've spent 8 MF.
- The status of +1 Morale and Lax lasts for the whole player turn. Not just till the end of MPh.

:halfstar: Delaying the board entry (A2.5)
If you are the Scenario Attacker or have reinforcements, your arriving units can skip entering the board in MPh and can enter in the APh instead. You cannot delay the entry any further than that, so if they forget to enter in the applicable turn, they are out. There are also rules for solving situations where your entry point is blocked.
	

Defensive First Fire

:halfstar: Shooting at a Road hexside (A4.132)
- If enemy infantry is crossing a Road hexside and using Road movement, you can try shooting at that hexside instead of the hex center dot with full FP and FFMO/FFNAM.

:star: Snap Shot (A8.15)
- You can shoot at an enemy crossing a hexside if you have LOS to that whole hexside. Don't get this mixed up with the Road hexside rule above.
- 1/2 FP and no FFMO/FFNAM. Cumulative with Dashing (It's 1/4 FP then).
- Does not leave Residual FP.

:star: Fire Lane (A9.22)
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 11
If you got a MG guarding a long open line, like a road, try laying a Fire Lane across that whole line. A Fire Lane leaves a form of Residual FP on every hex in that line.

It differs from a normal Residual in the following ways:
- The FP of Fire Lane Residual is one column to the left of the MG's original FP, not half FP.
- The FP of Fire Lane Residual does not shift left because of hindrances or other DRMs. That's because with Fire Lane, the bullets can always be traced to a source so hindrances give DRMs to attack DRs instead, based on where the shooting is coming from.
- However not all hindrances count. See Spilky ASL Table 11.
- If the MG operator breaks, the Fire Lane is canceled, and so are the Fire Lane Residuals.
- Every time a Residual FP attack DR is made it has a change to break that MG which would also cancel the Fire Lane.

:star: Enemy unit in your location
If an enemy unit manages to enter your location during MPh:
- If MMC, you must shoot at it, be it First Fire, Subsequent First Fire or even FPF. (A8.3212)
- Remember Triple Point Blank Fire (TPBF). (A7.21)
- While the enemy unit is in your location, you cannot shoot out of that location. (A8.311)
- Put a CC counter on the location but don't resolve the CC until in CCPh. (A8.31)

:halfstar: Residual FP clarification (A8.26)
- The strength of Residual FP shifts one column to the left on the IFT for each positive DRM caused by conditions outside the target hex (hindrance, CX, etc).
- This was clarified from SK2 onward.

Defensive Fire Phase (DFPh)

:star: Clearance (B24.7)
This is another phase where you can make a Clearance attempt.
- Except you can't clear Rubble or a Minefield. Those you can only do in your MPh.

Advancing Fire Phase (AFPh)

:star: Fire spreads
Flame/Blaze
- Flames can turn into Blazes. (B25.15)
- Blazes can spread new Flames. (B25.6)

:star: In the same location with the enemy (and not in Melee)
You can shoot them, with TPBF, even if a CC marker was placed earlier in the MPh. Remember to also halve the FP because of AFPh.

:star: Opportunity Fire (A7.25)
Units that used Opportunity Fire at PFPh can now shoot with full FP.

Rout Phase (RtPh)

:star: Voluntary Break (A10.41)
You can voluntarily break your unit at the start of the RtPh so it can rout away if need be.
- Must be ADJACENT or in normal range and LOS of an unbroken enemy ground unit.

:star: Concealment (A10.533)
- "?" stacks must be ignored as if they weren't there when choosing a rout destination. This can be either helpful or catastrophic to your routing units.
- If you rout into a "?", one enemy unit is revealed using Random Selection and if the stack is not a dummy, your unit is eliminated.
- A concealed unit may reveal itself anytime during RtPh. It can be a good tactic to force the routing unit to immediately choose a different destination to rout to.

:star: Surrendering and No Quarter
- If your broken unit is ADJACENT to a Known, Good Order, armed enemy Infantry unit and unable to rout without taking interdiction or resorting to Low Crawl it must surrender to that unit. See the prisoner rules. (A20.21)
- The captor can refuse to take prisoners and eliminate it instead. However this invokes No Quarter for the rest of the game and any subsequent Router must take Interdiction or use Low Crawl just like in Starter Kits. (A20.3)

:halfstar: Direction (A10.51)
- You can of course rout up/down building levels.
- You can use shellholes/entrenchements/pillboxes to your advantage to avoid Interdiction if they are along the shortest route to your destination even if you can no longer reach that destination (it takes 1 extra MF to enter or exit a foxhole for example).
- You don't have to rout through a minefield or a hex being bombarded by off-board artillery.

:halfstar: Voluntary Rout clarifications (A10.71)
As you might remember, an unbroken leader can rout with the broken units. It's called Voluntary Rout in the full ASL. Anyway, there are some restrictions that the SK rules don't mention:
- A leader cannot rout with a broken unit if he's Pinned (or Berserk).
- A leader does not improve the broken unit's portage capacity.

Advance Phase (APh)

:halfstar: Eligible advancing destinations (A4.7)
Location Primer
You can advance either:
- From one location to another.
Or
- One hex horizontally, as counterintuitive as it may sometimes sound. 

You cannot combine the two. No moving from downstairs to an adjacent hex upstairs.

For example you can advance directly from beneath a foxhole into another foxhole in an adjacent hex. It may sound strange because if it were the MPh, you'd first have to spend 1 MF to get out, then 1 MF to move into an adjacent hex, then 1 MF to move into a foxhole. But that move is allowed in APh because foxholes are not considered separate locations. (B27.13)
A pillbox on the other hand is a separate location. So you cannot advance out of a pilbox and into an adjacent hex at the same time.

:halfstar: Difficult terrain (A4.72)
SK rules makes it clear that if a move would cost all of the unit's MFs then that unit becomes CX, or if already CX, that move cannot be made. Full rules adds another twist:
- If the cost to enter that hex is (excluding SMOKE) four MF or more, it's the same deal (makes the unit CX, or if already CX, that move cannot be made). Example: Woods on an upper level hill.
- This cannot be avoided with the help of a leader. 

:halfstar: Entering the Board (A2.5)
As mentioned in the MPh, your units can enter the board in APh, instead of MPh.

Close Combat Phase (CCPh)

No longer are you doomed to stay in Melee for possibly the rest of the game since the full ASL rules introduce mechanics for Withdrawal. Ambush or Infiltration may let you withdraw from the first CC, otherwise you can only try to withdraw from a Melee.

:halfstar: Ambush (A11.4)
- Ambush can occur not only in woods or buildings but also anywhere where either side has concealed units.
- No Ambush if the CC counter was placed before CCPh.
- Successful Ambush lets you withdraw from CC either before or after the CC resolution, your choice. (A11.41)

:halfstar: Infiltration (A11.22)
If your CC DR is 2 or your opponent's CC DR is 12, you may immediately withdraw from the CC/Melee. 

Infiltration momentarily suspends the simultaneous nature of the CC, so what happens next depends on if you’re the ATTACKER or the DEFENDER (remember, the ATTACKER rolls first even in a simultaneous CC).
- First, remember to resolve the possible Field Promotion. (A18.12)
- If the ATTACKER rolls 2 he must first choose if he wants to withdraw before the DEFENDER resolves his attack. If he does, the DEFENDER does not get a change to strike back. That DR of 2 is still resolved against the DEFENDER but even if the DEFENDER was eliminated the ATTACKER does not gain control of that CC location. 
- If the DEFENDER rolls 2, he must suffer the ATTACKER’s roll first regardless.
- If the ATTACKER rolls 12, the DEFENDER does not roll for his attack if he chooses to withdraw.
- If the DEFENDER rolls 12, the ATTACKER’s roll is still resolved even if he chooses to withdraw.

:halfstar: Withdrawal from Melee (A11.2)
You can try to withdraw from Melee (not from CC) by announcing so at the start of the CCPh.
- Broken units must attempt to withdraw from Melee. A11.16
- Every Withdrawing unit gets -2 DRM to all CC attacks against them but also +1 DRM for every friendly unit that "stays and covers" i.e. is not withdrawing.

:star: Withdrawal Mechanics (A11.21)
- You withdraw to an adjacent location in the same manner as you'd advance in APh.
- The location cannot be occupied by a Known enemy unit.
- If you withdrew into a location containing enemy "?" or HIP units and it turns out it wasn't a dummy, your units are immediately eliminated.

:star: Concealment in CC/Melee (A11.19)
- HIP units in a CC location come to board under "?".
- All concealed units in CC must temporarily reveal their Strength factor which means dummy units gets removed. This doesn't remove the "?" altogether though.
- CC FP against "?" is halved.
- You only lose your "?" if you attack in that CC or suffer a Casualty Reduction. Thus it might be wise to forfeit your attack in order to retain your "?". Remember, concealed units are not held in Melee and can move or attack (with TPBF even) in the next turn.

:halfstar: SW/Gun elimination in CC (A11.13)
SW/Gun can be destroyed if its owner dies in CC and the colored dr of that CC DR is 1. Roll a subsequent dr and if it is < black Kill Number of that CC attack, then it's eliminated.

:star: Taking Prisoner in CC (A20.22)
- You can try to capture enemy units in CC if you announce a capture attempt before rolling the dice.
- +1 DRM to CC DR unless enemy is inexperienced in which case it's -1 DRM. If the final CC DR = Kill number you get one HS of the defender's choice.

:star: Resolve non-Flame Clearance (B24.7)
If you decided to clear some obstacles, other than Flame, in your MPh or DFPh, then now is the time to resolve those and see if you succeeded.

:star: Gain Concealment (A12.12)
Just a reminder, your units can gain concealment at the end of your turn if they are out of enemy LOS. Consult the Concealment Loss/Gain Table.

What's new with Support Weapons

:star: Assembling/Disassembling SWs (A9.8)
Some SWs (and Guns) may be dismantled to make them easier to carry.
- Such a weapon may start the scenario dismantled if wanted.
- The converting happens in PFPh or DFPh provided that the weapon has not yet been fired in that phase. It counts as using the weapon, meaning that if you convert it during PFPh, that weapon cannot move in MPh or fire in AFPh.
- A German HMG/MMG can be fired as LMG in its dm state. That's because the German HMG/MMG is basically the same weapon as LMG, just with more bells and whistles attached on.

:halfstar: Recovery of SWs (or Guns) (A4.44)
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 7
- If an MMC breaks and drops its SW/Gun, a SMC in that location can immediately try to pick it up.
- SMC can try to grab the SW/Gun from a broken unit in RPh or MPh. Don't even have to pay 1 MF for that.

:halfstar: SWs/Guns may set up unpossessed
Starter Kit 2 and onwards clarifies that a Weapons may not be set up unpossessed. However, there is no such rule in full ASL.

Machine Guns

:halfstar: Permanent Breakdowns (A.11)
Whenever the #B decreases, the original #B changes to #X (for example Sustained Fire or Captured Use).

:halfstar: Field of Fire (A9.21)
If a MMG or HMG is in woods/building/rubble, shoots, and has the ability to shoot again (ROF, Subsequent First Fire) it must shoot inside the same CA (Covered Arc, see Gun rules C3.2) as its previous shot for the rest of that phase. Use the Field of Fire counter.
- Unlike Gun however, the CA includes the MG's own hex.
- Pinned MG retains its CA until the end of DFPh.

:halfstar: Mandatory Fire Direction (A9.4)	
Enemy infantry over 16 hexes away are treated as concealed.

Remember Bore Sighting (C6.4), Spraying Fire (A9.5) and Fire Lanes. (A9.22)

Flame Throwers (FT)

:halfstar: FT's effect on terrain (B25.12)
- A FT may create a Flame if an Original K or KIA is rolled on the IFT. A subsequent DR is made like it was a regular Kindling attempt.

Demolition Charges (DC)
Demolition Charges

:star: DC's effect on terrain
- A DC with an Original KIA on the IFT, like any sufficient HE strike, can cause Rubble (B24.11) or Flames (B25.13).
- The Rubble creation is checked first with a subsequent dr; If that also hits the KIA then that building location, and all the levels above it, are Rubbled. If not, then a Kindling DR is made to see if a Flame is created.

:halfstar: Thrown or Set DC
In addition to placing DC, it can also be Thrown or Set.
- DC is Thrown during friendly fire phase (That means your PFPh, DFPh or AFPh) or Defensive First Fire. It's less reliable and affects both the target's and the thrower's location. (A23.6 - 23.63)
- Setting a DC in a location costs the unit all of its MFs and is Hazardous Movement. That unit can detonate it during any subsequent friendly fire phase only. That does not include Defensive First Fire! (A23.7 - 23.72)

:star: Making a Breach with a DC
DC can be used to Breach a Rowhouse Building (B23.711), or a Fortified Building. (B23.9221)

Panzerfausts (PF)

:star: In 10/43+ Germans can use Panzerfausts (C13.3)
Germans
It's an inherent SW, meaning it's available for the Germans in every scenario from 10/43 onwards (or PFks prior that by SSR but those are very rare).
- To use them, you'd first have to learn about Ordnance (SK2 stuff. They are similar to PSKs, see Part 2 for more). However, PFs are primarily used against tanks and have only limited application vs Infantry. It's perfectly OK not to use PFs in an infantry only scenario if you're not ready to learn about Ordnance just yet.

What's new with ELR

:star: Disruption (A19.12)
A unit is Disrupted if it breaks and exceeds its ELR but cannot downgrade to anything worse anymore (Conscripts are prone to disruption for example)
- Disrupted units surrender more easily, cannot self-rally, do not like to rout, won't withdraw from Melee etc. All in all they're a bunch of miserable folk.

:halfstar: Replacement (A19.13)
There is no neat single unit replacement chart like in the backs of Starter Kit manuals. Instead look at the pictures in chapter A25. If that doesn't help you can always work it out yourself using the following rules:
- The unit's class must be lower than its current class. So a 1st line unit cannot downgrade to another 1st line unit.
- At least one of the Strength factors (FP, range, morale) must decrease.
- None of the Strength factors can increase.

:halfstar: Underlined morale (A19.13)
Underlined morale no longer grants total immunity to ELR. Instead, if a unit with an underlined morale breaks and exceeds its ELR:
- If a squad, it splits into two broken HS.
- If a HS, it Disrupts.

In the event that a squad with an underlined morale rolls an original 12 AND it also exceeds its ELR: (A10.31)
- First split the squad into two HS.
- Then eliminate one HS.

Other Miscellaneous new rules, changes and clarifications

:star: Nationality distinctions (A25)
Germans
Be sure to read Chapter A25 before you start a game. Russians, for example, might get a Commissar which is always fun.
- For some reason, the German's ability to get Panzerfausts in 10/43+ is not mentioned here but in C13.3 instead.

:halfstar: Victory Conditions (A26)
- All the Control rules are much more detailed here than in the SKs.
- Unlike in the SKs, the Victory Point values are defined in the rules, not in the scenarios. (A26.2)

:halfstar: Random Selection (A.9)
In Starter Kits you might roll some dice to choose randomly which target is affected in some situation but in full ASL there's an official way called Random Selection. The basic difference to Starter Kits is that more than one target may be affected. Read all about it.

Some examples where Random Selection is used
- #KIA and K/#. (A7.3)
- FG cowers. Check which ones get Prep Fire/Final Fire marker (A7.9)
- Multiple SW Malfunction. (A9.71)

:halfstar: Morale Level Ceiling (A.18)
Some game effects (Fanatic, Human Wave, etc) may cause the morale level to rise but it can never rise above 10.
- This has nothing to do with DRMs to Morale Checks however. 

:halfstar: Stacking Limits (A5)
The limit is still 3 full squads; however it's no longer absolute:
- You cannot exceed it in setup but can during play. There will be penalties however.
- It also no longer makes a location invalid to Rout to.
- 5 SMCs equals 1 HS. (A5.5)

:halfstar: Mandatory Leadership clarification (A10.72)
Leadership DRMs, whether positive or negative cannot be ignored except when attacking.

:halfstar: Right of Inspection (A12.16)
You actually cannot check what's in a big stack of enemy units unless they are in LOS to some of your units. And of course you can never check what's under opponent's "?" counters.

:halfstar: Wounded SMC (A17)
- If SMC is wounded during movement and it has already spent over 3 MFs, it's Pinned right there.
- A MMC can carry a wounded leader at the cost of 5 PP. The leaders +2 MF bonus still works.

:halfstar: Self-rally clarification (A18.11)
DR 2 on Self-rally, in addition to Field Promotion, always rallies the MMC.

:halfstar: CX does not affect MC or PTC (A4.51)
- This was clarified from SK2 onward.

:halfstar: Half-Hex clarification (A2.3)
- If the scenario instructs you to setup only on board 1 you cannot setup on a half-hex that's butted against a half-hex on board 2.
- Same thing for Victory Conditions. If you have to control all the hexes on Board 1 this does not include the half-hexes that are butted against Board 2.

:halfstar: Official word on how to handle errors (A.2)
If you've made a rules mistake earlier, it cannot be unmade later. A good rule to remember in tournaments.

My personal opinion: I will, for the most part, ignore this rule and use my own judgement on a case-by-case basis. If it's a friendly game and my opponent forgot to make his one self-rally attempt in RPh, and he remembers it in PFPh, I'll let him do that self-rally.

query:
MF expenditure for smoke placement and Defensive fire: So my 747 US Paratrooper declares a smoke grenade attempt into an adjacent hex which expends 2 MF.

Can the defender declare D1stF vs the squad as the attempt is declared but before the smoke is placed? or is the MF expended only once the smoke is placed/attemp fails?
title: MF expenditure for smoke placement and Defensive fire
raw_question:
So my 747 US Paratrooper declares a smoke grenade attempt into an adjacent hex which expends 2 MF.

Can the defender declare D1stF vs the squad as the attempt is declared but before the smoke is placed? or is the MF expended only once the smoke is placed/attemp fails?
ground_truth_answer:
The MF spent is always considered as done before you can fire against it. Of course, smoke placement could fail, but the action is done.

Just yesterday my opponent spent 2 MF to place smoke grenades at an adjacent hex, but he forgot about a SQ of mine placed on another hexgrid, with clear LOS. So his SQ placed smoke on an hex and gave me two nice MF to shoot him with clear LOS, FFNAM and FFMO. You just have to love this game.

query:
Leadership and FGs: There are times when I wonder if I'm using using leadership with FGs correctly.

Here's this situation:

I have 3 squads, 2 in one hex and one in another. There is a 9-2 leader in the hex with 2 squads, and no leader in the other. My understanding is that you can't apply the leadership drm to the FG is all 3 squads fire together.

A second situation:

Again three squads (2 in 1 hex, 1 in a hex by itself). This time 2 leaders (9-2 in with the 2 squads, and a 8-1 in with the single squad). In this case I would apply a leadership drm of -1 to the FG.

Is this right? Or does the 9-2 det to add his drm to both situations. I'm fairly sure I'm playing it right.
title: Leadership and FGs
raw_question:

Residual fire and rof: So in a game we're playing an mmc fired its  inherent fp plus mmg, mmg retained rof and fired again.

We figured the first fire attack leaves no res but does the second attack leave any?
title: Residual fire and rof
raw_question:
So in a game we're playing an mmc fired its  inherent fp plus mmg, mmg retained rof and fired again.

We figured the first fire attack leaves no res but does the second attack leave any?
ground_truth_answer:
So in a game we're playing an mmc fired its  inherent fp plus mmg, mmg retained rof and fired again.

We figured the first fire attack leaves no res but does the second attack leave any?

Let me give an example so we can be clear. An American 6-6-6 squad and 4fp MMG fire at a moving unit that spends 2MF entereing a hex in normal range of both the squad and MMG.

The MMG makes ROF. The squad leaves a residual firepower of 2 in the hex.

The MMG fires again. This time it loses ROF. It would normally place a residual firepower of 2, but that doesn't increase the already existing residual firepower of 2 so it has no additional effect.

However, it the player had elected to forgo ROF (retained) from the first shot in order to increase RF (for tactical purposes lets say) then the attack was 6+4=10FP, resolved on the 8FP, leaving a 4FP RF counter instead of 2FP.

I usually find it more useful to place 2FP residual in two Locations instead of just one. But sometimes you have a proper choke-point that needs the 4FP residual.

It's very, very rare that the situation will come up in the Starter Kit rules - and no, they aren't identical.

Please note that a broken unit ADJACENT to an unbroken unit must rout during the Rout Phase (just before the Advance Phase) until no longer ADJACENT. (And it can't move ADJACENT to unbroken units throughout the rout). If it can't, it's eliminated for failure to rout.

If you've gotten a lot of play out of Starter Kit #1 and already have the ASLRB and BV, you can start this scenario.  It will be a huge chunk to bite off, but it's doable if you are willing to devote the time to reading and re-reading the rules as you play.  Some of the bigger things to get a handle on are:

Movement is a good bit different.  There's Bypass and Dash Moves, with attendant Snap Shots against hexsides units move through.  Takes some getting used to.  

Concealment and HIP is just for starters, you'll also have to get Searching and Mopping Up under your belt.  Huge effects of concealment on things like movement, ambush and close combat, determining rout paths, etc.

Blazes and fires--and smoke (with wind effects) will take some getting used to in this scenario.  Really important to leverage this as the Soviet player in coming up with a defensive scheme.  This stuff is going to channelize--and you don't want to be the one channelized into the streets under the muzzles of Finnish LMGs!  

Terrain.  Oh yeah, the buildings take some real practice to learn how to use them to good effect--particularly the multi-levelled ones.  Great article in the newest ASL Journal (#9) on buildings, written by Mark Pitcavage.

ground_truth_answer:
Can a berserker attempt to place smoke on the way to the nearest known enemy?
According to the ASOP, no:

A berserk unit executes its charge in Step 3.31A, After this, you jump directly to Step 3.35D... so a berserk unit never executes Step 3.32A, which is the step that allows SMOKE grenades to be placed. Berserk units technically can't do *anything* that's listed in Step 3.32A.

Consider, for example, Infantry OVR. This too occurs in Step 3.32A, seemingly making it NA to berserk units, so the berserk rules have to specifically allow it (A15.432). But there's nothing in the berserk rules that specifically allows the use of SMOKE grenades.

ground_truth_answer:
I just pulled out the PB1 'Ham and Bloody Jam' card - the SSR reads, 'To "clear" the bridge, the British must make a successful Clearance DR in any bridge Location as though removing a Set DC (B24.75).'

24.75 SET DC: Unpinned, Good Order Infantry which has not moved or fired (or directed fire) during that Player Turn (as evidenced by placement of a TI counter and the declaration of their removal attempt during their MPh/DFPh) in a Location containing a Set DC may remove that Set DC with a successful Clearance DR at the end of the CCPh.

So, you'll need to have a unit in place and ready to rock at least by the beginning of the last British Player Turn.  Since you roll at the end of the CCPh the German will still be able to interfere with the clearance attempt.

Good luck, and post an AAR when you're done!

JR

ground_truth_answer:
Main reason I stay out of ASL (yet). It looks to me that RB is like a bible open to never-ending discussions.ASL is a complex game.
If you compare the level of questions and errata in proportion of the size of the rules, they remain within reasonable bounds.
Note, too, that many questions arise from quite marginal situations, where rules interact in an unusual way.
What is nice, is that there are published official errata and clarifications which lead the community to play along the same rule interpretations.

It might be the reason that more than some ASLers play ASL and only ASL.The main reason of being hooked to ASL, is that it offers such a variety of possibilities, that players seem to discover its multiple facets on and on.

Shhh! Under any circumstances we should not even suggest that this ancient text might need some serious rewrite...The ASL RB is not the most pedagogical ruleset - I believe that is a statement that has been accepted from the beginning.
The SL had a "step by step" rule learning system.
But each addition to the rules created a dispersion (and unsuperable contradictions) that led to the "reference" ruleset style we have now.
However, there remains some dispersion (e.g Smoke rules), which can be countered by reference cards.

The coherence of the rules remains, IMO, remarkable, compared to many less abundant rulesets.
To try for a "serious" rewriting, one should have a very experimented knowledge of the present Rulebook - or the risk of missing essential interactions and taxonomy conventions will be enormous.
And the interaction of the rules rely upon the paragraph references : the basic structure could not be modified.

One way to go - I have been tempted to do it, but haven't enough energy and time to - would be to illustrate about each point of rule with an example and to have a "shortened" description of each point of the rule (more graphical).
It would not replace the current RB, but help checking the rules more easily.
Note that the Index is really a precious resource, as it often has sumarized definitions and lists most of the rules interactions.

But ASL is a complex game. There is a price of effort to learn it (and the learning doesn't really end - even on the side of learning the rules).

Now, to be an ASLer, I believe one must have a twist of mind that allows one to appreciate that type of game.
I don't mind if it is slightly pathological : to spend hours pushing cardboard units and having fun is a special way of life. ;)

The other thing to bear in mind Rafaell is that I haven't played ASL for a long time. This is only my second game since coming back a few weeks ago, what's more I still have a lot on pre-conceptions from SL, which tend to muddy the waters a little :)

I had got back into board gaming the middle of last year as I wanted a different experience from that provided by computer wargames. To get me back into the hobby I bought Conflict of Heroes (CoH) which I have now played to death. 

CoH is a very good game and what is more the rulebook is only 30 odd pages from what I remember - maybe less. When playing CoH my initial reaction was why did I ever bother with ASL in the eighties when CoH seems to simulate most of the salient points of WW2 warfare.

But after many plays of CoH and its sequel I started yearning for something more. Something with more depth, tactical variety and a little more unpredictability. In the latter case CoH only uses one DR for an attack, which makes it very easy for a player to work out what is likely to happen. In games like ASL there are effectively two or more DR, one for effect and several DR's for any pertinent morale checks that might be needed. This makes ASL both predictable and unpredictable at the same time(!) work that one out!

What 'turned' me was when I went through Jay Richardson's pdf ASLSK tutorial here on boardgame geek with VASSAL. What struck me was the richness of tactical options available - much more than in simpler games like CoH. I really enjoyed running through the tutorials - even though my experience with CoH would suggest otherwise.

The upshot is that I'm now back and having a blast. The ASL rules really do put you on the ground with your troops. For the moment I'm soloing, but once my familiarity grows I will start seeking out online games in VASSAL.

ASL is a very worthwhile system - but it demands a lot of upfront time to read through the rules. Once read it is amazing how quickly the rules flow during a game. In the last two games I have played, I have rarely had to look up rules as the majority of them are common sense. I guess this is a testament to how well an ASL game flows - despite the huge ruleset.

RobP

ground_truth_answer:
It seems that low level Japanese commanders were not trained to use any tactical flexibility at all - rather they were instilled with the Samurai tradition of relentless frontal attacks. 
 

I'm not at all sure this is an accurate statement. The Japanese were well versed in military tradition and learning, and had a set of tactical solutions provided in manuals. The Japanese Army ran rings around the Chinese Army, and did well against the Soviet Army in 1939.

Japanese field tactics had some distinct differences to the US Army, the most significant being the belief in closing with the enemy to close combat (shared by the British), the primacy of offensive action (which WW1 had knocked out of the Western Allies), and the need for swiftness in assault (which the Japanese had demonstrated in the 1905 War with Russia). The Japanese also often used infiltration and outflanking. A combination of terrain and technology base generally precluded the use  of massive bombardment and massed armoured blitzkreig, but the Japanese did use these relatively small arms effectively.

Japanese field tactics worked well in China, Manchuria, Malaya, Burma, Philippines and Dutch East Indies. The problem came when the Allies started heavily equiping their troops with individual automatic weapons. In essence, the Allied solution to Japanese Banzai charges was firepower, the same solution as happened in WW1, and the Japanese had no technological solution available. The best option was the night attack, which limited the amount of time units were under fire. 

It is probably fair to say that Japanese Officers were indifferent to the casualties of an attack, and that most were taught that the best chance of victory was through close combat assault. So the Japanese tactics reflected that view, but were not chosen without consideration, and indeed later in the Pacific war, they clearly changed to much more defensive and attritional tactics to further the grinding war strategy the Japanese were relying upon to seek an offer of conditional surrender.

Correct the Rushing Russian tank can claim Wall Advantage as the PzIV cannot deny Wall Advantage.

The PzIV recieves all benefits of the wall.

ground_truth_answer:
I would guess that the German tank still gets +2 TEM for being behind a stone wall even though he does not get the hull down benefit of Wall Advantage.
Wall Advantage is *not* required for Hulldown Status. As per B9.36, Hulldown applies whenever Wall TEM could apply. So the PzIV is Hulldown to Russian E, but not to Russian F. (And Russian F is Hulldown to the PzIV, but Russian E is not.)

This all seems fairly odd...
Partly this is a simplification for ease-of-play purposes. This same situation, if played on the large Deluxe ASL boards (2.2" hexes), would indeed have the PzIV claiming WA over the Russian tank, because in Deluxe ASL WA is claimed individually for each hexside, rather than for an entire hex at once.

I think that regular ASL was originally intended to work this way, but it proved impractical to keep track of WA on a hexside-by-hexside basis with the small regular hexes. Thus, the requirement that you can only claim WA if you can claim it for the entire hex keeps confusion to a minimum, but it does lead to some odd situations like this.

query:
Simple AFV Combat Question: Now it's the Defensive Fire Phase. I fire at the tank two hexes away. Because the enemy tank moved during this turn it is still considered a "moving target" even though it spent a MP to stop. Correct?
Yes. It remains a Moving Target until the end of the Player Turn.

So do I get no apply Case L Point Blank Range?
Case L will apply because the target is stopped; the fact that the target is still a Moving Target is irrelevant here. The target would have to be non-stopped or in Motion for Case L to be NA.

C.8 says that he is a "moving target" because he entered a new hex during the current turn? But does that make him a Motion target?
Nope... "in Motion" and "Moving Target" are two different things.

Case L does not apply to a Motion/Non-Stopped target/firer. The whole "moving", "Motion", "In-Motion", "Non-stopped" business seems very non-intuitive.
Yes, indeed it is. The unfortunate terminology used can be quite confusing.

Here are a couple of resources that you may find helpful:

An ASLSK Tutorial (Part 5)
http://www.boardgamegeek.com/thread/361467/an-aslsk-tutorial-part-5

This is an ASLSK tutorial that explains the basics of the ASL armor system in exhaustive detail, with particular emphasis placed on the multiple states of moving, Motion, stopped/non-stopped, and Moving Target. Everything in this tutorial also applies to full ASL, but the ASLSK rules unfortunately use Case numbers instead of Case letters (Case L in ASL is Case 25 in ASLSK).

ASL Phases Quick Reference
http://www.boardgamegeek.com/filepage/43693/asl-phases-quick-reference

This PDF file contains – among many other things – a copy of Ole Boe's "Vehicular Movement Status" summary for ASL... a tiny chart that is a life-saver when you are trying to sort out the ASL armor system. (This same chart is also in the ASLSK tutorial article above, but that version lacks one entry that is needed for the full ASL rules.)

Also do I get to place acquisition?
Yes.

Now it's Advancing Fire Phase. The enemy tank fires back at me. Does it get Case L Point Blank Fire? Does it get to apply acquisition?
Yes to both.

Do Snipers activate on Res. FP attacks?

Yes - any non-OBA IFT DR qualifies.

JR

There you go.  It's probably beneficial to one player or the other to put it down.

This goes along with the concept of Snipers in the first place.  Are you obligated to down Res. FP?  If it is not beneficial to you (that is let's say the only way it can affect a unit is to roll your sniper) are you required to place it?

Snipers are my favorite rule.  If you roll your opponent's sniper and he doesn't notice it, are you obligated to point it out?  If so, then how can he prove it?  Maybe you didn't see it either?  And he didn't see it in the first place so how would he even know?

This is when you invoke the Banozic Sniper activation method.  That is, every time your opponent rolls a DR which is capable of activating the sniper, you yell out, "Sniper!".  Then the onus is on your opponent to disprove you, which is easy to do by just pointing at the dice.  But if you do this, no sniper will ever be missed.  Same thing could be said for ROF.

I guess my point is that laying Res. FP is always more beneficial to one of the players, not necessarily the Defender.  But as the Attacker you should be cognizant of this and make sure Res. FP is placed appropriately.

Someone asked in another thread how to get better at the game.  I think one way is to jump into these tiny details and understand them as deeply as possible.  In this instance we are kind of talking about player obligation and ethics, but still...  If  you want to learn the game you need to get real geeky about it.

I am really hazy on DFF and VCA/TCA changes. I notice rule D2.401 allows a "motion attempt" at any moment during your opponent's move. The rule doesn't say why you'd want to do that (a constant failing of the ASLRB, I"m finding - good at how, terrible at why/when you'd want to use a given rule).
Hi, Nick. A motion attempt during your opponent's MPh is usually used so it's harder for the enemy AFV to hit you since the fact you're in motion will add the Case J +2 TH DRM. The rulebook does have it's faults, but in this case I think it's pretty clear why you'd want to make a motion attempt since D2.401 is immediately followed by D2.41: "TARGET CONSEQUENCES: Any Motion vehicle is eligible for the Case J To Hit (Motion Target) DRM when fired upon, regardless of fire phase."

Here are my questions:

1) is a successful motion attempt required to allow VCA change in DPh/DFF? That is to say, does a NT vehicle NEED to make a succesful motion attempt to change its VCA in the Dph?
Not exactly. If you make a successful motion attempt (again, to make it harder to get hit) then you are free to make VCA/TCA changes, per D2.401. But you can also change your VCA during your opponent's MPh or the DFPh by firing outside your VCA. Check out D2.11: "A VCA can also be changed following a successful Motion Attempt (2.401), as a result of firing outside its CA during any fire phase (other than its own Mph; C5.1), or at the end of any fire phase in which it is still eligible to fire a turret/bow-mounted weapon (3.12 and C3.22)."

However, remember that if you change your TCA or VCA to fire on an enemy, your TH DR will face the Case A DRMs depending on what kind of AFV you have and how many hexspines your shifting your CA. If you're just turning your turret, you face either a +1 or +2 for the first hexspine (depending on whether you have a fast- or slow-traverse turret) and +1 for each additional hexspine. If your AFV is non-turreted OR has a turret but elects to change the entire VCA instead (maybe because you want your stronger armor facing the enemy) it faces the +3 VCA change DRM for the first hexspine and +1 for each additional hexspine. Check out D5.11: "All Guns use Case A to fire at targets outside their current CA when changing their CA for a shot in that phase. Turreted vehicles change only their TCA so that their target lies within that TCA. OBA - Conversion of SR to FFE:1 possible with no enemy units in/adjacent to SR hex?: Situation as follows:

- Radio Contact maintained.
- Battery access.
- SR on board.
- Observer has LOS to ground level of SR-hex.
- No (enemy) units in/adjacent to SR-hex.

Question:

Is it possible to convert the SR to FFE:1 in place although there are no (enemy) units in/adjacent to the SR-hex?

The OBA flowchart states:

Does Observer have a LOS to the base level of the hex? 

If there are units in or adjacent to the SR hex, are all of them unknown to the Observer?

This seems to point rather to the question, if there are known and/or unknown units. But what if there are no units at all? Would there be an extra chit draw necessary?

As a background: In the previous Advance Phase, all enemy units advanced out of the potenital blast zone. Nevertheless, I would still like to convert the SR to FFE:1 to deny the enemy re-entry and to try to rubble a building and to possibly clear wire/mines.

Thanks for your help
title: OBA - Conversion of SR to FFE:1 possible with no enemy units in/adjacent to SR hex?
raw_question:
Situation as follows:

- Radio Contact maintained.
- Battery access.
- SR on board.
- Observer has LOS to ground level of SR-hex.
- No (enemy) units in/adjacent to SR-hex.

Question:

Is it possible to convert the SR to FFE:1 in place although there are no (enemy) units in/adjacent to the SR-hex?

The OBA flowchart states:

Does Observer have a LOS to the base level of the hex? 

If there are units in or adjacent to the SR hex, are all of them unknown to the Observer?

This seems to point rather to the question, if there are known and/or unknown units. But what if there are no units at all? Would there be an extra chit draw necessary?

As a background: In the previous Advance Phase, all enemy units advanced out of the potenital blast zone. Nevertheless, I would still like to convert the SR to FFE:1 to deny the enemy re-entry and to try to rubble a building and to possibly clear wire/mines.

Thanks for your help
ground_truth_answer:
C1.33 to C1.337 (SR & FFE:1/2 options) does not (on my reading) expressly deal with the situation where you can see the SR but there are no enemy units (Known or otherwise) in the blast radius.

However, C1.21 (Battery Access) says this:

"... whenever Converting any SR/FFE:C to a FFE:1 ..., Battery Access must be attempted a second (ie an extra) time if >= one non-hidden enemy ground unit is in/adjacent-to the AR (or, when Converting, to the SR/FFE:C) counter's hex but none of those units are Known to the Observer ..."

So the way I see it, if the projected blast area is empty, you can convert without an extra Battery Access draw.  It is only if there are enemy units there which are not Known that the extra draw is required.

It's not in the Assault Phase section either, so have we just invented this rule whole-cloth, or is it hidden somewhere in the book..?Here is the rule :

A4.41 AFPh SW FIRE LIMITS: No MMG, HMG, mortar, INF/RCL SW, or 5/8" non-vehicular ordnance counter which moved [other than being Recovered (4.44)] during the MPh may fire during the ensuing AFPh [EXC: German dm MMG/HMG may fire as LMG; 9.8]. However, if such weapons remained stationary while their new owners moved into their Location, they can be fired during the ensuing AFPh with the normal penalties for fire in the AFPh—assuming they were Recovered during that MPh (4.44). A weapon fired during the AFPh cannot use Intensive Fire and is limited to one shot regardless of its ROF [EXC: if using Opportunity Fire; 7.25].

Also, I'm having trouble deciphering the rules about the ability of HMGs to take down vehicles - and I fear I've got them very confused. Am I right in thinking that they simply cannot take down armoured vehicles, but can take down an unarmored vehicle by firing as ordinance, and then rolling under the number on the 'star' row of their IFT column?
vs armored, an MG (whether LMG, MMG or HMG or vehicle MA MG) uses the TH-TK process.
vs unarmored, it uses the IFT's * line.

A9.6 VEHICULAR TARGETS: The process for resolution of MG fire vs vehicular targets is dependent on whether the vehicle Target Facing/Aspect is armored or not. If the Target Facing is armored, such fire is resolved on the AP To Kill Table after securing a hit on the To Hit Table; otherwise it is resolved on the * Vehicle line of the IFT and no To Hit DR is necessary. A non-captured MG To Hit DR always uses the black To Hit numbers regardless of nationality when firing as ordnance.
9.61 explains further the processes used.
Note that any cause of halving the MG's fire prohibits it from firing as ordnance (e.g. an LMG that has moved during the AFPh).

query:
Is exchanging SW counted as action ?: Hi all,

  If a leader receives a SW from another good order unit in the same hex, is he still legible for rallying broken units in that RPh? It's a questions against 4.431, which is very unclear to me.

  Thanks.
title: Is exchanging SW counted as action ?
raw_question:
Hi all,

  If a leader receives a SW from another good order unit in the same hex, is he still legible for rallying broken units in that RPh? It's a questions against 4.431, which is very unclear to me.

  Thanks.
ground_truth_answer:
I don't believe a Ldr is required for transfer of SWs between units, is he?
Correct. Two units in the same location may transfer a weapon between themselves without the presence of a leader. The only requirement for a transfer is that both units involved be in Good Order and unpinned. (A4.431)

If the transfer takes place in the RPh, then the "one action per unit per RPh" restriction also applies to both units. For example, a unit that attempts to recover a weapon in the RPh could not participate in a transfer in the same RPh.

Note that the Attacker may also conduct transfers at the start of the APh. (Step 7.11A of the ASOP)

If not, then is it that he's occupied recieving a SW *himself* (or transfering from himself), that counts as an action and prevents him then from rallying?
Right. If a leader gives a weapon that he's carrying to another unit, or receives a weapon from another unit, that's his one allowed action for that RPh. As long as he is not personally involved in a transfer (or any of the other listed RPh actions) he is free to rally broken units.

query:
ASL Noob Has Questions?: Armor Leaders and ELR are not explicitly written down, but the info is there in the rules. For ELR replacement, the rules say:

A19.13 REPLACEMENT An unbroken Personnel unit which fails an MC by and amount > its ELR is immediately Replaced by a broken Personnel unit of lesser quality but the same size.

According to A19.11:

 All crew-types, Commissars, heroes, unarmed and already broken units are never subject to Replacement due to ELR failure

Now, the definition of "personnel" in the Index is:

All SMC and MMC counters, including those mounted as Cavalry or Passengers/Riders, but excluding inherent crews since they are not in counter form.

Note the word "inherent", for in the section relating to Armor Leaders, it says:

D3.41 An Armor Leader is considered inherently present in the particular AFV his owner assigns him to...

and further more:

D3.43 An Armor leader affects only its own vehicle/crew (even a captured vehicle) and ceases to exist once the crew takes counter form. Should that particular vehicular crew reoccupy a vehicle, the Armor Leader will once again exist in that vehicle.

Now, since by definition, an Armor Leader is not personnel, then he is not subject to ELR Replacement. This is reinforced by the fact that inherent crews are explicitly excluded and the Armor Leader is part of an inherent crew according to D3.43.

query:
Moving vs expending MF: 1. If an ATTACKER SQ in OG does not declare AM and then expends 2 MF to deploy smoke and it gets first fired by this MF expenditure (with clear LOS), does the DEFENDER get FFNAM/FFMO modifiers?

2. Further, everywhere in the ASLRB where there is a rule about "moving", is MF expending always considered a form of "moving" or must the Infantry units really move from a Location to another to be considered "moving"?

title: Moving vs expending MF
raw_question:
1. If an ATTACKER SQ in OG does not declare AM and then expends 2 MF to deploy smoke and it gets first fired by this MF expenditure (with clear LOS), does the DEFENDER get FFNAM/FFMO modifiers?

2. Further, everywhere in the ASLRB where there is a rule about "moving", is MF expending always considered a form of "moving" or must the Infantry units really move from a Location to another to be considered "moving"?

If you know the answers, could you please indicate the specific rules? 

Thanks!

Edit: spelling.
ground_truth_answer:
A4.2 Whenever a player moves a unit during his MPh he states alound the MF expended by that unit in entering each hex or in performing any other activity within its current hex.

So activities that spend MF are "moving" - throwing smoke, picking up a SW, going into a foxhole.

A4.61 Assault Movement, if it is to be used, must be declared prior to movement of that unit,

So, to answer your questions;

1. If you do not declare AM and the expend 2MF - you are moving (per A4.2) and not AM (per A4.61) so yes, you will receive the FFNAM modifier (and the FFMO modifier if you are in open ground).

SIDEBAR - if you are successful with your smoke - that can negate the FFMO modifier, and you will receive the smoke hindrance as well for the FF shot.

2. See A4.2. MF expending is "moving"

Hope that helps,
Dan

Multi-hex is allowed (unless Passengers/Riders are also firing)  

D6.64
In all cases, the normal rules for FG (A7.5-.55) still apply.

A FG may consist of units from more than one Location only if each participating unit occupies a Location ADJACENT to another participating unit of the same FG.

CE halftrack paasengers may FG normally. Other passengers are restricted to firing with other passengers of the same vehicle and with the vehicles non-MA (unless it is IFE capable) armament. Riders may only FG with other same-vehicle riders and the AAMG of that vehicle.

ground_truth_answer:
1. A bridge and a strange bypass move 
When the Russian tank moves to the bridge it can of course continue to J1. But what if it doesn't want to. Can it move to J2?
No, you have to cross a road hexside when entering or leaving a bridge (B6.4).

2. Hull Down
Is Hull Down something that happens automatically any time a tank is behind a wall, or is it something that must be claimed and must the tank be stopped or can it be moving (or in motion or whatever)?
A vehicle behind a wall always has HD status if the +2 Wall TEM would otherwise apply (D4.21), so even a moving/Motion vehicle can have HD status when it is behind a wall.

Gaining HD status from a Height Advantage is not automatic, however (D4.22).

Here a Russian tank is just cruising along the road. Is it automatically Hull Down to Puma?
Yes.

Are both tanks Hull Down or only the first tank there, claiming it?
Wall Advantage applies, so only one of the two vehicles would have HD status.

3. Tanks in same hex
I'm planning to move through the Russian tank to V7 and shoot it in the rear. If I move to the same hex with enemy tank, what exactly happens? Or what are the Russian tank's options? Especially since it hasn't fired it's CMG yet? (Although I told my opponent to save his CMG until I get in his rear so he could shoot and change his VCA in the process (which he did but I still had plenty of MP to get to his rear again)).

Anyways, what if he shoots in the same hex. What modifiers does he get (in addition to buttoned up, moving target and intensive fire)?
Also Case E, fire within hex, +2. Note that Case L will *not* apply.

What if his Turret was pointing to the right and I moved to his hex from left. Must he change his TCA even if I'm in his hex?
Yes (C5.51).

Does he retain Acquired Target in the same hex? What about when I move past him to V7?
Yes to both, because you have not moved out of his LOS.

4. And what about that CMG....
I never found a good summary about all the modifiers that applies to tank's MGs in different situations..

The IFT only lists motion/bounding first fire as 1/2 FP but surely there are more to this...
Bounding (First) Fire: x 1/2 FP (D3.31)
Motion/Non-Stopped: x 1/2 FP (D2.42)

So, if a moving AFV fires its MGs, they fire at 1/2 FP if the AFV is Stopped; if the AFV is non-Stopped, they fire at 1/4 FP.
(1/2 x 1/2)

Where's the +2 protection for the CE crew? It's not on the IFT or I'm blind.
D5.31 (it is not on the IFT).

Doesn't it matter if the opponent tank is moving? Isn't it harder to hit?
Not when you're firing on the IFT with small arms (D2.41).

Is there PBF or TPBF ever?
Yes, as normal.

Cower?
Vehicular MGs never cower.

Back to question 3. What if that CMG fired when the Puma was in the same hex? What are all the modifiers?
FP x3 for TPBF, +2 DRM.

query:
Bridge TEM question: The RB states that unhindered fire against unit(s) on a Bridge that crosses only the road depiction is eligible for -1 FFMO DRM, and fire against units on a Bridge that does not cross only the road depiction is subject to a +1 TEM DRM, no?

I understand there were changes made to these rules via published errata (that were controversial in some circles), and that they were subsequently rescinded?  

Not looking for any flame wars! - just wondering if anyone can provide a short history of the rule changes, and confirm if my understanding of the rules as posted above is correct and current.
title: Bridge TEM question
raw_question:
The RB states that unhindered fire against unit(s) on a Bridge that crosses only the road depiction is eligible for -1 FFMO DRM, and fire against units on a Bridge that does not cross only the road depiction is subject to a +1 TEM DRM, no?

I understand there were changes made to these rules via published errata (that were controversial in some circles), and that they were subsequently rescinded?  

Not looking for any flame wars! - just wondering if anyone can provide a short history of the rule changes, and confirm if my understanding of the rules as posted above is correct and current.
ground_truth_answer:
The bridge TEM controversy wasn't just a simple case of MMP making a mistake... there is actually an error in the game's components.

The bridge counters show 0 TEM along the road, +1 TEM otherwise.

The Terrain Chart says -1 TEM along the road, +1 TEM otherwise.

The two components do not agree, so one of them is wrong.

When MMP was asked to rule on this, they ruled that the Terrain Chart was correct (-1 TEM), and issued errata to fix the wording of the rules in Chapter B to support this. But it seems that most players were using 0 TEM for bridges, which was supported by the original wording of the Chapter B rules... hence the uproar and controversy.

The players eventually convinced MMP that the Terrain Chart was, in fact, wrong and MMP rescinded their original errata.

So, the final result is that the bridge counters are correct as printed; the Terrain Chart is wrong (errata in Journal 8 corrects the wording of the Terrain Chart); and the Chapter B rules were correct (errata in Journal 8 "undoes" the earlier errata).

If you get AP4, it has replacement pages that include B7/B8, so you won't need to update those.

query:
A couple of questions: Do you "cower" everytime you roll doubles, even snake eyes, when shooting?

Do you go under DM everytime you fail a MC or get Casualty reduced?
title: A couple of questions
raw_question:
Do you "cower" everytime you roll doubles, even snake eyes, when shooting?

Do you go under DM everytime you fail a MC or get Casualty reduced?
ground_truth_answer:
Do you "cower" everytime you roll doubles, even snake eyes, when shooting?

You cower, even on snake eyes, unless an SMC (like firing a MG), berserk, Fanatic, British elite and first line, Finnish, ordnance, OBA or vehicular.

Do you go under DM everytime you fail a MC or get Casualty reduced?

You go under DM when you break, even voluntarily.

You also go under DM if you are already broken and: 

a) you're attacked by White Phosphorus

b) you're attacked with "enough FP to possibly inflict a NMC on the target" (even if the firing unit cowers). Ordnance must secure a hit to be considered an 'attack'

c) you're in a Location attacked by an effective (1 or 2 result) Sniper

d) a Known enemy unit becomes ADJACENT to you (even if the enemy unit Moves on, even if it is an enemy unit advance)

Casualty Reduction alone does not cause you to go DM. A77.302 (first edition) says "A squad is reduced to a HS with the same broken/non-broken status of the squad it was Reduced from.."

2) Either it fires the HMG alone (hoping to keep ROF) or it chooses to use Subsequent First Fire.
In that latter case, it may opt not to fire the HMG (to avoid sustained fire penalties), but the HMG will still be marked with a Final Fire counter as the squad.

Then if I want to enter the pillbox I need to roll a die and have more MF than the roll to move into the location?

ground_truth_answer:
I'll provide even more detail because wire and PBs are kind of silly, for precisely the interpretations stated above - they are counterintuitive and not the way you assume they should be played. Getting through the wire and INTO the PB is as described above, but getting out is goofed up - to leave the PB, you get placed back ON the wire (I know - it's b*llsh*t to me too). This essentially comes down to B26.4 ('...to enter a Wire Location...') and B30.1 (A pillbox is a separate non-vertical-level Location inside its hex...'). So, when you leave the PB Location, you are entering the Wire Location anew for the purposes of B26.4. Even if you immediately try to reenter the PB, you still have to go through the wire; dumb, stupid, absurd mechanic, but thems the rules. 

It gets worse when you consider the placement of DCs vs the wired PB. The unit placing the DC gets to do so without (i) paying the wire dr or (ii) paying the +1 MF for PB entry). So, to defend your PBs well with wire, you need to have the wire one hex out to catch the DC placers and not impede your PB boys from leaving. Of course, a bunker will let you get out without taking the wire dr (B27.54).

This was discussed over at the Gamesquad forum a while back (Fall 2009?), but the search function seems screwed up since the last 'upgrade' and the Fall 2009 timeframe seems to have disappeared into the archive, which I have no aptitude for searching

-----------
Here are the Perry Sez responses I got Oct 3, 2009 (I don't seem to have sent in anything about paying wire costs for leaving the PB). To  my mind, both responses contradict the rulebook:

Q. (A23.3, B26.4, B26.45, B30.2) May a unit attempt to Place a DC vs a pillbox that is under a Wire counter if the Placing unit is in an adjacent hex or is it prevented from doing so by B26.45, despite not being ‘on’ the Wire counter? If it may, then does it have to make the B26.4 Wire MF dr as part of its A23.3 expenditure?

It does not have to get beneath the wire amd no Wire rolls; B26.51.
-------------
> Q. (A23.3 & B30.4) Does a unit trying to Place a DC against a pillbox have to pay the extra 1 MF for pillbox entry? 

No.
----------
P.S. Ben, please consider editing the subject to 'Wire & Pillbox questions'.
